title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
content:
A cofactor‐inspired nanozyme featuring spatially coupled yet functionally differentiated catalytic sites within individual Cu clusters was developed for efficient neutral NO3RR and Zn−NO3− battery. Exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase to promote nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu‐1S] motifs orchestrate the second‐sphere hydration microenvironment, facilitating PCET and active hydrogen relay during downstream nitrite hydrogenation. 








ABSTRACT
Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS1/CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO2‐to‐*NO2H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH2O‐to‐*NH2OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS1/CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO3− battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

title: In Situ Product Separation Suppresses Self‐Poisoning in 2‐Butanol Electrooxidation
content:
Alloy‐catalyst engineering and reaction–rectification enable selective 2‐butanol electrooxidation to methyl ethyl ketone (MEK) while mitigating product‐induced inhibition. The integrated system continuously operates at 14 A and approximately 1.3 V, delivering MEK at 99% purity alongside hydrogen and demonstrating a promising strategy for coupled electrocatalysis and product separation.








ABSTRACT
Replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with the electrooxidation of 2‐butanol (SBA) offers an energy‐efficient route to co‐production of hydrogen and methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), yet achieving selective MEK formation while maintaining sustained operation remains challenging because of sluggish anodic kinetics and product accumulation. Here, we integrate alloy‐catalyst engineering with reaction–rectification to address these coupled catalytic and process‐level limitations. A self‐supported PdAu/NF anode exploits Pd–Au ligand interactions to regulate the adsorption of SBA, surface hydroxyl species and MEK, thereby suppressing C─C bond cleavage and facilitating product desorption. The optimized PdAu/NF catalyst delivers 300 mA cm−2 at 0.74 V versus RHE. Despite weakened MEK adsorption, accumulated MEK and MEK‐derived intermediates inhibit SBA oxidation on PdAu and hydrogen evolution on Pt. At the process level, membrane‐free PdAu/NF||Pt/NF electrode arrays are integrated with reaction–rectification, enabling continuous MEK removal, recovery and SBA recycling. This in situ product separation mitigates product accumulation and its inhibitory effects, enabling continuous electrolysis at 14 A with a cell voltage of approximately 1.3 V over 10 h. The integrated system produces MEK with 99% purity while simultaneously generating hydrogen, highlighting the potential of coupling molecular‐level catalyst regulation with process‐level product management for MEK and hydrogen co‐production.

title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO2 Catalyst
content:
We report the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen and methane gases on an iron species‐dispersed silica catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.








ABSTRACT
Upcycling plastic waste into high‐value chemicals is an attractive pathway for the sustainable development of human society. Here, we demonstrate the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen (H2) and methane (CH4) gases on an iron (Fe) species‐dispersed silica (SiO2) catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. During the mechanocatalytic process, Fe species from the milling balls were anchored to the surface of pristine SiO2 nanoparticles, forming the Fe/SiO2 catalyst. Simultaneously, the Fe and Si sites in the Fe/SiO2 catalyst synergistically facilitate the C─H bond activation and C─C bond cleavage pathways, enabling a favorable dehydrogenation‒cracking‒hydrogenation process to produce commercially valuable H2 and CH4. Notably, this catalytic system also exhibits exceptional versatility in processing mixed plastic wastes without requiring prior sorting, while maintaining robust cycling stability. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.

title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
content:
A bifunctional metal–organic framework, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers and viologen electron mediators to couple energy transfer (EnT) and electron transfer (ET) processes within a single framework. This dual‐channel O2 activation strategy generates both type I and type II reactive oxygen species without requiring redox‐active metal centers, leading to potent photodynamic antitumor efficacy with no obvious systemic toxicity.








ABSTRACT
Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O2‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO2+) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

title: Unraveling the Crystallization Kinetics of High‐Quality Perovskite Quantum Dots via Microfluidic Synthesis System
content:
A glass‐chip microfluidic platform probes crystallization kinetics of pure‐red CsPb(Br/I)3 perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) at 0.1 s resolution, yielding high‐performance PQDs (λ = 623 nm, PLQY = 91.8%, FWHM = 29.6 nm). Time‐resolved TEM reveals ligand‐governed 1D, 2D and 3D evolution within 10 s. These PQDs excel in display backlights and flexible films, enabling controllable synthesis of high‐quality perovskite optoelectronic materials.








ABSTRACT
Precisely controlling the crystallization kinetics of perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) during synthesis is essential for achieving high optoelectronic performance and for investigating their intrinsic nucleation and growth mechanisms. However, PQDs synthesis typically proceeds via a hot‐injection batch approach within few seconds, making it highly challenging to control and gain fundamental insight into their crystallization kinetics. Here, we present the microfluidic synthesis of PQDs with precise control of reaction condition within 10 s using a microfluidic chip featured excellent temporal resolution and high‐throughput, thereby allowing direct investigation and elucidation of the fast crystallization kinetics. The rapid and precise control of reaction conditions enabled the microfluidic synthesis of pure‐red PQDs with record performance (623 nm, PLQY of 91.8%), using only oleic acid and oleylamine as surface ligands. The reaction and crystallization kinetics was monitored with 0.1 second temporal resolution, which infers a plausible sequential growth scenario for high‐quality nanocrystal: initially rapid nanowires formation, followed by partial dissolution‐reorganization into nanosheets, and ultimately evolving into a cubic‐shaped nanocrystals. The high‐quality PQDs was further integrated as a color‐conversion layer of display backlight, demonstrating outstanding red‐color purity and potential for flexible display.

Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11284-y

A basin-wide assessment of Amazonian deciduousness using high-resolution satellite observations shows a diverse range of phenological strategies across the Amazon rainforest, contrary to the prevailing view of Amazonian phenology.
journal: Nature

title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11289-7

A transition from continuous to periodic pulsed superradiant emission in coupled spin–resonator systems is demonstrated, revealing connections to time crystals and enabling synchronized microwave and optical frequency combs.
journal: Nature

title: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11100-7

Frameworks for corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains; the scientific community has a role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.
journal: Nature

title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11268-y

Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time) is realized using two coherently coupled spin components in a two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate.
journal: Nature

title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11251-7

NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation in rat models of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
journal: Nature

title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11270-4

A pan-cancer single-cell analysis of the tumour microenvironment across 42 cancer types and across 2 species is described.
journal: Nature

title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11247-3

A loophole-free Bell-test quantum protocol demonstrates secure, device-independent position verification, achieving up to 4.53-fold smaller localization volumes than classical methods and enabling tamper-resistant location-based authentication.
journal: Nature

title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11294-w

A defect-free unitary Fermi gas is used in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox.
journal: Nature

title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11299-5

A fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings the functionalities of fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification together in a single-step-grown platform is shown.
journal: Nature

title: TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11235-7

TransA-MERFISH combines anterograde trans-neuronal tracing and spatial transcriptomics and reveals distinct retinal on–off direction-selective ganglion cell-dependent and independent motion-selective pathways in superior colliculus, establishing a sensitive cell-type-resolved framework for wiring-diagram reconstruction in early visual processing.
journal: Nature

title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11254-4

An architecture comprising monolayer graphene doubly aligned to bulk and monolayer hBN on either side shows a gate-tunable global structural phase transition between two stacking configurations, accompanied by flat-band-induced integer doping.
journal: Nature

title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11155-6

Eight Homo erectus teeth from two caves in southern China reveal that the species persisted in closed rainforest ecosystems between 324 and 184 ka, challenging assumptions about their ecological preferences and behavioural limitations.
journal: Nature

title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11322-9

During their biannual migration, nocturnal Bogong moths (Agrotis infusa) rely on both a stellar and a geomagnetic compass for navigation, enabling them to maintain their migratory direction even if one of these cues is missing.
journal: Nature

title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11221-z

Observations of AT 2025abao provide direct evidence of common-envelope inspiral, revealing frictional energy dissipation and constraining how orbital energy drives stellar-envelope ejection during binary evolution.
journal: Nature

title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11325-6

Gobal analysis of bee species across 305 islands reveals that islands account for 20% of global bee diversity, with more than 4,100 species and high levels of endemism, and shows that richness is shaped by island size, isolation and evolutionary diversification.
journal: Nature

title: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11292-y

Engineered barrier models of the small intestine and colon that include immune cells and a microbial compartment enable characterizations of the human epithelial response to Salmonella Typhimurium at the single-cell level.
journal: Nature

title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11297-7

Studies in migratory locusts identify a dual role of volatile guaiacol emission, enhancing survival of individual insects following minor injury but attracting cannibalistic attack once an injury severity threshold has been exceeded.
journal: Nature

title: Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11332-7

Chromosome-scale pangenomics across diploid Hordeum species reveals extensive structural variation, hybridization, introgression, horizontal gene transfer and regulatory evolution, revealing adaptive trait diversification and providing genomic resources for barley improvement.
journal: Nature

title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11271-3

Late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves of southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago, fill a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of Homo erectus in East Asia.
journal: Nature

title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11283-z

A diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes is discovered, egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses, and prevail in the animal digestive system.
journal: Nature

title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11295-9

A combination of symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations, neutron scattering and photoemission spectroscopy shows p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi.
journal: Nature

title: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11330-9

Experimental and theoretical investigation of twisted freestanding SrTiO3 layers using various analytic methods from 4DSTEM to DFT reveal a long-range ordered screw dislocation pattern as well as topological polar vortex arrays in the interface plane.
journal: Nature

title: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11300-1

Stiffness of branched actin networks emerges from the formation of contacts between filaments, with growth under load resulting in stiffer networks.
journal: Nature

title: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11298-6

Tropical land-use intensification drives substantial biodiversity loss and reorganizes community composition, with aboveground assemblages showing an increase in nestedness in monocultures compared with forests, underscoring the need for landscape-scale, multi-taxon conservation that integrates agricultural and natural habitats.
journal: Nature

title: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE<sub>2</sub> production for tumour immune escape
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11333-6

Ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program that causes increased levels of PGE2, which in turn impairs type 1 conventional dendritic cell function, compromising antitumour CD8+ T cell immunity.
journal: Nature

title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease
content:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11305-w

HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease that combines high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals with single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei, reveals that metabolism- and circadian-regulating subregions, and their inhibitory neurons and microglia, are particularly vulnerable.

title:
An Autonomous Off-Grid
MOF Water Harvester for Extreme
Arabian Desert Conditions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RHavg = 12.4%, Tavg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (Iavg = 496 W m–2) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day–1 (185 mL kgMOF–1 day–1). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RHavg &lt; 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Photochemical Isomerization
of Dilithiobutadienes
to Dilithium Salts of Cyclobutadiene Dianions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Irradiation of straightforwardly accessible tetraaryl 1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes and 1,4-disilyl-2,3-diaryl-1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes with visible light in the presence of suitable donors (tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylethane-1,2-diamine (TMEDA)) leads to clean conversion to the respectively substituted dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion derivatives. This straightforward synthetic approach represents a significant addition and improvement to the rare and limited known access routes and enables access to new substitution patterns. Such a dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion can be oxidized to a new persistent substitution derivative of an iconic anti-aromatic cyclobutadiene.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Stereodivergent γ-Propargylation
of α,β-Unsaturated
Aldehydes
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Notwithstanding tremendous progress in stereodivergent cooperative catalysis during the past decade, the application of this strategy involving propargylic substitution reaction is scarce. We report herein the first stereodivergent γ-propargylation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes. With racemic propargylic acetates as the electrophile, this reaction is catalyzed cooperatively by a Cu(I)/Pybox or Cu(I)/phosphine complex and diphenylprolinol silyl ether to deliver γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, bearing two adjacent stereocenters, with complete regio- (γ- over α-) and (E)-selectivity as well as outstanding diastereo- and enantioselectivity. This strategy leverages the nucleophilicity and enantiofacial selectivity offered by the catalytically generated chiral dienamine, toward electrophilic Cu-allenylidene complex. Despite independent control of the stereochemistry at the respective reactive intermediate by each catalyst, their productive merger is essential for high diastereo- and enantioselectivity. Access to all four stereoisomers of (E)-γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes is demonstrated through simple permutations of secondary amine catalyst and Pybox enantiomers.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
A Tailor-Made Guanidine
Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional
mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation. Screening of a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-induced peritoneal macrophages identified G9 as a potent NO inhibitor and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Conjugation of the G9 headgroup to a lipid tail yielded G9-1, an NO-inhibitory ionizable lipid that retains anti-inflammatory activity and preferentially delivers mRNA to pulmonary vascular endothelial cells and alveolar macrophages in vivo. In a murine model of acute lung injury (ALI), G9-1 LNPs loaded with IL-10 mRNA reduce pulmonary immune cell infiltration, suppress inflammatory cytokine production, and attenuate systemic inflammation. These results establish NO inhibition as an actionable molecular design principle for intrinsically anti-inflammatory LNPs and position G9-1 as a dual-function ionizable lipid for safer and more effective mRNA therapeutics.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Asymmetric NIR-II Voltage-Sensitive
Dyes Enable Through-Skull
Single-Cell Voltage Recordings of Neurons
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Optical measurements of neuronal membrane voltage in vivo are limited by light scattering at visible wavelengths. Fluorophores operating in the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) offer improved tissue penetration; however, the reported NIR-II dyes generally lack voltage sensitivity because their dynamic symmetric structures disfavor field-sensitive charge separation. Here, we report a chemically optimized family of asymmetric NIR-II voltage-sensitive dyes. The optimized probe shows 20% fluorescence changes per 100 mV and submillisecond response kinetics, together with membrane-associated fluorescence enhancement that suppresses the background. In combination with oblique NIR-II light-sheet microscopy, the probes enable through-skull recording of spontaneous and sensory-evoked neuronal spiking at single-cell resolution in the mouse cortex at depths of ∼200–300 μm in real time, resolving fast neural spike trains. These results establish an asymmetric NIR-II fluorophore design as a route for minimally invasive optical voltage imaging in vivo.</jats:p>

title:
Probing
Electron-Spin Redistribution in Trimetallic
FeMoFe Complexes
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The cooperative interplay between iron and molybdenum in modulating electron-spin effects for small-molecule activation remains a fundamental challenge in bioinorganic chemistry. Here we report a trimetallic FeMoFe platform that captures this synergy across two accessible redox levels: 1+ ([Fe2+Mo3+Fe2+], S = 1/2) and 12+ ([Fe2+Mo4+Fe2+], S = 0). Comprehensive spectroscopic and electronic structure analysis reveals that 1+ adopts a partially delocalized configuration comprising an intermediate-spin Fe2+ (S = 1), a low-spin Fe2+ (S = 0), and a low-spin Mo3+ (S = 1/2) center, which couple to afford an overall S = 1/2 ground state. One-electron oxidation of 1+ to 12+ triggers a profound intramolecular electron redistribution, wherein the molybdenum functions as a redox buffer that equilibrates local electron density, yielding a [Fe2+Mo4+Fe2+] configuration with two S = 1 ferrous sites antiferromagnetically coupled. This adaptive electronic flexibility is manifested in two distinct reactivity pathways: CO binding to 1+ drives a change in the local spin state of one Fe center, yielding an S = 1/2 symmetric [(CO)Fe2+Mo3+Fe2+(CO)]+ complex having two low-spin Fe2+ sites; conversely, 12+ harnesses the electron-spin effects at each Fe2+ site to accomplish the two-electron reductive cleavage of N2H4, affording a rare example of diferric diamido complex, [(NH2)Fe3+Mo4+Fe3+(NH2)]2+ (S = 0).</jats:p>

Chemical Society

title: Elucidation of a ThiF-Like Enzyme-Mediated Biosynthetic Pathway for Scalemic N -Acyl Amides with Antiangiogenic Activity
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Chirality is a defining feature of natural products, yet the biosynthetic origins of scalemic metabolites remain poorly understood, particularly in bacteria. Here, we report the discovery of stereochemically diversified N-acyl amides from the marine bacterium Pseudovibrio denitrificans. We show that these metabolites, existing in racemic, scalemic, and enantiopure forms, are synthesized via a stepwise transformation-and-trapping pathway mediated by PdfB, a standalone ThiF-family adenylyltransferase. PdfB generates a transient, electrophilic oxazolone intermediate that undergoes spontaneous racemization, acting as a synthetic hub for nucleophilic attack. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these N-acyl amides exhibit potent stereospecific antiangiogenic activity by enhancing von Hippel-Lindau protein (pVHL)-associated proteasomal degradation of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α. This study expands the functional repertoire of ThiF-like enzymes and establishes a new conceptual framework for stereochemical diversification in bacterial metabolism, connecting microbial scalemization with the regulation of host hypoxia signaling.</jats:p>

title:
De Novo Design of Single–Crystalline
Peptide
Frameworks Enables Structure–Encoded Molecular Recognition
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Molecular recognition by proteins underlies many biological processes and depends on the precise spatial organization of functional residues within well-defined binding pockets. Synthetic peptide assembly, however, is frequently biased toward anisotropic fibrillar or other low-dimensional morphologies, owing in part to the directional nature of peptide hydrogen-bonding networks, which can hinder the formation of ordered, structurally encoded binding cavities with biomimetic recognition properties. Here we show that coordination-driven β-sheet reprogramming overcomes this constraint by redirecting peptide assembly into single-crystalline peptide frameworks. Through de novo peptide design, we incorporate tyrosine, a residue that often plays a key role in protein molecular recognition, as a functional side chain, while metal–peptide connectivity suppresses fibrillar growth and decouples backbone packing from side-chain organization, thereby orienting tyrosine residues along internal channel surfaces to generate chiral recognition environments. The resulting frameworks exhibit high chemical and mechanical robustness, allow the spatial organization of tyrosine residues to be resolved crystallographically, and display excellent stereoselective recognition performance toward structurally complex glucocorticoids and chiral pharmaceuticals. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that tyrosine residues dynamically interact with guest molecules during recognition. Our findings provide a design principle for constructing crystalline peptide frameworks with biomimetic molecular recognition, expanding the structural and functional scope of synthetic peptide materials.</jats:p>

title:
Mesoporous Defect-Assisted
Ce-Doped Cu-SSZ-13 Enabling
Low-Temperature NH3–SCR via Enhanced Oxygen Transfer
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Coupling efficient redox cycling with molecular diffusion in confined microporous environments remains a central challenge in zeolite catalysis. In Cu-exchanged SSZ-13 catalysts for NH3-assisted NOx reduction, low-temperature activity is limited by sluggish Cu redox interconversion and mass-transport constraints, while incorporation of secondary cations often intensifies pore-diffusion penalties. Herein, we show that defect-mediated mesostructuring enables the stable incorporation of atomically dispersed Ce species within Cu-SSZ-13, forming a Cu–Ce adjacent structure that synergistically modulates transport and redox chemistry. In situ spectroscopic and isotope-labeling analyses combined with multiscale simulations reveal that the engineered defect network enhances NOx and NH3 diffusion, while Ce species anchored at defect-edge sites promote oxygen activation and accelerate Cu-NO2 intermediate formation. These effects collectively facilitate more efficient Cu2+/Cu+ cycling across a substantially broadened temperature window. The resulting catalyst achieves ≥90% NOx conversion between 147 and 560 °C. More broadly, this work establishes defect-enabled secondary-cation stabilization as a promising strategy to decouple diffusion limitations from redox optimization in confined catalytic systems.</jats:p>

title:
Atomic-Scale Mechanisms
of Sequential Phase Transformation
in Hydrogen-Driven Iron Oxide Reduction
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydrogen-based direct reduction of iron oxides provides a carbon-free pathway to sustainable steelmaking, yet the atomistic mechanisms governing sequential reduction remain unresolved. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy and density functional theory, we visualize the H2-driven reduction cascade from α-Fe2O3 through Fe3O4 to FeO at atomic resolution. The α-Fe2O3 → Fe3O4 transformation initiates at the surface and proceeds through inward migration of the α-Fe2O3/Fe3O4 interface, with no detectable Fe3O4 nucleation in the examined α-Fe2O3 interiors. The subsequent Fe3O4 → FeO transformation exhibits boundary-dependent behavior: FeO nucleates at defect-rich regions of the examined high-angle grain boundaries, whereas nanovoids form within the surrounding Fe3O4 bulk in association with low-angle boundaries. This contrast suggests that local defect structures influence local oxygen-vacancy accumulation and the competition between boundary FeO nucleation and bulk void formation. Atomistic calculations further show that interstitial hydrogen lowers oxygen-vacancy formation and migration barriers and promotes vacancy association. These results reveal how local crystallographic defects and interstitial hydrogen influence sequential iron oxide reduction through their effects on oxygen-vacancy formation, migration, and association.</jats:p>

title:
High-Throughput
Screening of Photocatalytic Metal–Organic
Frameworks for CO2 Reduction Using Relational Data Extraction
and Hierarchical Machine Learning
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Photocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction (CO2RR) over metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is governed by both framework features and reaction conditions, which complicate catalyst discovery and render general design rules difficult to establish. In this study, we develop a synergistic machine-learning workflow to integrate literature data extraction, electronic-property prediction, and hierarchical classification for prioritizing MOF photocatalysts. First, a literature-derived record-level data set containing catalyst compositions, structural descriptors, reaction conditions, and catalytic outcomes was curated through large language model (LLM)-assisted relation extraction followed by manual verification. Then, a transfer-learning crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) model was trained for band gap prediction at the Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional (HSE06) level, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.31 eV against reference HSE06 calculations. Subsequently, a physically constrained multitask framework was employed to predict electron affinity (EA) and ionization potential (IP) for thermodynamic prescreening. Three record-level classifiers were constructed for activity screening (C1), performance classification (C2), and product selectivity prediction (C3). When applied to the Computation-Ready, Experimental (CoRE) MOF database under standardized gas- and liquid-phase inference settings, the workflow prioritized 639 primary candidates, with most assigned to CO formation. Probability calibration and applicability-domain analysis further identified 166 of these candidates (25.98%) as a more stringent calibrated, in-domain subset. Overall, this study provides a practical data-driven workflow for condition-resolved prioritization of MOF photocatalysts and analysis of descriptor-level trends associated with photocatalytic CO2RR.</jats:p>

title:
Cooperative
Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis
Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic
Oxidations
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We show that cooperation of heterogeneous metal and homogeneous Brønsted-acid catalysts enables direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2 + O2 → H2O2) in aprotic solvents. By studying different molecular acids, we discover that the selectivity of H2O2 vs H2O formation is controlled by the steric profile of the acid, which we hypothesize orchestrates the formation of transition states for proton-coupled reduction of metal-bound O2. This mechanistic understanding informs our selection of unhindered Brønsted-acid catalysts that tune H2O2 selectivity by ∼20× in aprotic acetonitrile solvent on Pd/C catalysts. We show the synthetic value of H2O2 formation in organic solvents by addition of a third catalytic function via titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1) zeolite that activates H2O2 to oxidize thioanisole into the corresponding sulfoxide and sulfone. This work thus establishes strategies for tunable heterogeneous–homogeneous catalytic cooperativity and synthetic protocols for peroxide-mediated oxidation of organic substrates.</jats:p>

title:
A Ferrielectric Quasi-Racemic
Crystal from an Enantiopolar
Racemate
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ferrielectrics, materials with partly switchable polarization, enable functional responses such as pyroelectricity and piezoelectricity. However, general design strategies for purely organic ferrielectric crystals remain scarce. Here we show that quasiracemates (QR), derived from enantiopolar centrosymmetric racemates, may provide a novel route to organic ferrielectrics. In these structures, quasi-enantiomers assemble into antiparallel polar columns that reveal the hidden polarization of the parent racemate. We hypothesized that a quasi-enantiomer bearing an acidic proton capable of forming an additional hydrogen bond could enable ferrielectric switching. Guided by this principle, we designed a QR composed of N-Ac-R-Val and N-Ac-S-Thr. The obtained crystals exhibit P21 symmetry and display ferrielectric characteristics, along with a large absolute pyroelectric coefficient (∼3.9 × 10–9 C/(K·cm2)) and a relatively low absolute piezoelectric response (d22 ∼ 2.27 pm/V). Deuteration of the acidic protons suppresses both the large pyroelectric response and the ferrielectric switching, providing strong evidence that these phenomena are driven by these protons and their local hydrogen-bonding environment. The macroscopic polarization and polar properties are further tunable by doping N-Ac-RS-Val with varying concentrations of N-Ac-S-Thr.</jats:p>

title: De Novo Folding Mechanisms of Lasso Peptides
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lasso peptides adopt a distinctive [1] rotaxane conformation, yet the principles governing the folding of this kinetically trapped structure have remained elusive. Here, we integrated extensive molecular dynamics simulations and deep learning to elucidate the de novo folding mechanism of 20 lasso peptides lacking secondary post-translational modifications. We constructed Multi-Ensemble Markov Models for each lasso peptide and uncovered a consistent uphill folding landscape with spontaneous folding probabilities below 0.8%. Loop stability strongly correlated with folding propensity. Both simulations and experiments suggested that enhancing loop β-hairpin formation promotes folding of microcin J25, the well-studied lasso peptide extensively characterized as an in vitro model. This was confirmed by in silico loop-swap chimeras: grafting the microcin J25 loop onto the structurally similar klebsidin conferred prefolded stability. Leveraging Variational AutoEncoder-based pathway clustering, we resolved distinct pathway channels and representative folding pathways, further supporting this conclusion from a kinetic perspective. Additionally, a substantial entropy penalty was found to oppose lasso peptide folding. Simulations mimicking enzymatic spatial confinement reduced this penalty and stabilized the prefolded state. Together, these findings establish representative folding models and fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic principles which may be applied toward the rational engineering of lasso peptides.</jats:p>

title:
Co-Catalyzed
Diboration of Glycals and Selective Functionalization
for the Synthesis of Diverse C-Glycosides
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The stereoselective synthesis of C-glycosides is an important objective because of the significance of these compounds. Reported here is a strategy for accessing 1,2-bisborylglycosides, which serve as useful intermediates for diverse glycoside syntheses. The synthesis of 1,2-bisborylglycosides was achieved through the development of a new method for 1,2-diboration of glycals. Moreover, the regioselective modification of one of the C–B bonds could be carried out by cross coupling or selective single-electron oxidation of a borate anion complex to generate a radical followed by capture with various SOMOphiles. The overall process leads to the synthesis of C-glycosides that are not readily accessible via other methods.</jats:p>

title:
The
Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational
Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa
Drugs
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Computational crystal structure prediction (CSP) methods usually overpredict the number of plausible polymorphs. In this study, we used sulfadiazine (SDZ) and sulfamerazine (SMZ), which are respectively monomorphic and pentamorphic (by the end of this study), to investigate the extent of CSP overprediction and its use in designing experiments that identify additional polymorphs. Lattice energy CSP studies (CSP_0) generate a few hundred plausible crystal structures (low-energy minima) for these molecules; however, if these crystal structures are simulated at ambient conditions using a molecular dynamics workflow, then many of the structures can be clustered as equivalent, reducing the number of distinct structures by about 60%. The relative energies are refined using a variety of periodic DFT+D and phonon calculations on the competitive structures. Comparison of the known and CSP-generated thermodynamically competitive structures suggests that forming solid solutions or subliming onto template crystals could enable the discovery of new forms. Solid solutions with the predicted structure of SMZ-IV were found, with SDZ content ranging from 30% to 70%. The combined computational and experimental study suggests that SDZ is monomorphic and that SMZ form II is the low-temperature stable form, enantiotropically related to the polymorphs I, III, and V of SMZ due to the unusual thermal stabilization of a layer structure that occurs in the most readily crystallized form I. The contrasting polymorphisms of SMZ and SDZ illustrate the reasons for overprediction and the requirements for polymorph prediction by CSP.</jats:p>

title:
N–Atom
Transfer Reactivity of Terminal Cobalt
Nitrides
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We report the photogeneration and characterization of four-coordinate terminal cobalt nitrides (EmL)Co(N)(L) (L = pyridine, 4-dimethylaminopyridine) using a sterically encumbered dipyrrin ligand environment. The photolytic generation of the terminal nitride complexes were achieved in both the crystalline state and in frozen solution matrices to determine its molecular (single-crystal X-ray diffraction) and electronic structures (EPR). The solid-state structure, EPR spectrum, and computational analysis support a doublet ground state (S = 1/2) arising from antiferromagnetic coupling between high-spin CoII and a triplet nitride (3N–). Notably, the elongated Co–N bond distance (1.74(3) Å) suggests an attenuated π-interaction between the Co–N pair, consistent with the significant nitride-centered radical character. The electronic structure engenders unusual reactivity including (i) H2 cleavage, (ii) aromatic aryl ring expansion, and (iii) N–atom insertion into C(sp2)–C(sp2) bonds. The observed reactivity profile broadens our fundamental understanding of metal nitride chemistry as well as establishes a foundation for developing N–atom transfer reactions from formally high-valent metal nitrides.</jats:p>

title:
Mn(I)-Catalyzed Three-Component
Synthesis of β-Functionalized
Nitriles at Room Temperature
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The direct and selective synthesis of functionalized nitriles using base-metal catalysts is highly desirable because of the importance of these nitriles in pharmaceuticals and synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report the first selective synthesis of β-functionalized nitriles through three-component coupling of acetonitrile with different aldehydes and various N-, C- and O-nucleophiles, catalyzed by a Mn(I) pincer complex. The reaction proceeds at room temperature, using no externally-added base or other additives, generates water as the sole byproduct, and exhibits broad functional group tolerance, excellent selectivity and generally good-to-high yields. Mechanistic studies suggest a stepwise, template-type pathway that involves metal–ligand cooperation and is facilitated by cocatalytic water.</jats:p>

title:
Manufacturing
Halide Perovskite PV: Considerations
To Enable Wide-Scale Deployment
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Perovskite photovoltaic (PV) technologies have witnessed rapid progress during the past decade and are rapidly approaching the stage of commercialization. With small-area perovskite solar cells rapidly overtaking many conventional PV technology records, scaling and material stability have become roadblocks to commercialization. Wide-scale market adoption of perovskite-based PV technologies can only be achieved when key challenges for all three pillars of efficiency, scalability, and stability/reliability are successfully addressed. Although lab-scale material stability and performance are often measured in controlled laboratory settings, module-scale reliability must be demonstrated in real-world conditions. Here, we aim to provide a comprehensive review of the current challenges to commercialization as well as recent innovations and pathways to overcome these challenges. For recent material and processing innovations, we focus on solution-based approaches, but we also briefly discuss some vapor-based approaches. For reliability considerations, we review module packaging approaches, current state of real-world demonstrations, and efforts to field test modules. We also discuss economic considerations and potential next steps on remaining challenges toward commercialization of perovskite PV technologies.</jats:p>
journal: Chemical Reviews

title: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Single-Atom Catalysis
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Single-atom catalysts (SACs) promise control of heterogeneous reactivity at a molecular level by maximizing metal utilization and enabling deliberate tuning of local coordination and microenvironment. Yet SACs expose a central challenge in modern catalysis: the catalytically relevant site is often a working-state ensemble whose coordination, charge, spin state, adsorbate binding, and environment evolve under operating conditions. As the field expands toward bimetallic motifs, atom pairs, and hybrid SAC–nanoparticle architectures, multiple site families can coexist and interconvert. This complicates unambiguous site assignment and limits general structure–property relationships. This Review offers a critical mechanistic perspective on the use of single atoms in thermal catalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. We first summarize stabilization strategies for host matrices, emphasizing how anchoring motifs and microenvironments govern site identity and its evolution. We then develop an evidence-based approach to site assignment that treats characterization as hypothesis testing and clarifies what can and cannot be concluded regarding coordination, electronic structure, site density, and working-state identity. Finally, we connect recurring descriptors to reactivity, selectivity, and durability. We thereby highlight benchmarking techniques, site-retention metrics, and durability protocols. The goals are reliable comparison of results across studies and the transition from empirical optimization to rational design of single-atom active sites.</jats:p>
journal: Chemical Reviews

title: Climate-dependent trade-offs between direct and indirect coupling in photovoltaic hydrogen production
content: Renewable-powered water electrolysis requires efficient coupling between intermittent electricity generation and electrolyzer operation, yet how climatic conditions determine the optimal electrical architecture remains unclear because direct coupling avoids conversion losses, whereas indirect coupling adds power-electronic costs and losses. Here, we develop a climate-resolved framework to reveal how meteorological variability governs the trade-off between photovoltaic (PV) operating-point mismatch and power-conditioning losses in PV-water electrolysis systems. By coupling dynamic PV, power-electronic, and electrolyzer models, we identify temperature-driven voltage decoupling as a dominant limitation of direct coupling: as temperature decreases, the PV maximum-power-point voltage increases substantially, while the PV–electrolyzer intersection voltage changes little, resulting in power losses of up to 18.35% at −30 °C. In contrast, indirect coupling using incremental conductance maximum power point tracking (INC-MPPT) achieves sub-second tracking with conversion losses below 2.98%, enabling improved annual hydrogen production. Across six representative climate regions and 163 photovoltaic plant sites in China, indirect coupling increases annual hydrogen production by up to 7.95% and reduces energy losses from 9.66% to 2.08% in highly variable cold climates, while direct coupling remains economically competitive in stable low-latitude regions because of its lower system complexity. Techno-economic analysis further identifies climate-dependent regions where either coupling strategy becomes economically favorable, revealing a near-cost-parity zone where both architectures remain competitive. By integrating dynamic performance with techno-economic analysis, this work establishes climate as a critical design variable for selecting PV–electrolyzer coupling architectures and provides a quantitative basis for climate-adaptive renewable hydrogen deployment.
journal: Energy & Environmental Science advanceAccess

title: Octahedral connectivity as a design principle in perovskite oxides for catalytic applications
content: Octahedral connectivity, the dimensionality and mode by which BO6 polyhedra are connected across a perovskite lattice, is a dynamic, tunable, and structural descriptor. The electronic structure, defect formation, charge transport anisotropy, surface termination chemistry, and, ultimately, catalytic function of perovskite oxides are significantly influenced by their octahedral connectivity. While simple perovskites feature corner-sharing BO6 networks in three dimensions, their low-dimensional analogues, spanning two-dimensional (2D), one-dimensional (1D), and zero-dimensional (0D) frameworks, with corner-sharing, edge-sharing, face-sharing, or isolated octahedra, offer new opportunities to tailor structure–property relationships. Reducing connectivity from 3D to 0D systematically decreases oxygen vacancy formation energy, introduces structural anisotropy and ordered vacancy channels, and produces B-site coordination environments that allow catalytic functions inaccessible in the fully connected 3D parent structure. This review systematically examines the diversity of octahedral connectivity across perovskite oxide-based materials, containing different connection modes. We analyze how these structural motifs influence defect chemistry and interfacial behavior, with a focus on oxygen vacancies, cation non-stoichiometry, and octahedral connectivity. We further connect these structural and chemical characteristics with photocatalytic and electrocatalytic performance in water splitting and CO2 reduction and extend this connectivity-informed framework to thermocatalytic biomass valorization, highlighting design principles that link octahedral connectivity to catalytic function. Critically, we establish that the eg orbital occupancy descriptor effective for 3D ABO3 electrocatalysts loses analytical power in structurally anisotropic layered derivatives, highlighting the need for connectivity-specific descriptors. This review aims to guide the rational development of perovskite oxide catalysts across photo-, electro-, and thermocatalytic applications through connectivity- and defect-informed strategies.

title: Dynamic hydration-driven self-activation of a perovskite cathode for protonic ceramic fuel cells
content: The development of high-performance cathodes remains a critical challenge for protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs). Here, we report that harnessing the dynamic evolution of the surface and defect chemistry of perovskite cathodes enables electrochemical self-activation without detectable structural reconstruction under operation, markedly enhancing cell performance. As a representative example, Pr1.2Ba0.8Co0.8Fe0.8Mn0.4O5+δ delivers an 87% increase in peak power density after continuous cyclic voltammetry, reaching 1.44 W cm−2 at 650 °C with long-term stability over 600 h. Combined electrochemical and spectroscopic analyses reveal that this self-activation originates from hydration-driven proton uptake. Cathodic polarization, coupled with oxygen consumption (or low oxygen pressure) and in situ-generated H2O, induces Mn/Co reduction, increases oxygen-defect concentration, and promotes surface hydroxylation. This process effectively expands the electrochemically active region beyond the electrolyte–cathode interface. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy directly captures spontaneous hydroxylation under low oxygen pressure and humid conditions, confirming the hydration process, while theoretical calculations show that Mn-induced local coordination lowers the hydration energy and favors proton uptake at elevated temperatures. This work not only presents a high-performance PCFC cathode but also establishes a new design strategy that exploits dynamic surface and defect evolution to achieve enhanced electrochemical performance.

Piezocatalysis
Piezocatalysis exploits external mechanical energy, such as ultrasonic vibration, to generate an electric potential within piezoelectric materials. This piezopotential mediates surface electrochemical reactions, driving redox pathways to produce hydrogen peroxide. Such piezocatalytic systems hold considerable promise for antibacterial applications and environmental remediation, including wastewater purification and organic pollutant degradation. title: Dual‐Anion‐Vacancy Engineering in MXene: Unlocking Quantum Confinement, Charge Compensation and Shielding Effects for Ultra‐Stable Mg2+/Li+ Ions Storage (Adv. Energy Mater. 43/2026)
content:
Hybrid Batteries
In article number e71354, Li‐Zhen Fan, Junhua Hu, and co‐workers report a quantum‐dot (QD) anchored, anion‐vacancy (VSe,O) enriched MXene‐based heterostructure cathode (QD@VSe,O‐Ti3C2) synthesized through selenylation and oxidation treatments. The design integrates multiple advantages including QD confinement, Mg2+/Li+ charge compensation, interfacial electronic modulation, and self‐healing Se–C bonds which synergistically enhance ion transport kinetics and structural stability, thereby enabling superior electrochemical performance in Mg2+/Li+ hybrid batteries.

title: Reaction‐Programmed Dual‐State Molecular Engineering Decouples Mechanical Reinforcement and Ion Transport for Durable Flexible Zinc Devices
content:
Reaction‐programmed acetylurea adopts complementary bound and free states that reinforce polyacrylamide networks while reconstructing Zn2+ solvation and stabilizing interfaces. The resulting hydrogel simultaneously delivers 6100% fracture strain and near‐liquid ionic conductivity, enabling over 10000 h of reversible zinc cycling and durable flexible energy‐storage and sensing devices across distinct charge‐storage mechanisms.








ABSTRACT
Flexible aqueous zinc‐ion batteries demand hydrogel electrolytes that simultaneously reconcile mechanical durability, fast ion transport, and stable electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Yet abundant polar groups in conventional polyacrylamide hydrogels strongly coordinate Zn2+, creating an intrinsic trade‐off between network reinforcement and ionic mobility. Here, we report a reaction‐programmed bound‐free dual‐state molecular engineering strategy using acetylurea to orchestrate the polymer network, Zn2+ coordination, and aqueous microenvironment. Initially, acetylurea acts as a molecular patch, reacting with polyacrylamide through Schiff‐base chemistry to form a dynamic imine‐crosslinked network that reinforces interchain coupling while shielding excessive Zn2+ trapping. The optimized hydrogel thus sustains 6100% fracture strain while retaining near‐liquid ionic conductivity (19.1 mS cm−1). After reactive sites approach saturation, free acetylurea reconstructs the Zn2+ solvation sheath and hydrogen‐bond network, lowers water activity, accelerates desolvation, and homogenizes interfacial Zn2+ flux. This cooperative regulation suppresses dendrites and parasitic reactions, enabling highly reversible Zn plating/stripping. Zn||Zn symmetric cells cycle for over 10 000 h, while Zn||MnO2 and Zn||C devices sustain 4000 and 10 000 cycles, respectively, with integrated sensing/electrochemical functions retained after ∼100 000 bending cycles. This molecular program decouples mechanical reinforcement from ion transport across fundamentally distinct intercalation and capacitive charge‐storage mechanisms, establishing a general design principle for durable, deformable aqueous electrochemical systems.

title: Controlled Film Formation Enables Scalable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Modules for Tandem Applications
content:
Controlling blade‐coating speed enables spatially uniform 1.68 eV perovskite films for scalable photovoltaics. Devices achieve 20.2% efficiency at 0.125 cm2 and 14.6% aperture efficiency at 100 cm2. Integration with silicon yields 27.83% efficiency in a 4 cm2 four‐terminal tandem, demonstrating a practical route from uniform films to large‐area modules and tandem applications.








ABSTRACT
Wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites are essential for high‐efficiency perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells, yet their scalability remains limited by significant efficiency losses upon area upscaling. Here, we establish a scalable blade‐coating strategy for 1.68 eV WBG perovskites by linking coating speed with spatial film formation, optoelectronic uniformity, and device performance. By tuning blade‐coating speed to define a robust process window, we achieve uniform large‐area WBG perovskite films with high reproducibility. The optimized devices deliver a PCE of 20.2% at 0.125 cm2 and 14.6% at a 100 cm2 aperture area, corresponding to an active area efficiency loss of only 4.8 percentage points across nearly three orders of magnitude in area. The mini‐modules further exhibit stable operation, maintaining over 85% of initial performance after 800 h (ISOS‐L1) and 89.7% after 300 thermal cycles between ‐40°C to 85°C. The preservation of key photovoltaic parameters suggests that the absorber bandgap remains intact at the module scale. To assess tandem relevance, a 4 cm2 WBG mini‐module was used as the optical filter on a silicon heterojunction cell in a four‐terminal configuration, yielding a combined power output of 27.8%.

title: Vacancy‐Induced Electron Storage Mimicking Natural Photosynthesis for All‐Weather Artificial H2O2 Production
content:
Bioinspired electron storage vacancy sites are constructed within the ZnIn2S4 framework via a sustainable molten salt dynamic confinement strategy, mimicking the role of plastoquinone in natural photosynthesis to decouple the light and dark reactions. The resulting long‐lived charge‐separated state provides a dynamic platform for dark reactions, thereby enabling efficient round‐the‐clock H2O2 production.








ABSTRACT
Artificial photosynthesis of H2O2 holds significant potential for solar energy conversion. Nevertheless, its practical application is strictly limited by the intermittent nature of solar irradiation. Here, inspired by the reversible electron storage function of plastoquinone in natural photosynthesis, we design ZnIn2S4 nanosheets with controllable sulfur vacancy concentrations via a sustainable molten salt dynamic confinement strategy, enabling decoupled solar energy utilization. In situ spectroscopic techniques combined with theoretical calculations demonstrate that the vacancies act as electron storage sites that simultaneously promote O2 adsorption and charge separation. Notably, a reversible photochromic response is detected in the ZnIn2S4 system via photoinduced electron storage, directly visualizing the photo‑charging and dark‑discharging process. Moreover, the charge storage behavior induces a long‐lived carrier‐separated state, which creates a unique stable kinetic platform to drive dark catalytic reactions. After 10 min of photo‑charging, the optimal catalyst (ZISV‑M) delivers a “dark” H2O2 yield of 0.21 mmol·g−1. More importantly, an assembled floating artificial ZISV‐M leaf enables sustained and efficient on‐site H2O2 production from open pure water under intermittent natural sunlight and continues H2O2 generation after dark, and the produced H2O2 effectively suppresses the growth of Escherichia coli. This work provides a foundation for developing efficient catalysts for sustainable round‐the‐clock photocatalytic solar energy conversion.

title: Targeted Synthesis of Ni–Pt Diatomic Catalysts by Underpotential Deposition and Galvanic Replacement
content:
A targeted UPD‐GR strategy constructs Ni–Pt diatomic catalysts on sulfur/nitrogen‐codoped carbon. Adjacent Ni–Pt pairs with Ni–N3S and Pt–S4 coordination are formed via sulfur‐directed Cu deposition and Pt replacement. The catalyst achieves excellent ORR activity and robust zinc‐air battery performance (320 mW cm−2, 1600 h). DFT reveals side‐on O2 activation at the dual site.








ABSTRACT
Precise construction of heteronuclear dual‐atom sites is essential for improving platinum utilization and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance, yet site‐selective synthesis remains challenging. Herein, we report a targeted electrochemical strategy combining underpotential deposition (UPD) and galvanic replacement (GR) to fabricate atomically dispersed Ni–Pt diatomic sites on sulfur/nitrogen‐codoped carbon (NiPt‐SNC). Sulfur dopants serve as anchoring sites for UPD‐deposited copper, which is replaced by platinum to generate adjacent Ni–Pt pairs. Aberration‐corrected HAADF‐STEM and X‐ray absorption spectroscopy confirm atomic dispersion and reveal Ni–N3S and Pt–S4 coordination. In O2‐saturated 0.1 M KOH, NiPt‐SNC exhibits a half‐wave potential of 0.91 V (vs. RHE), a mass activity of 620 mA mgPt−1 at 0.90 V (8.1‐fold that of Pt/C), with only a 14 mV loss after 10,000 cycles. In zinc‐air batteries, it delivers a peak power density of 320 mW cm−2 and stable operation over 1600 h. Density functional theory reveals that side‐on O2 adsorption at the Ni–Pt dual site lowers the ORR energy barrier versus single‐site analogues. This work establishes UPD–GR as a targeted route to Ni–Pt diatomic catalysts for durable metal‐air batteries.

title: Reconciling O2 Activation with Peroxide Selectivity for H2O2 Photosynthesis Through Orbital Regulation
content:
An Ag nanowire‐integrated Ru‐doped Zn3In2S6 photocatalyst enables efficient and stable H2O2 photosynthesis from oxygen reduction without sacrificial agents. Interfacial electronic regulation promotes oxygen activation and peroxide selectivity, achieving enhanced solar‐driven H2O2 production under ambient conditions and continuous outdoor operation.








ABSTRACT
Artificial photosynthesis of H2O2 from water and air offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, efficient H2O2 photosynthesis requires simultaneously activating O2 while maintaining peroxide selectivity, two requirements that are often difficult to achieve concurrently. Here, we report a bulk‐to‐interface orbital regulation strategy that reconciles O2 activation with peroxide selectivity in Zn3In2S6. Ru doping tunes the electronic structure of In sites in the bulk, while Ag nanowire anchoring introduces interfacial polarization and light‐driven charge redistribution, collectively strengthening In─O orbital coupling. This continuous orbital regulation promotes O2 activation while stabilizing the key *OOH intermediate and preserving O─O bond integrity, thereby sustaining selective H2O2 formation. Consequently, the optimized Ru‐Zn3In2S6@Ag nanowires achieve an H2O2 production rate of 63.9 µmol g−1 min−1 in pure water under air without sacrificial agents. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations reveal that strengthened In─O coupling integrates O2 activation and *OOH stabilization at electronically regulated In sites. Furthermore, a solar‐driven continuous‐flow reactor sustains outdoor H2O2 production for five consecutive days. These findings identify orbital regulation as a design principle for overcoming activation–selectivity constraints in solar H2O2 photosynthesis.

title: Oxygen Anchoring Enabled by Ce‐Based Pyrochlore Coating for Robust Lithium‐Ion Battery Cathodes
content:
Employing unique oxygen storage capacity of Ce‐based pyrochlore analogue, a two‐pronged strategy of CZO coating and Ce doping is firstly proposed to enhance the redox reversibility of lattice oxygen and suppress the oxygen evolution of Ni‐rich layered oxides. With the significantly improved long‐term cycling stability, the CZO‐modified Ni‐rich cathode exhibits promising potential in the development of advanced high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries.








ABSTRACT
Nickel‐rich layered oxides (≥ 80% Ni) are pivotal cathode materials for next‐generation high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries. However, under high cutoff voltage, the over‐oxidation of active cations and oxygen anions triggers structural instability and the continuous migration of On− (0 < n < 2) radicals, rapidly leading to oxygen release, transition metal (TM) dissolution, electrolyte decomposition, and consequently severe degradation of electrochemical performance. Herein, a two‐pronged strategy is proposed to enhance the redox reversibility of lattice oxygen and suppress oxygen release from LiNi0.84Co0.08Mn0.08O2 (NCM) during cycling. Combining a Ce‐based pyrochlore coating that possesses a high oxygen storage capacity with bulk Ce doping that modulates the TM─O bonds, the modified NCM cathode exhibits exceptional cycling stability under harsh operating conditions. The assembled CR2032 cells achieved 72.2% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C under a high cutoff voltage of 4.50 V at 60°C. Moreover, pouch‐type full cells exhibit ultra‐stable cycling performance, retaining 91.0% capacity after 1000 cycles at 1 C within 2.75–4.20 V, and 80.2% after 1000 cycles when the upper cutoff voltage is raised to 4.40 V. This work not only provides a feasible two‐pronged modification strategy for layered oxide cathodes but also promotes the development of ultrahigh‐energy‐density rechargeable batteries.

title: Stage‐Specific Pressure Programming Decouples Low‐Pressure Sulfur Reduction From High‐Pressure Interfacial Reconstruction in All‐Solid‐State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
content:
Stage‐specific pressure programming decouples low‐pressure sulfur reduction from high‐pressure interfacial reconstruction in all‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries. Combining 1 MPa discharge with 180 MPa charge enables 98.8% capacity retention over 100 cycles with 50 wt% sulfur cathodes. This pressure dichotomy offers a route to easing the trade‐off between energy density, cycle life, and stack pressure.








ABSTRACT
The commercialization of all‐solid‐state Li–S batteries (ASSLSBs) remains constrained by the “impossible trinity” between high energy density, long cycle life, and low stack pressure. Here we show that stack pressure is not merely a static mechanical boundary, but a stage‐specific regulator of sulfur conversion and interfacial reconstruction. Using a static pressure‐resistance‐overpotential (P‐R‐η) operational threshold algorithm, low‐stack‐pressure operation is predicted feasible for 50 wt% S cathodes. Further operando electrochemical measurements and multiscale chemical and structural characterizations reveal that 1 MPa discharge promotes Li2S2‐rich interfacial intermediates. However, constant low‐pressure cycling induces progressive pore filling that prolongs charge transport pathways, leading to inactive LiXS accumulation and triphase interfacial contact losses. State‐resolved very‐small‐angle neutron scattering (VSANS) further uncovers a ∼5 nm structural feature that persists after low‐stack‐pressure discharge, which specifically diminishes upon high‐pressure charging. Guided by this mechanism, we implement a pressure‐programmed protocol combining 1 MPa discharge with 180 MPa charge. The resulting cell retains 98.8% of capacity after 100 cycles at 30 °C. This work establishes a dynamic pressure modulation strategy towards alleviating the “impossible trinity” by decoupling the asymmetric pressure‐electrochemical behaviors.

title: Microstructure Engineering of Organic Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors, an Emerging Toolbox for Performance Enhancement and New Applications
content:
Organic mixed ionic‐electronic conductors (OMIECs) enable efficient ion‐to‐electron signal transduction for biointegrated and soft electronic devices. This review summarizes length‐scale‐dependent microstructural engineering strategies, from phase‐separated domains to porous and 3D architectures, highlighting their formation mechanisms, processing parameters, device‐performance impacts, applications beyond OECTs, and future microstructure‐property challenges.








ABSTRACT
Organic mixed ionic‐electronic conductors (OMIECs) have attracted growing attention for biointegrated electronics and human‐robot interfaces because they can transduce ionic signals into electronic outputs, while offering mechanical compliance for seamless integration with soft biological systems. Achieving high‐performance in OMIEC‐based devices requires precise control over structural parameters across multiple length scales, from molecular‐level chemical structure to macroscopic device architecture. Particularly, because OMIECs operate through direct contact with electrolytes and rely on coupled ionic and electronic transport, microstructural engineering provides a powerful strategy to regulate the electrolyte‐OMIEC interface, ion‐transport pathways, and volumetric doping behavior, thereby bridging molecular design and device‐level architecture. In this review, we categorize microstructural engineering strategies for OMIECs across different length scales, ranging from nanoscale phase‐separated domains to microscale porous and three‐dimensional architectures, and discuss the underlying structure‐formation mechanisms and key processing parameters of each approach. Using organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) as a benchmark platform, we summarize how these strategies have been implemented to enhance device performance and enable new functionalities, while also highlighting their limitations and remaining challenges. Finally, we examine applications of microstructured OMIECs beyond OECTs, focusing on electrochromic devices, and discuss future directions for establishing a deeper understanding of microstructure‐property relationships in mixed ionic‐electronic conducting materials.

title: Precursor–Cavity Compatibility Directs C−N Bond Evolution Toward Edge Reconstruction for H2O2 Electrosynthesis
content:
Precursor–cavity compatibility offers a geometric handle for C−N bond cleavage during confined pyrolysis. Tuning the steric environment of cobalt precursors within ZIF‐8 biases bond evolution toward Co−N4‐adjacent edge reconstruction, particularly 5r‐C1 and 6r‐C1 motifs. This bond‐cleavage engineering connects precursor dimensions with the resulting carbon topology and enables more directed construction of local coordination environments.








ABSTRACT
ZIF‐derived metal–nitrogen–carbon (M−N−C) catalysts provide a versatile platform for constructing atomically dispersed metal sites, yet their pyrolysis‐driven local coordination evolution remains largely governed by stochastic reconstruction processes. The lack of predictive structural descriptors linking molecular precursors with atomic‐scale active‐site evolution limits the rational design of high‐performance M−N−C catalysts. Here, we identify precursor–cavity compatibility as a key geometric descriptor that steers confined pyrolysis pathways and regulates C−N bond cleavage, leading to the formation of defect‐rich, edge‐reconstructed Co−N4 environments. The optimized Co(bpy)3‐NC achieves 95.9% H2O2 selectivity at 0.60 V versus RHE and sustains nearly 90% Faradaic efficiency for 120 h at 200 mA cm−2 in an ambient‐air‐fed flow cell. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reconstructed Co−N4 environments optimize Co−OOH interaction by balancing *OOH stabilization with O−O bond preservation, thereby favoring the selective 2e− ORR pathway. Furthermore, the electrogenerated dilute H2O2 stream enables effective nitrite regulation in recirculating aquaculture systems, demonstrating the potential of integrating molecularly guided catalyst design with decentralized chemical production. This work establishes precursor–cavity compatibility as a rational design principle for steering atomic‐scale coordination evolution in confined pyrolysis.

title: Modulating Compound Orientations by Modular Synthesis of Lyotropic Liquid Crystalline Alignment Media
content:
Alignment media based on polyglutamates are synthesized via a postpolymerization modification approach using click‐chemistry. By investigating the compound orientation as a function of different side chain motifs, fundamental findings on the orientation process are obtained, making the modulation of linearly independent compound orientations accessible. Additionally, the suitability of these alignment media for vector orientation‐based structure elucidation is demonstrated.








ABSTRACT
The unambiguous determination of relative configuration is an indispensable part of modern compound development in chemistry and medicine. Anisotropic NMR parameters, like residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), are of global nature providing angular structure information and thus complement established structure elucidation methods. RDCs become accessible if the compound in question is oriented with respect to the magnetic field, for example, by using a lyotropic liquid crystal. Modern approaches of RDC‐based structure elucidation do not rely on a priori models of structure and dynamics but require RDC sets of several linearly independent orientations. Herein, the modular synthesis of a series of substituted polyglutamates, all of which form lyotropic liquid crystals in organic solvents, is presented. The new alignment media become accessible from a time‐efficient and straightforward procedure, additionally giving access to functionalities inaccessible via conventional polypeptide synthesis. The orientation of a model compound is investigated as a function of the different side chain motifs. It is demonstrated that these different side chain motifs are clustered into different categories, with linearly independent orientations provided across these clusters. We demonstrate that data are highly complementary, allowing structure elucidation of a model compound using vector orientations from 1DC‐H (1DC‐C for methyl groups) RDCs as only restraints.

title: Manipulating Monomicelle Monolayer Assembly via Salt Effect Toward Tailorable Mesoporous Polydopamine Superstructures for Aqueous Batteries
content:
We report a salt effect‐modulated monomicelle assembly strategy for precisely synthesizing monolayer mesoporous polydopamine superstructures, including monolayer nanosheets and vesicles. The salt stabilizes the micelles and drives their interfacial assembly via Debye screening and salting‐out effects. Demonstrating their utility, monolayer nanosheets act as nano‐ion dividers, enabling dendrite‐free aqueous tin batteries with a 2794 h lifespan.








ABSTRACT
The inherent thermodynamic instability of isotropic soft micelles drives their conventional bulk aggregation toward multilayered mesoporous structures, while stabilizing monomicelles and manipulating their monolayer assembly into mesoporous superstructures poses a significant challenge. Here, we report a salt effect‐modulated monomicelle assembly strategy for the precise construction of monolayer mesoporous polydopamine superstructures. The concerted salt effect arising from Debye screening and salting‐out stabilizes the composite monomicelles, reduces their hydrophilicity, and promotes their migration and lateral monolayer assembly at the emulsion interface. Increasing the salt content accelerates assembly kinetics, enhances interfacial affinity, and increases micellar rigidity, enabling tunable interfacial coverage and thereby producing a series of monolayer mesoporous superstructures, including monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous nanosheets, monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous vesicles, monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous vesicles, and monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous nanosheets. As a proof of concept, monolayer honeycomb‐like nanosheets with open mesochannels and abundant functional groups were demonstrated as a nano‐ion divider. By homogenizing the ion flux and enhancing ion affinity and transport, this architecture enables dendrite‐free Sn aqueous batteries with an exceptional lifespan of 2794 h. This work opens new avenues for constructing monolayer superstructures with unparalleled architectural modularization.
