title: Acoustic‐Electromagnetic Information Sensing and Security Protection via Intelligent Transparency Metasurfaces
content:
An optically transparent intelligent metasurface enables programmable control of acoustic information encoded in electromagnetic echoes. By modulating echo amplitude and phase, the metasurface suppresses or alters reconstructed speech and generates speech in the absence of acoustic excitation. These capabilities reveal physical‐layer vulnerabilities in cross‐domain sensing and offer a reconfigurable approach to acoustic privacy protection.








ABSTRACT
Acoustic‐electromagnetic (EM) cross‐domain sensing converts information carried by sound‐induced mechanical vibrations into remotely measurable EM signals, supporting applications in human–computer interaction, environmental sensing, and the Internet of Things. However, the ability to reconstruct acoustic information from weak phase signatures in EM echoes also creates a risk of acoustic information leakage. Existing shielding and encryption schemes are difficult to combine with covert integration and real‐time reconfigurability, and struggle to intervene directly in the mapping process, thereby are poorly suited to end‐to‐end threats in complex scenarios. Here, we propose an interface for cross‐domain sensing and security protection based on an optically transparent intelligent metasurface with reconfigurable control over echo amplitude and phase. The intelligent metasurface reshapes the acoustic‐to‐EM mapping and controls the demodulated output without altering the acoustic source signal. We fabricate a prototype with programmable amplitude and phase control and partial optical transparency. Experiments demonstrate three controllable effects along the acoustic–EM transduction chain: acoustic information suppression, ambiguity generation, and hallucinatory speech output in the absence of acoustic excitation. This work provides an integrable and configurable physical‐layer paradigm for cross‐domain protection and information manipulation in cross‐domain sensing systems.

title: Metallurgical Interface Engineering Constructing In Situ Li3N‐Enriched Interphase: A Bulk‐Interface Synergy Strategy Toward Practical Silicon Anodes
content:
A bulk multiphase integration and interphase modification strategy is developed for Si anodes. Sn and M (Bi, Ni) form a conductive composite buffering volume expansion, while a polydopamine‐derived carbon coating transforms in situ into a Li3N‐enriched interphase. The SiSnM@Li3N anode delivers > 1000 mAh g−1 at 15 A g−1, 87.3% retention over 1000 cycles, and wide‐temperature operation (−30°C–60°C), demonstrating practical viability.








ABSTRACT
Silicon anodes are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries but suffer from volume expansion, unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and sluggish Li+ diffusion. Herein, we report a vacuum‐suspension‐melted (VSM) bulk multiphase integration and interphase modification strategy to address these challenges. Unlike conventional mechanical mixing, VSM constructs a SiSnM (M = Bi, Ni) composite with metallurgically bonded Si/metal interfaces, forming a conductive network that buffers internal stress via atomic‐scale interfacial stress transfer. Simultaneously, a polydopamine‐derived nitrogen‐doped carbon coating transforms in situ into a Li3N‐enriched interphase during cycling, which exhibits high ionic/electronic conductivity, accelerates interfacial charge transfer, and suppresses continuous SEI breakdown. The resulting SiSnM@Li3N anode delivers 87.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1.5 A g−1 and >1000 mAh g−1 at 15 A g−1, with reliable operation from −30°C to 60°C. Stable cycling at 2.5 mg cm−2 confirms practical relevance. Full cells with Li‐rich Mn‐based cathodes show stable performance, and 5 Ah‐level pouch cells deliver 84.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 6 A discharge. This work concurrently tackles ionic, electronic, and mechanical constraints, offering a practical path to high‐energy durable Si‐based batteries.

title: Anodic Selective Etching: A Mechanism‐Centric Perspective for Electrochemical Subtractive Manufacturing
content:
This review presents anodic selective etching (ASE) as a versatile electrochemical route for transforming materials into porous frameworks, ultrathin layers, and functional surface architectures. It defines the main mechanistic regimes of ASE, links electrochemical control to microstructure evolution, summarizes representative applications, and outlines the remaining barriers to scalable and predictable subtractive manufacturing.








ABSTRACT
Anodic selective etching (ASE) is a precision electrochemical subtractive manufacturing strategy that enables controllable material removal, interfacial reconstruction, and morphology evolution under electrochemically controlled conditions. Unlike material‐centric reviews that mainly catalogue substrates or products, this mechanism‐centric framework reveals common electrochemical principles, enabling cross‐material comparison, transferable design rules, and predictive control over selectivity, reaction location, and structural evolution. This review unifies ASE across material platforms and structural scales through five dominant modes: composition‐ and phase‐selective anodic dissolution, structural site‐selective anodic etching, semiconductor carrier‐ and space‐charge‐controlled etching, film‐ and passivation‐controlled subtraction, and geometry‐ or three‐phase boundary‐localized etching, together with representative coupled mechanisms. The roles of anodic material characteristics, electrolyte composition, and electrochemical parameters in defining selectivity windows, localization behavior, and structural outcomes are critically discussed. These mechanisms enable low‐dimensional materials, porous and core–shell architectures, surface finishing and shaping, and meniscus‐localized tip fabrication. Key challenges in multicomponent selectivity, electrolyte sustainability, and scalable manufacturing are outlined, alongside opportunities in in situ and operando characterization, multi‐physics modeling, and data‐driven optimization toward reproducible and programmable electrochemical manufacturing.

title: Reactive Phase Conversion‐Enabled 1D/3D Heterostructure Engineering Toward High‐Performance Perovskite Photovoltaics
content:
A reactive phase‐conversion driven bulk crystal modulation strategy was developed via in situ reaction between CMMIMCl and PbI2, establishing a 1D/3D hetero‐dimensional architecture that simultaneously reshapes crystallization pathways, redistributes residual stress, and redefines defect energetics across the film. The resulting inverted devices deliver a certified champion PCE of 26.98%, and perovskite/TOPCon tandem device attain a certified efficiency of 32.98%.








ABSTRACT
We report a reactive phase conversion strategy for 1D/3D heterostructure engineering in perovskite photovoltaics. During crystallization, 1‐carboxymethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium chloride (CMMIMCl) reacts with PbI2, enabling the in situ formation of one‐dimensional (1D) CMMIMPbI3 within the 3D perovskite matrix. This precursor‐level process simultaneously consumes residual PbI2 and constructs an internally coupled 1D/3D heterostructure, which regulates crystallization kinetics, promotes oriented crystal growth, and redistributes residual stress. The resulting 1D framework further modulates defect energetics and interfacial charge transport, thereby suppressing non‐radiative recombination and ion migration. Notably, at an optimized low CMMIMCl concentration, the initially formed 1D‐related species potentially serve as crystallization templates, modifying the crystallization pathway and facilitating more complete conversion of PbI2 into high‐quality 3D perovskite. Benefiting from these integrated structural and optoelectronic improvements, inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.09% (certified 26.98%), while scalable perovskite modules reach 22.01%. Furthermore, wide‐bandgap PSCs achieve a PCE of 23.66%, enabling perovskite/tunnel oxide passivated contact tandem devices with an efficiency of 33.03% (certified 32.98%). This work establishes a versatile route for simultaneous regulation of crystallization, defects, strain, and charge transport in high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Enhancing the Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction of Spinel Co Sites Under an Alternating Magnetic Field by Regulating Their Spin State
content:
The separate incorporation of Zn and Cr atoms into tetrahedral and octahedral Co sites in inverse spinel NiCo2O4 induces a charge redistribution that converts low‐spin Co3+ sites into intermediate‐ and high‐spin states, respectively, thereby altering the d‐band center of Co sites to optimize intermediates adsorption under alternating magnetic field and increase photocatalytic CO2 reduction performance.








ABSTRACT
The integration of spin‐engineered catalysts with an external alternating magnetic field (AMF) in a collaborative manner has emerged as an appealing approach to enhancing photocatalytic performance. However, the intrinsic correlation between spin state of catalyst and the magnetic field‐assisted mechanism still needs to be explored. Here, we propose a spin‐state modulation strategy involving the selective substitution of the geometric configuration of Co sites in the NiCo2O4/C3N4 heterojunction. Separately incorporating Zn and Cr atoms into tetrahedral and octahedral sites induces a charge redistribution that converts low‐spin Co3+ sites into intermediate‐ and high‐spin states, respectively. Detailed characterizations and theoretical simulations reveal that an AMF can increase the concentration of CO2‐derived intermediates on the surface of the spin‐engineered catalysts. This enhancement is strongly correlated with the spin configuration of Co sites. The modulated arrangement of electrons in cobalt alters the corresponding d‐band center under AMF, consequently optimizing the binding strength of crucial intermediates. Remarkably, the Zn‐doped sample with an intermediate‐spin state exhibits an impressive CO production rate of 318.3 µmol g–1 h−1 under an AMF, which is 15 times higher than without AMF assistance. This work provides new insight into developing efficient spin‐related catalysts with the help of an external magnetic field.

title: Probing Phonon Dynamics for Kinetic Stabilization of Single‐Crystal Nickel‐Rich Cathodes
content:
Si─Ti co‐doping in single‐crystal LiNi0.83Co0.12Mn0.05O2 modulates TM─O phonon dynamics, as suggested by combined Raman and DFT analyses. Along with reduced Li/Ni mixing and modified surface chemistry, this phonon modulation is proposed as one possible contributor to the improved oxygen stability. With these combined effects, the optimized cathode delivers 83.17% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 5 C for high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries.








ABSTRACT
Structural degradation and lattice oxygen loss remain major obstacles to the long‐term stability of nickel‐rich layered cathodes, especially under high‐voltage and high‐rate operation. Conventional strategies primarily rely on thermodynamic stabilization via cation doping or surface protection, while the kinetic dimension of oxygen release has received less attention. Herein, we investigate Si─Ti co‐doped single‐crystal LiNi0.83Co0.12Mn0.05O2 cathode materials, which exhibit reduced Li/Ni mixing, modified surface chemistry, and altered transition metal–oxygen (TM─O) lattice dynamics. Combined Raman spectroscopy and phonon dispersion calculations suggest that Si─Ti co‐doping enhances phonon scattering and modifies TM─O optical phonon modes. Operando and synchrotron‐based characterizations reveal substantially enhanced reversibility of lattice oxygen redox and transition‐metal local coordination. As a result, the optimized cathode exhibits suppressed oxygen release and mitigated irreversible phase transitions, retaining 83.17% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 C. These improvements are likely associated with the synergistic effects of thermodynamic and kinetic stabilization, with phonon dynamics proposed as one possible contributor among these coupled effects. This work highlights that the kinetic factors relevant to oxygen release warrant greater attention in the design of durable Ni‐rich cathodes.

title: In Situ Programming of Armored CAR‐Macrophages by Microneedle‐Mediated Gene Delivery for Melanoma Immunotherapy
content:
A self‐locking microneedle platform enables localized in situ programming of tumor‐associated macrophages with antigen‐specific CAR and hypoxia‐responsive anti‐PD‐L1 scFv. The system promotes macrophage‐mediated tumor recognition, inflammatory immune remodeling, and coordinated CD8+ T‐cell responses, while endogenous TYRP1 targeting improves tumor control and survival with predominantly localized checkpoint‐blocking activity.








ABSTRACT
Despite clinical advances in CAR‐T therapy and immune checkpoint blockade, effective immunotherapy for solid tumors remains limited by restricted immune‐cell access and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR‐M) provide an alternative strategy by combining antigen‐directed myeloid programming with local immune remodeling. A self‐locking microneedle platform incorporating mannose‐modified nanoparticles (MNPs) enables localized in situ programming of CAR‐expressing macrophages at melanoma sites. The platform co‐delivers a tumor‐antigen‐directed CAR and a hypoxia‐responsive anti‐PD‐L1 single‐chain variable fragment (scPD‐L1). Initial studies in B16F10‐OVA tumors establish antigen‐dependent CAR activity and coordinated local immune remodeling. Therapeutic efficacy is subsequently evaluated in parental B16F10 tumors using an endogenous tyrosinase‐related protein 1 (TYRP1)‐directed CAR. MNP(TYRP1/scPD‐L1) microneedles delay tumor progression, prolong survival, and promote coordinated myeloid and CD8+ T‐cell responses, while providing lower terminal tumor burden, greater local surface CAR+ tumor‐associated macrophage abundance, and reduced systemic exposure compared with dose‐matched intratumoral administration. Reciprocal depletion further shows that CAR‐programmed macrophages contribute to the antigen‐directed myeloid response, whereas CD8+ T cells are major downstream effectors required for maximal and sustained tumor control. These findings establish a localized transcutaneous strategy that coordinates antigen‐directed myeloid programming with adaptive antitumor immunity.

title: Biomimetic Subcellular Chemomechanical Nano‐Regulator for Allergic Rhinitis Treatment
content:
Pathological extracellular‐matrix stiffening is associated with epithelial mechanometabolic dysfunction and barrier collapse in allergic rhinitis. A spatiotemporally programmable subcellular chemomechanical regulator integrates targeted, ROS‐responsive anti‐inflammatory delivery with catalytic ROS scavenging and antifibrotic matrix remodeling. This preclinical strategy restores mitochondrial homeostasis and epithelial‐barrier integrity, attenuates tissue stiffening and mucosal inflammation, and shifts systemic immune readouts toward tolerance.








ABSTRACT
Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a highly prevalent and debilitating chronic inflammatory disease; however, its complex pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely explored, resulting in a significant lack of effective therapeutic strategies in clinical practice. Here, we found that the submucosal extracellular matrix undergoes profound pathological stiffening during AR development and is associated with severe epithelial mechanometabolic dysfunction and physical barrier collapse. Based on this pathomechanical observation, we developed a spatiotemporally programmable subcellular chemomechanical regulator (SCM) to reconstruct the damaged mucosal barrier. Capitalizing on its precise targeting and cascade‐responsive capabilities, SCM provides immediate anti‐inflammatory activity to stabilize stressed epithelial cells. Beyond this acute intervention, the regulator scavenges intracellular free radicals, attenuates pathological mitochondria‐associated membrane (MAM) over‐coupling, and restores mitochondrial metabolic homeostasis. In parallel, the Mn‐containing nanocore and pirfenidone jointly attenuate fibroblast activation and abnormal extracellular‐matrix stiffening. Formulation‐resolved cellular and animal studies distinguished a predominant TA‐associated contribution to early inflammatory and epithelial‐barrier responses from a predominant PFD‐associated contribution to later matrix remodeling. Full SCM combined these stage‐associated response domains while rebuilding epithelial‐barrier integrity and shifting systemic immune readouts toward tolerance. These findings provide a preclinical mechanobiology‐guided framework for treating AR and other mechanically driven inflammatory diseases.
journal: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents

title: Stepwise Proximity Labeling With a Switchable Organophotocatalyst
content:
The O‐nitrobenzoxadiazole (O‐NBD) unit, originally developed for affinity labeling, is catalytically inactive. However, after reacting with a lysine residue of the protein of interest (POI), the resulting N‐NBD catalyzes the labeling reaction. This switchable proximity labeling approach utilizing the NBD unit selectively labels an interacting partner of the POI and suppresses the nonspecific labeling caused by free catalysts.








ABSTRACT
Photoinducible proximity labeling (PL) using photocatalysts offers high spatiotemporal resolution for profiling protein–protein interactions (PPIs). Conventional approaches require genetic installation of a tag to tether the photocatalyst to a protein of interest (POI), which may perturb native protein function and cause artificial labeling. Ligand‐directed delivery of photocatalysts to native POIs has emerged as a tag‐free alternative; however, this strategy suffers from nonspecific labeling by unbound catalysts and an inherent washing dilemma, where insufficient washing leads to background labeling while excessive washing disrupts ligand binding. These limitations have severely restricted tag‐free and ligand‐directed PPI profiling. Herein, we report a switchable photoinducible PL strategy based on a nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD) unit that becomes catalytically active only after covalent conjugation to a POI. This approach consists of a two‐step process: introduction of an N‐NBD moiety into the POI using a catalytically inactive O‐NBD unit, followed by light‐induced PL catalyzed by N‐NBD. N‐methyl luminol and 1‐methyl‐4‐arylurazole were identified as labeling reagents selectively activated by N‐NBD. Targeting mitochondrial voltage‐dependent anion channel (VDAC) enabled selective labeling and proteomic identification of mitochondrial proteins. This switchable PL method circumvents the washing dilemma, suppresses nonspecific labeling, and enables tag‐free proteomic analysis with improved spatial selectivity.

title: Electric‐Field Responsive Molecular Switch Unlocks Stable 4.5 V‐Class Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
content:
By coupling molecular reactivity with the evolving interfacial electric field, this work introduces an electric‐field coupling agent that functions as a voltage‐gated molecular switch. Above a critical field, field‐driven migration, reorientation, and selective bond cleavage form a self‐limiting gradient interphase, converting the high‐voltage field from a degradation force into an on‐demand trigger for stable 4.5 V sodium layered oxide cathodes.








ABSTRACT
High‐voltage operation of sodium layered oxide cathodes is essential for unlocking energy density, yet the intensified interfacial electric field destabilizes the cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI), posing a persistent challenge. Herein, we reveal that interfacial stability is governed not solely by oxidative tolerance but by the coupling of molecular species to the dynamically evolving interfacial field. Guided by this insight, we define an electric field coupling agent (EFCA) that combines strong field responsiveness with appropriate redox propensity to enable threshold‐gated reactivity. Acting as a molecular switch, the agent remains chemically inactive below a critical field but becomes activated above it through field‐driven migration, reorientation, and selective bond cleavage. A dual‐descriptor framework integrating a customized field sensitivity index (FSI) with HOMO energy identifies sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate as an effective switch. Upon activation, the resulting field‐insensitive and electrochemically inert fragments assemble into a self‐limiting and compositionally gradient interphase with a boron‐rich outer layer. Such coupled interfacial chemistry achieves a counterintuitive field‐enhanced stability, enabling the manganese‐based sodium layered cathode to cycle stably at 4.5 V with 87.9% retention after 1000 cycles and demonstrating practical viability in 1 Ah pouch cells. The mechanism is further validated across analogous layered oxides, establishing a generalizable paradigm for on‐demand interfacial protection in high‐voltage batteries.

title: Entropy‐Triggered Mechanistic Reconfiguration: Unleashing Adjacent‐Site Oxygen Coupling to Circumvent Scaling Limit in Water Oxidation
content:
Entropy‐driven geometric and electronic reconfiguration of a 3DOM high‐entropy spinel oxide unlocks adjacent‐site O–O coupling, triggering an OER pathway switch from the adsorbate evolution mechanism to the oxide pathway mechanism. This mechanistic transition circumvents conventional scaling constraints and reconciles high catalytic activity with exceptional long‐term stability.








ABSTRACT
The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains the anodic bottleneck of water electrolysis for green hydrogen production. The conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) is constrained by linear scaling relationships, whereas lattice oxygen involvement inevitably causes structural degradation, imposing a persistent activity‐stability trade‐off. Here, we realize a mechanistic transition from AEM to the oxide pathway mechanism (OPM), thereby circumventing the activity scaling limit, by constructing a noble‐metal‐free high‐entropy spinel oxide featuring a three‐dimensionally ordered macroporous (3DOM) hierarchical porous architecture. Mn/Al‐induced high‐entropy lattice contraction shortens adjacent‐metal distances, providing the geometric prerequisite for direct O–O coupling. Meanwhile, entropy‐driven electronic redistribution elevates Co valence and modulates Co–O covalency, optimizing oxygenated‐intermediate adsorption and enriching surface *OH species for subsequent O–O coupling. The 3DOM hierarchical porous framework further exposes OPM‐favorable sites and accelerates mass transport. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a low overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm−2, sustains stable operation for over 3000 h at 100 mA cm−2, and enables an anion‐exchange membrane water electrolyzer to achieve 1.604 V at 1 A cm−2 with 2500 h durability. This mechanism‐guided high‐entropy design opens a route beyond the activity‐stability trade‐off.

title: Cascade Radical Homopolymerization of Isocyanide‐Containing Monomers via Photoinitiation
content:
A radical cascade homopolymerization has been developed under photoirradiation, enabled by rational monomer design. The key to its success is a radical relay that converts highly reactive imidoyl radicals into thiyl radicals. These thiyl radicals exhibit high reactivity toward isocyanides, thereby ensuring efficient chain propagation. This strategy affords polythioethers bearing cyclic imine units along the main chain, with degrees of polymerization up to 140.








ABSTRACT
Isocyanides are highly valuable building blocks in organic synthesis and have been established as C1 monomers in transition‐metal‐catalyzed chain‐growth homopolymerization. Although their radical copolymerization with electron‐deficient partners such as acrylates has been reported, the long‐standing challenge of radical homopolymerization remains unresolved. Herein, we report the first successful radical cascade homopolymerization of isocyanide monomers. This strategy is enabled by a novel monomer design that promotes a sequence of radical translocation and ring closure over fragmentation. The process efficiently affords polymers featuring an unprecedented backbone of five‐membered cyclic imines. Moreover, the use of phenyl isocyanide enables the direct synthesis of polyindoles. This work introduces a versatile platform for increasing architectural complexity in polymer backbones and opens new avenues for monomer design in radical polymerization.

title: Halogen‐Dependent Regulation of the Thyroid Hormone Transporter by Antipsychotic Drugs and Their Analogues
content:
Halogenated antipsychotic drugs unexpectedly upregulate the thyroid hormone transporter MCT8 in mammalian cells. This work provides the first example of halogen‐dependent protein expression, revealing a new dimension of structure‐activity relationships in medicinal chemistry.








ABSTRACT
Antipsychotic drugs are primarily used to manage psychosis and other psychotic disorders. Their main mechanism of action involves blocking dopamine D2 receptors in the brain, and they remain important for the treatment for schizophrenia. In this paper, we describe an unusual property of several commonly used antipsychotic drugs and their analogues for their ability to modulate the thyroid hormone transporter system. Specifically, these compounds significantly increase the protein expression of monocarboxylate transporter 8 (MCT8), a key transporter responsible for carrying thyroid hormones across the plasma membrane in a variety of cell lines. Our findings indicate that the presence of halogen substituents plays a critical role in promoting the MCT8 upregulation. Furthermore, the magnitude of this effect is dependent on the nature of the halogen atom, with iodine‐containing phenothiazine derivatives exhibiting the strongest induction of MCT8 expression. The increased transporter expression was accompanied by enhanced cellular uptake of MCT8‐selective fluorescent probes, confirming functional activity. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first example of halogen‐dependent regulation of protein expression in mammalian cells.

title: Universal Transfer Reagents for the Synthesis of Carbon‐Labeled Methyl, Fluoromethyl, and Difluoromethyl Motifs
content:
Unifying multiple isotopic transformations around a versatile precursor class provides a sustainable, practical route to 13C‐ and 14C‐labeled difluoromethyl, monofluoromethyl, cyclopropane, and epoxide derivatives. This platform addresses long‐standing challenges in late‐stage carbon labeling for drug discovery and tracer synthesis.








ABSTRACT
The preparation of 13C‐ and 14C‐labeled difluoromethyl compounds remains a major challenge despite the growing importance of the CF2H group in medicinal chemistry. Here, we report a practical and sustainable solution based on carbon‐labeled sulfoximines readily prepared from primary isotopic sources. These stable reagents act as versatile C1‐transfer agents and provide access not only to difluoromethyl derivatives, but also to cyclopropanes, epoxides, and monofluoromethyl compounds. The strategy enables the efficient synthesis of valuable labeled building blocks and pharmaceutical motifs under mild conditions. By unifying multiple labeling transformations around a common precursor class, this work significantly broadens the scope of carbon‐isotope chemistry for life‐science applications.

title: From Empirical Tuning to Predictive Design: Decoupling Dynamic Bottlenecks in Photocatalytic H2O2 Production via Z‐Score Importance Analysis
content:
A Z‐score and LOFO (Leave‐One‐Feature‐Out) framework deconvolutes entangled dynamic bottlenecks in photocatalysis. Using Au(I)‐based covalent metal‐organic framework isomers with controlled stacking (AA, AB, and ABC) for H2O2 photosynthesis, the dominant rate‐determining factor shifts with stacking: bulk charge transfer limits AA, while surface adsorption limits AB and ABC. This strategy advances photocatalyst design from empirical tuning to a bpredictive, function‐aware paradigm.








ABSTRACT
Deconvoluting the intertwined dynamic bottlenecks of photogenerated charge and reaction substrates remains a fundamental bottleneck in heterogeneous photocatalysis due to the lack of reasonable and effective tools. This study presents a quantitative, interpretable framework to deconvolve the entangled factors limiting solar‐driven photocatalysis. Using Au(I)‐based covalent metal‐organic framework (CMOF‐Au) isomers with controlled stacking (AA, AB, and ABC) as a model platform for hydrogen peroxide photosynthesis, we applied a Z‑score and LOFO (Leave‐One‐Feature‐Out) importance analysis. This approach revealed that the dominant rate‐determining factor shifts with stacking: bulk charge transfer governs performance in AA stacking, whereas surface adsorption limits AB and ABC stacking. The method successfully quantifies the relative contribution weights of key functions (charge dynamics, interfacial transfer, surface adsorption, and mass transport) and demonstrates high predictive power across diverse photocatalysts, including covalent organic frameworks, porous aromatic frameworks, C3N4, and overall water‐splitting systems. By uncovering counterintuitive mechanisms, such as Simpson's paradox, our work establishes a generalizable strategy for decoupling multivariate factors, moving photocatalyst design from empirical tuning toward a predictive, function‐aware paradigm.

title: Stepwise Alloying‐Driven Local Chemical Fluctuations Enables Simultaneous Optimization of Charge and Phonon Transport in BiTe Thermoelectrics
content:
Local compositional fluctuations in Bi0.75Sb0.25Te0.7S0.15Se0.15 produce dense intragranular dislocations. They suppress phase separation, reduce lattice deformation potential, break the effective mass‐mobility trade‐off, and deliver a record‐high average ZT of 0.56 (300–573 K), the highest value ever achieved in BiTe‐based systems.








ABSTRACT
BiTe‐based room‐temperature thermoelectric (TE) material family suffers from intrinsic efficiency‐limiting carrier‐mobility trade‐offs. Herein, we report an n‐type Bi0.75Sb0.25Te0.7S0.15Se0.15 material with tailored local compositional fluctuations, which achieves a peak ZT of ∼ 0.64 at 377 K and a record‐high average ZTave of ∼0.56 over 300–573 K, which stands as the maximum value for BiTe‐based TE systems. The excellent performance originates from conduction band flattening and dense intragranular dislocations, which are produced by the local compositional fluctuations. Band flattening spanning the Γ–A path together with enhanced valleys alignment increase the carrier effective mass, thereby improving the Seebeck coefficient. In addition, intragranular dislocations induce multiscale stress mismatches to achieve efficient phonon scattering, while reducing lattice elastic deformation and weakening phonon‐electron coupling. These synergistic effects allow this alloy a high power factor of ∼14.7 µW cm−1 K−2 and a low lattice thermal conductivity of 0.37 W m−1 K−1 at 377 K. This work proposes a feasible and effective strategy for modulating charge and phonon transport in TE materials.

title: Brønsted Acid Enrichment Around Zeolite‐Encapsulated Pd Promotes Efficient Tandem Catalysis
content:
A metal cation‐directed Al‐siting (MCD‐Al) strategy places Pd nanoparticles encapsulated in Beta zeolite (Pd@Beta‐MCD) catalyst with encapsulated Pd nanoparticles embedded in a locally acid‐enriched microenvironment. By enhancing metal–acid cooperativity and matching the rates of Pd‐catalyzed hydrogenation and acid‐catalyzed alkylation, the catalyst achieves a record cyclohexylbenzene yield of 48.1% with 77.5% selectivity in benzene hydroalkylation.








ABSTRACT
Metal‐acid bifunctional catalyst design is essential for selectivity control in tandem catalysis. However, reactive intermediates often experience a kinetic mismatch between metal‐ and acid‐catalyzed elementary steps, thereby being consumed through competing pathways and diverted toward undesired products. Herein, we developed a metal cation‐directed Al siting (MCD‐Al) strategy to enrich framework Al sites around Pd nanoparticles encapsulated in Beta zeolite (Pd@Beta‐MCD), enabling tunable Brønsted acid site density close to metal sites by controlling metal precursor loading. When Pd@Beta‐MCD was employed in benzene hydroalkylation, the spatial proximity of metal–acid sites accelerated transfer of Pd‐generated cyclohexene to adjacent acid sites, and the high Brønsted acid site density around Pd nanoparticles remarkably facilitated cyclohexene protonation for alkylation. Pd@Beta‐MCD achieved its maximum cyclohexylbenzene yield of 48.1% with a corresponding selectivity of 77.5%, outperforming Pd/HBeta (21.1% and 30.1%) and Pd@HBeta (27.7% and 38.3%), representing the best performance reported to date for this reaction. Moreover, Pd@Beta‐MCD showed superior cycling stability over eight runs. We demonstrated that the concentrated Brønsted acid sites adjacent to metal centers resolve the kinetic mismatch and steer the cyclohexene intermediate toward an alkylation‐dominated pathway. This work provides an effective strategy to strengthen metal–acid synergistic matching and facilitates precise control of key intermediates in tandem catalysis.

title: Pathway Selection in Phenol Oxidation by a Ni(III)−Hydroxo Complex: Solvent and Substrate Control of Proton‐Coupled Electron Transfer
content:
A highly basic Ni(III)─OH complex displays a substrate−controlled crossover between CPET and stepwise PT/ET pathways, while solvent−dependent association dictates the observed kinetics.








ABSTRACT
Understanding the factors governing pathway selection in proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) remains a challenge in oxidative chemistry. Herein, we investigate phenol oxidation by a late‐transition metal hydroxo complex [Na(15c5)][Ni(PS3″)(OH)] ([Na(15c5)][1], 15c5 = 15−crown−5 ether and PS3″ = [P(C6H3‐3‐Me3Si‐2‐S)3]3−). Oxidation in CH3CN affords a mononuclear Ni(II) product, whereas reactions in THF generate a mixed‐valent Ni(II)Ni(III) dimer, revealing a solvent dependence of both reaction pathway and product distribution. Reactions in THF exhibit saturation kinetics and a kinetic isotope effect (KIE) value of 2.1, enabling direct interrogation of the elementary PCET step. Hammett, thermodynamic, and semiempirical free‐energy analyses independently reveal a substrate‐dependent mechanistic crossover: Electron‐rich phenols undergo concerted proton−electron transfer (CPET), whereas increasingly acidic substrates react through a stepwise proton‐transfer/electron‐transfer (PT/ET) pathway. In contrast, reactions in CH3CN display inverse KIE value together with anomalous free‐energy relationships, indicating a kinetically coupled regime in which precursor association and PCET become experimentally inseparable. Moreover, oxidation in CH3CN proceeds 103−104 times faster than in THF, suggesting that the polar solvent facilitates PCET through stabilization of a polarized transition state. These findings establish an example of solvent‐ and substrate‐controlled pathway selection in PCET and highlight how the reaction medium can influence the mechanistic manifestation of O─H bond activation.

title: Beyond Lithium Solvation: Tuning Cation‐Solvent‐Anion Interactions for Stable Lithium‐Metal Batteries
content:
Focusing on the electrolyte chemistry in high‐energy rechargeable batteries, this work identifies a previously overlooked ternary cation‐solvent‐anion interaction motif in non‐aqueous electrolytes and reconciles the gaps between the classical aqueous electrolyte picture and emerging non‐aqueous systems, which can be used to stabilize conversion‐type electrode materials (e.g., sulfur) and enhance their electrochemical performances. 








ABSTRACT
Electrolyte chemistry in nonaqueous solvents is central to the electrochemical performance of high‐energy rechargeable batteries, yet the molecular basis of ion solvation in these systems remains incompletely understood. In conventional dipolar aprotic electrolytes, the high electron‐donating ability of the solvent favors cation‐dominated ion‐dipole interactions, such that anions remain largely free or are only weakly incorporated into cation solvation structures. Here we establish an explicit molecular picture of cation‐solvent‐anion ternary interactions in nonaqueous electrolytes and show that these interactions critically govern both bulk electrolyte properties and electrode‐electrolyte interfaces. We find that fluorinated ether‐based solvents, despite being widely regarded as non‐solvating diluents, can exhibit selective solvation of high‐electron‐donating anions, including halides and polysulfides. Coupling these ternary interactions to the redox chemistry of sulfur electrodes suppresses the dissolution and migration of polysulfide intermediates in ether‐based electrolytes, thus mitigating the shuttle effect and improving the cycling stability of Li°||S cells. More broadly, our findings revise the prevailing view of solvation in nonaqueous electrolytes and provide a molecular framework for solvent design and electrolyte formulation to advance high‐energy lithium‐ and other monovalent cation‐based rechargeable batteries.

title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes
content:
Nature Energy, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02174-8

Mixed-matrix membranes promise to combine the processability of polymers with the transport advantages of porous fillers, yet poor compatibility between the two limits their performance. New research shows that tailoring interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks enables high filler loadings, producing improved membranes for carbon capture.
journal: Nature Energy

title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
content:
Nature Energy, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02171-x

Deep decarbonization benefits health and ecosystems but does not necessarily reduce land, water or mineral pressures. Here the researchers show that different pathways can shift when metals are extracted without changing total demand.
journal: Nature Energy

title: The person behind the scientist
content:
Nature Materials, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02808-y

Matteo Seita and Mengying Liu discuss their reflections as organizers of The Past Metallurgists Society lecture series, where scientists meet to share stories of distinguished metallurgists from the past.
journal: Nature Materials

title: Nanostructures strengthen titanium alloys
content:
Nature Materials, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02801-5

Machine learning guides the design of an additively manufactured titanium alloy containing superfine features at the 10 nm scale through controlled martensitic transformation, which achieves an ultimate tensile strength of more than 1.7 GPa and 7.5% uniform elongation.
journal: Nature Materials

title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
content:
Nature Materials, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02813-1

All-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries are a next-generation high-energy-density solution for energy storage. Here catholyte/cathode interfaces are found to be as important as transport tortuosity in thick sulfur cathodes, and an areal capacity of 10 mAh cm−2 is demonstrated at a stack pressure of 15 MPa and sulfur loading of 6.1 mg cm−2.
journal: Nature Materials

title: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes
content:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02310-7

Oxoboranes, compounds featuring a central dicoordinate boron atom engaged in a B–O triple bond, have long been regarded as highly reactive and are typically observed only as transient species. Although attempts to synthesize them date back to the 1960s, their isolation in the condensed phase has proved challenging. Now, two independent studies describe the isolation of neutral and cationic oxoboranes derived from related diboracumulenes.
journal: Nature Chemistry

title: Sorting reaction pathways to program alkene skeletons
content:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02306-3

Small changes in alkene structure usually mean big changes in synthetic routes. Now, nickel catalysts that sort radical and organometallic pathways can deliver four alkene architectures from related building blocks.
journal: Nature Chemistry

title: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
content:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02302-7

Conjugated molecular belts show unusual electronic and magnetic properties owing to their radially oriented p orbitals. Now, anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts have been synthesized through a nickel(0)-mediated coupling strategy followed by Scholl oxidation. These hybrid nanobelts show global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96 or 120 π electrons.
journal: Nature Chemistry

Particle-resolved 4D nano-tomography identifies fast ionic transport pathways as key regulators of electrochemical activity and reversibility in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

content:

title: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump
content:

Using one Earth system model with increasingly complex plankton food webs, the study finds that greater ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven declines in ocean carbon export, suggesting simple models may underestimate future weakening.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79750-9

Tabernanthe iboga produces the medically important alkaloids voacangine and ibogaine, but key steps in their biosynthesis, as well as the biosynthetic route to the structurally distinct alkaloid ibophyllidine, have remained unresolved. Using genome sequencing, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and biochemical reconstitution, the authors identify the missing enzymes required for coronaridine and voacangine biosynthesis, elucidate the complete pathway to ibophyllidine, and achieve heterologous production of voacangine in Nicotiana benthamiana.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Chemical upcycling of mixed polyolefins via rapid C–H nitration
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79649-5

Post-polymerization modification provides a route to upcycle polyolefin waste, but most current systems have long reaction times and are substrate specific. Here, the authors report the rapid C-H nitration of various polyolefins with high selectivity and functionalisation degrees, forming functionalised polyolefins with enhanced tensile and adhesive properties.

content:

content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79418-4

In this study, the authors used measurement data combined with modeling and machine learning to estimate global human generation of five individual ARGs and intI1, discharge, and surface-water abundance, highlighting hotspots of per-capita generation and total abundance.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78986-9

This study shows that arteriviruses, like coronaviruses, form pore complexes that span their double-membrane replication organelles, pointing to a conserved nidovirus strategy that links the synthesis, export and packaging of viral RNA.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Laser ablation rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry imaging with few-micrometer sampling pixels
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79489-3

In mass spectrometry imaging, smaller pixel sizes usually come at the cost of reduced signal and more complex sample preparation. Here, authors develop a gentle infrared laser ablation approach that maps metabolites and lipids at few-micron pixel sizes in fresh-frozen and clinical tissue in open air.

content:

content:
Nature Reviews Materials, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41578-026-00994-4

An article in Advanced Functional Materials reports a wood–metal–organic framework thermoelectric that converts both heat and evaporation-driven water flow into electricity, inspired by the transport functions of natural trees.

title: Stabilizing non-noble metal electrocatalysts for acidic water oxidation
content: Renewable-powered water splitting needs to move beyond scarce iridium, but non-noble metal electrocatalysts dissolve in acid. This review maps their degradation and stabilization tactics. It also flags a neglected real-world problem: fluctuating solar and wind start-stop cycles speed decay that steady lab tests miss, which demands device-level testing for scalable clean hydrogen.
