title:
Supramolecular
Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation
of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We report the design, preparation, and study of a supramolecular pseudopeptidic cage that selectively binds twin phosphotyrosine (pTyr–pTyr) peptides and modulates their enzymatic dephosphorylation in water. The receptor combines an expanded aromatic cavity specifically designed to encapsulate a twin Tyr-Tyr motif with peripheral Lys-derived ammonium groups that engage phosphate residues through electrostatic interactions. In addition to studying the cage’s binding properties through different experimental and computational techniques, we investigated the ability of the receptor to modulate the kinetics of the irreversible phosphate hydrolysis catalyzed by alkaline phosphatase (ALP). When different substrates are connected through irreversible catalytic reactions, forming a nascent network, the presence of a supramolecular protecting host, able to selectively bind these substrates, modifies the system outcome in a way that cannot be predicted from the mere comparison of individual binding constants. This leads to unexpected, emerging behaviors, altering the relative intermediate concentrations through time and therefore regulating the network response. We demonstrate the biochemical potential of this cage by protecting the twin pTyr–pTyr motif within the activation loop of JAK2 kinase from dephosphorylation by λ-protein phosphatase. Altogether, our results establish supramolecular substrate protection as an effective strategy to regulate multistep enzymatic reaction networks.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Composition-Driven
Discovery of Multimetallic Catalysts
Using Features Inspired by the Virtual Crystal Approximation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Structure–activity relationships built on structure-derived descriptors are a dominant paradigm in catalyst screening. However, this structure-driven framework scales poorly to multimetallic systems, where active sites are heterogeneous, dynamically reconstruct under operating conditions, and require extensive structural enumeration and system-specific descriptor engineering. Here, we introduce a composition-driven screening strategy for multimetallic catalysts using feature construction inspired by the virtual crystal approximation. Specifically, multimetallic sites are represented as composition-weighted pseudoatoms, allowing readily available elemental properties to be converted into predictive features without explicit structural modeling. Unlike elemental fractions alone, these features encode physicochemical differences among the constituent metals. We demonstrate this approach using Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) as a compositionally tunable and reconstruction-prone validation platform for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Combining the composition-derived features with symbolic regression yields an explicit expression for ranking compositions, guiding experimental identification of four high-performance PBAs. We further evaluate this strategy across six literature data sets spanning different catalyst families and reactions, independently training a model for each. Using one of the models, we screen and experimentally validate a perovskite catalyst achieving an overpotential of 189 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in acidic OER. These results demonstrate the broad applicability of virtual crystal approximation-inspired feature construction for composition-driven screening of multimetallic catalysts.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Radical Molecular-Junction
Covalent Organic Framework
for Asymmetric Iodide Conversion: 100,000 Cycles in Zn-Iodine Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Aqueous Zinc–iodine batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their eco-friendliness and safety. However, conventional two-electron cathode hosts suffer from poor cycling life due to polyiodide shuttling and sluggish one-step I–/I2 redox kinetics, which limits their practical usage. Herein, we designed a molecular-junction covalent organic framework (COF) denoted as TNCOF, integrating the tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) donor and the naphthalene diimide (NDI) acceptor. Typically, TTF forms a robust radical-cationic TTF•+ structure by anchoring to iodine electrostatically. TTF•+ and electron-withdrawing NDI within the T•+NCOF molecular junction provide a driving force through an intense local electrostatic potential for the asymmetric iodine conversion (AIC) pathway (I–/I3–/I2 vs. I2/I–), markedly boosting reaction kinetics and suppressing polyiodide shuttling. The optimized T•+NCOF cathode delivers a specific capacity of 228.7 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 and achieves an ultralong cycling stability exceeding 100,000 cycles, which is one of the highest records in this field. In situ measurements, Peak Force Tunneling atomic force microscopy (AFM) results, and calculations confirm the robust adsorption capability of T•+NCOF and demonstrate the accelerated I3– conversion kinetics. This work establishes that a radical-cationic molecular-junction COF enables robust I3– anchoring and a unique AIC pathway, offering a novel strategy to overcome inherent stability challenges in Zinc-halogen batteries.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Electrothermal Mapping:
A Methodology for Decoupling
Redox, Protonation, and Denaturation Dynamics of Cytochrome c
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Differential scanning calorimetry, fluorometry, circular dichroism, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry are routinely used to study thermal and chemical denaturation of proteins. However, these powerful methods monitor protein unfolding in bulk aqueous solutions but overlook interfacial environments, such as lipid membranes and confined crevices, where electrostatic and hydrophobic forces reshape protein conformational landscapes and dictate their function. Herein, we introduce an electrothermal methodology that uniquely probes protein conformational changes in a potential-modulated biomimetic environment. Electrochemistry at the Interface between Two Immiscible Electrolyte Solutions (ITIES) captures nonredox fingerprints of cytochrome c under heat stress, offering a unique perspective on protein behavior without relying on electron transfer reactions and revealing interfacial activity not evident in bulk solutions by conventional methods. Electrothermal mapping presents the protein thermal stability as a current–potential–temperature landscape, enabling direct comparison of the protein’s native and non-native conformational states driven by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Ultimately, our work establishes a new paradigm for predicting protein behavior under heat stress at membrane-like interfaces, with far-reaching implications for biotechnology and medicine, including drug development, enzyme engineering, and protein expression, where protein stability and crevice accessibility are critical.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Transition-Metal-Mediated
Discharge Intermediates
Set Anionic-Redox Potentials and Voltage Hysteresis in Li-Rich Cathodes
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Voltage hysteresis arising from anionic redox reactions remains a central bottleneck for lithium-rich cathodes. While ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has been invoked to describe the charging pathway, its proposed reverse counterpart, metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT), remains experimentally unresolved during discharge. Here, using cation-disordered rock-salt Li2Ni0.33Ta0.66O3 (LNTO) as a model system, we combine electrochemical relaxation analysis with synchrotron-based spectroscopy to identify, for the first time, a metastable reduction intermediate characterized by Ni(2-δ)+/(O–O)n− during discharge, thereby providing direct experimental validation for the MLCT framework. The discovery of this metastable intermediate demonstrates that discharge proceeds through a two-step electrochemical–chemical pathway, wherein the spontaneous relaxation evolution of the metastable intermediate drives free-energy dissipation and voltage hysteresis. Guided by this picture, Ru substitution was introduced to modulate the cation–anion electronic structure, enabling Ru 4d–O 2p hybridization to generate persistent low-energy hole states that lower the energy of the metastable discharge intermediate and shift O–O dimer reduction to higher potentials. We further show that the discharge intermediate serves as the energetic link through which transition-metal electronic structure governs the effective anionic-redox potential. This work provides a discharge-side thermodynamic framework for understanding and mitigating voltage hysteresis in Li-rich anionic-redox cathodes.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Extraframework Cations
Promoted Ultratrace Acetylene
Capture by Coordinatively Unsaturated Nickel Sites in FAU Zeolites
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Removal of ultratrace alkynes to produce polymer- and electronic-grade olefins is an important but extremely challenging task. Here, we report a dual-cation strategy in FAU-type zeolites that enables the unprecedented capture of acetylene at concentrations of parts per million (ppm). The optimized Ni–Ba–Y adsorbent delivers high dynamic uptakes of 0.37–0.82 mmol·g–1 at acetylene concentrations of 500–10,000 ppm, with acetylene/ethylene selectivity exceeding 100 under industrial relevant conditions. Neutron powder diffraction (NPD) and theoretical calculations reveal that Ba2+ at Site I modulate the coordinatively unsaturated Ni2+ centers at Site II, enhancing π-back-donation to adsorbed acetylene. Process simulations demonstrate that adsorptive separation using Ni–Ba–Y achieves over 200-fold higher space-time productivity (STP) of ethylene and reduces energy consumption by over 44% compared with conventional catalytic hydrogenation processes. This dual-cation strategy will promote the design of zeolite adsorbents for challenging industrial separations.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Taming Metal–Electrolyte
Interface via Two-Dimensional
Organic Metal Chalcogenide Colloids for Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Anode-free metal batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technologies, yet their application is severely limited by dendrite growth and rapid capacity decay induced by an unstable metal–electrolyte interface. Herein, we propose a “colloid electrolyte” strategy employing coordination polymer nanosheets as electrolyte additives for constructing anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs). Unlike conventional molecular additives or inert particle suspensions, these colloidal nanosheets provide spatially organized and continuously available interfacial reaction domains, thereby spatially regulating electrolyte component distribution and interfacial reactions. These nanosheets, composed of AgS layers uniformly decorated with fluorinated groups, undergo in situ decomposition at the metal–electrolyte interface. This process generates gradient distributions of Ag nanoparticles and NaF/Na2S species, which guide the spontaneous formation of a functionally graded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This hierarchical SEI enables dendrite-free Na deposition and imparts sustained interfacial protection during cycling. Consequently, high-cathode-loading AFSMBs achieve an ultralong lifespan (&gt;1600 cycles), representing a 10-fold improvement over counterpart cells without the colloidal additive. Notably, 0.5-Ah-level anode-free pouch cells exhibit stable cycling for 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes coordination polymer colloids as a new class of electrolyte additives for advanced alkali metal batteries.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Concerted Ligand-to-Metal
Charge Transfer Absorption
and Localized Photoluminescence in an Fe(III) Photosensitizer
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>There is tremendous interest in the electronic structure of [FeIII(phtmeimb)2]+, the first iron complex to show room temperature photoluminescence (PL) with an excited-state lifetime sufficient for dynamic quenching in fluid solution. Two types of excited states are generated by light absorption, termed the Franck–Condon (FC) state and the thermally equilibrated excited state (THEXI) that is photoluminescent. Herein we report solvatochromic and electroabsorption studies to probe the electronic structure of these two states. The doublet ligand-to-metal-charge-transfer absorption was found to be mostly solvent independent while a notable solvatochromism in the PL spectra indicated the presence of an excited-state dipole in polar solvents (μ⃗ = 16 ± 10 D), best formulated as [FeII(phtmeimb•+)(phtmeimb)]+*. However, standard and higher-order electroabsorption spectra revealed concerted and equal charge transfer from the two tridentate ligands to the metal, giving rise to a significant polarizability change (Δα) without the generation of a dipole moment (Δμ⃗ = 0) best formulated as [FeII(phtmeimb+1/2)2]+*. The strong interligand coupling necessary for such concerted charge transfer is proposed to be mediated by a t2g orbital of the Fe(III) center. Taken together, these findings provide new insights into this famed photoluminescent open-shell iron complex relevant to the design of improved iron photosensitizers.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Cathode Surface Reconfiguration
via Solvent Chemistry
for Durable All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Electrode surfaces and interfaces critically dominate the performance of all-solid-state lithium batteries. However, established additive-oriented strategies physically isolate the cathode from the electrolyte without improving the restricted Li+ transport pathways of the cathode surface. Here, we propose a solvation-mediated chemical etching mechanism governing cathode surface reconfiguration, driven by competition between solvent coordination and lattice stabilization. The solvent coordination, coupled with electron and proton transfer, weakens transition-metal–oxygen covalency and destabilizes lattice-bound surface species, shifting the interfacial energy landscape toward solvation-favored states. This triggers selective transition-metal dissolution and oxygen modulation, ultimately reorganizing confined surface regions into continuous Li+ transport networks. Using micron-sized single-crystalline Li- and Mn-rich cathodes as a model, we demonstrate the formation of a Mn- and O-deficient interfacial layer equipped with a three-dimensional Li+ diffusion network. This functional layer accelerates Li+ diffusion and anionic redox kinetics while suppressing transition metal migration and oxygen release. Consequently, charge-transfer resistance drops drastically (from 585 to 67 Ω) and Li+ diffusion increases 90-fold at 4.8 V, enabling 80.3% capacity retention after 2800 cycles at 2C. This solvent-driven reconfiguration provides a scalable framework for stabilizing diverse cathodes in next-generation advanced batteries.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Discerning between
Excimer and Singlet Fission Sites
Using Modulated Magnetic Field Photoluminescence
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Magnetic field effects play a key role in the characterization of organic electronic materials. In particular, the microscopic processes underlying singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation have been clarified in recent years through the observation and subsequent theoretical explanation of magnetic field effects in these processes. Here, we study magnetic field effects on the luminescence of 5,12-bis((triisopropylsilyl)ethynyl)tetracene, a well-studied material in which both singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation occur. By performing highly sensitive modulated-field magneto-photoluminescence experiments we observe magnetic field effect lineshapes with rich detail, allowing a precise characterization of triplet exciton dynamics. By additionally filtering these magnetic field effects by luminescence wavelength, we can identify the excimer state by its unique magnetic field signature. Finally, we show that a theoretical explanation of these field effects requires a model that explicitly accounts for quantum coherences, which highlights the importance of detailed spin dynamics modeling in understanding magnetic field effects, even at room temperature.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Phototunable Solid–Liquid
Interfacial Energy
via Ion–Electron Coupling
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The solid–liquid interfacial energy governs wetting, adhesion, and friction, yet is commonly regarded as a static property defined by surface chemistry and liquid composition. Here we show that light can reversibly modulate the interfacial energy at chemically invariant semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces by tuning the electrostatic coupling between electronic carriers in the solid and ions in the liquid. Using dark dynamic tensiometry, we directly quantify photoinduced changes in advancing and receding contact angles, revealing pronounced and reversible wettability modulation that is absent on insulating or metallic substrates. Systematic control experiments indicate that, in simple salt electrolytes, the response arises primarily from electrostatic coupling between photomodulated carriers and mobile ions in the electric double layer, rather than from detectable photochemical surface modification or changes in bulk liquid properties. In situ atomic force microscopy and ionovoltaic measurements provide microscopic and quantitative evidence that light attenuates or enhances electrostatic double-layer forces and ion–electron coupling, and reveal a sign reversal in the photoresponse between PFOTS-modified and bare Si interfaces. The opposing responses of PFOTS-modified and bare interfaces persist on p-type Si, showing that the effect is not confined to n-type substrates. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this phototunable coupling extends to reversible control of kinetic friction, enabling active modulation of droplet sliding dynamics. These results also identify imaging light as a potential source of bias in contact-angle measurements at photoactive semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces. These findings establish ion–electron coupling as a tunable thermodynamic lever linking semiconductor physics to macroscopic interfacial energy, opening opportunities for optically controlled wetting, friction, and interfacial transport.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Spatiotemporally Decoupled
Cascade Photocatalysis
on Dual S-Scheme Heterostructure with Interfacial Polarization
Fields and Proton Shuttle Channels
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Transient surface reaction dynamics govern artificial-photosynthesis-enabled multistep tandem biomass oxidation but are hindered by spatially intermingled reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and temporally entangled elementary-step sequences. A spatial-engineering strategy for fabricating ZnS/Sv-chalcogenide/MoSe2 (Sv = sulfur vacancies, chalcogenide = ZnIn2S4, Zn0.5Cd0.5S, CdIn2S4) dual S-scheme heterostructure, with chalcogenide as the shared mediator between the ZnS/chalcogenide and chalcogenide/MoSe2 S-junctions, is developed by anchoring MoSe2 nanoparticles onto chalcogenide nanosheets epitaxially grown from ZnS hollow dodecahedral cages. These ternary-component nanoreactors integrate dual interfacial features, the interfacial localized polarization field and the interfacial proton shuttle channel, to orchestrate dynamic intelligent catalysis. Specifically, the interfacial localized polarization field drives spatially decoupled ROS generation (•OH, •O2–, •OOH) via the asymmetric charge distributions, enabling zone-specific ROS to undertake differentiated oxidation tasks. Interfacial proton shuttle channel drives temporally decoupled elementary-step sequences via the interfacial dynamic hydrogen-bonding networks, thereby liberating pH-dependent proton transfer through directed radical protonation (•O2– → •OOH). This synergy provides a proof of concept for neutral 5-hydroxymethylfurfural-to-2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (HMF-to-FDCA) conversion and demonstrates a fundamental research-to-practical-application capability. This work proposes a generalizable catalyst design paradigm integrating interfacial localized polarization fields and interfacial proton shuttle channels, offering innovative insights for guiding spatiotemporally decoupled multistep cascade catalysis.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Aryl Palladium Acetates
as Highly Active Species in
Intermolecular Heck Reactions of Hindered Olefins
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Despite decades of development since the early 1970s, the intermolecular Heck reaction of hindered tri- and tetrasubstituted olefins with aryl halides has remained a challenge. Traditional approaches relied on rate-acceleration by directing groups or high reactivity of cationic arylpalladium species generated from triflates and diazonium salts. Herein, we report the first general and efficient Heck coupling between trisubstituted alkenes (and selected tetrasubstituted olefins) with aryl iodides and bromides. Our protocol employs simple PdCl2 or Pd(OAc)2 as precatalyst and needs no directing groups. It features an exceptionally broad substrate scope, accommodating diverse (hetero)aryl halides and both acyclic and cyclic olefins, and the reaction proceeds efficiently on a gram scale with remarkably low palladium loadings. The practical value of this method is highlighted by its application in concise synthesis of several pharmaceutically relevant motifs. Mechanistically, HRMS and DFT calculations revealed that phosphine-free complexes of arylpalladium acetates─either monomer [(Ar)Pd(OAc)] or its paddlewheel dimer with bridging acetates─serve as the key active species. These species exhibit minimal steric hindrance, a high partial positive charge, and high electrophilicity at the palladium center, synergistically facilitating the binding and rapid insertion of hindered alkenes.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Symmetry-Breaking Charge Localization Controls Radiationless
Decay in a Multibranched Charge-Transfer State
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Symmetry breaking in multibranched charge-transfer (CT) excited states is generally viewed as a mechanism for excited-state localization, yet how such localization controls the subsequent fate of the excitation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that environmental stabilization of a symmetry-broken CT state can fundamentally reshape radiationless decay in a bent donor–acceptor–donor chromophore. Increasing solvent stabilization drives rapid reorganization toward a lower-energy CT configuration, collapsing the singlet lifetime from 1.98 ns in toluene to 9.2 ps in acetonitrile while increasing the effective nonradiative rate (knr) from 2.14 × 108 to &gt;1.11 × 1011 s–1. Femtosecond transient absorption establishes that formation of the stabilized CT configuration precedes terminal population loss, while triplet accumulation observed in nonpolar media disappears as singlet depletion becomes ultrafast. Controlled toluene–acetonitrile mixtures further reveal that the nonradiative rate does not obey a single invariant energy-gap dependence: distinct energy-gap-law regimes emerge as the CT state is progressively stabilized, followed by a strongly reorganized regime in which knr continues to accelerate despite little additional change in the energy gap. Independently, the changing relationship between emission spectral variance and Stokes shift shows that the nuclear reorganization of the relaxed CT ensemble also changes with stabilization. Together, these results support a solvent-dependent symmetry-breaking landscape in which progressive charge localization reshapes both the excited-state energy and the nuclear coordinates governing access to the ground state. Symmetry breaking therefore acts not simply as an electronic localization process, but as an environmental kinetic switch, converting a long-lived, emissive and triplet-forming CT state into a rapidly quenched excited state.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Photoaffinity Capture
of Unit-Resolved Ubiquitin–Decoder
Contacts Underlying Topology-Selective Recognition of Heterotypic
Chains
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Heterotypic K63/K48 polyubiquitin chains encode diverse cellular outcomes, ranging from proteasomal degradation to nonproteolytic signaling. Although chain topology is increasingly recognized as a critical determinant of these functions, how architectures composed of the same linkage types are decoded into distinct outputs remains poorly understood. This gap has persisted because molecular technologies capable of both chemically capturing topology-selective decoders and defining the unit-resolved contacts underlying selective recognition remain undeveloped. Here we report diazirine-functionalized K63/K48 triubiquitin probes that resolve the unit-specific ubiquitin–decoder contacts essential for topology-selective decoding of the K63/K48 chains with distinct branch architectures. Site-specific installation of a single diazirine moiety into defined ubiquitin units enabled systematic interrogation of the contributions of individual ubiquitin units to topology-selective recognition by quantifying their engagement with decoders through photo-cross-linking efficiency. Specifically, the mixed K63/K48 tribuiquitin (Ub3) probes with diazirine on the K63-linked segment captured a previously unrecognized preference of OTUB1 and RAD23B for mixed K63/K48 chains through more efficient photo-cross-linking than the corresponding branched K63/K48 Ub3 probes. In addition, liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) analysis of the cross-linked products identified auxiliary contacts of the K63-linked segment in mixed K63/K48 Ub3 as the molecular basis for the topology-selective recognition by OTUB1 and RAD23B. Thus, these chemically defined photoaffinity K63/K48 chains provide a versatile platform for dissecting the molecular logic by which heterotypic ubiquitin-chain topologies are decoded into distinct intracellular outputs.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title: Controllable Growth of Micron-Thick Films for Bifacial Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bifacial perovskite solar cells require a micron-thick absorber layer to compensate for optical losses, yet the poor controllability in fabricating high-quality thick films critically limits device performance. Here, we developed an isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor atmosphere control system. By precisely tuning the duration of N2 purging to introduce IPA vapor into the PbI2 annealing chamber, we obtained a porous, highly crystalline PbI2–IPA intermediate film that facilitates subsequent ammonium salt intercalation. This results in a substantially lower energy barrier for the conversion from PbI2–IPA to α-FAPbI3, enabling the spontaneous α-phase formation at room temperature while completely bypassing the undesirable δ-phase. The resulting bifacial PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency of 23.78% (certified 23.71%) and a power generation density of 27.83 mW/cm2 with a short-circuit current density of 29.96 mA/cm2, at an albedo of 0.2, demonstrating excellent performance for bifacial PSCs. This work provides a rational pathway toward efficient bifacial perovskite photovoltaics.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Impacts of Residence Time and Temperature on CO Electrolysis to Acetate at the 100 cm2 Electrode Scale
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The electrochemical reduction of carbon monoxide (CO) to acetate offers a promising route to upgrade waste carbon into a valuable product, yet scale-up beyond laboratory-scale cells remains underexplored. Here, we develop a 100 cm2 CO electrolyzer in a membrane–electrode assembly (MEA) configuration using a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-guided approach. An anode-side serpentine flow field increases electrolyte velocity and anolyte residence time, facilitating oxygen removal and promoting further anodic oxidation of crossover ethanol to acetate. Combined with controlled reactor temperature, these effects improve acetate selectivity and operational stability. At 200 mA cm–2, the electrolyzer achieves a peak acetate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 65% and stable operation for 140 h. These results identify anolyte residence time and reactor temperature as important reactor-level parameters impacting product distribution and stability, providing practical design guidance for selective and scalable CO-to-acetate electrolysis at the 100 cm2 scale.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Architected Si-Based Anodes for All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Silicon anodes have emerged as a key enabler for next-generation all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). In particular, the Li-Si alloy shows a low expansion coefficient and high ionic/electronic conductivity, but remains plagued by poor mechanical integrity and interfacial stability. Here we describe a Mg-doped Si interlayer at the Li metal-Li6PS5Cl interface, which electrochemically transforms into a Li-rich composite anode comprising Li14.39Mg0.61Si4 and Li-Mg alloy during cycling. Mg incorporation promotes the formation of a homogeneous lithiated Si framework, establishing a continuous ion/electron transport network. In addition, the unique porous architecture effectively mitigates stress and achieves favorable mechanical matching with Li6PS5Cl, thereby enhancing structural stability. Paired with a LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode, the cell with an areal loading of 17.9 mg cm–2 delivers stable cycling over 1000 cycles at 3 C with 92.5% capacity retention. This multicomponent anode design offers a new paradigm for structural engineering of Si-based anodes and paves the way for high-energy-density ASSBs.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: When Is Molecular-Dynamics-Predicted Ionic Diffusivity Reliable in Solid Electrolytes?
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Molecular dynamics is widely used to predict ionic diffusivity in solid electrolytes, but the reliability of these predictions is often difficult to assess. Our analysis identifies finite trajectory length, limited cell size, and insufficient sampling as key limitations. Using cubic Li7La3Zr2O12, we show that these limitations can remain hidden behind apparently linear mean-squared displacements and well-behaved Arrhenius relations, leading to inaccurate diffusivities, activation energies, and extrapolated Nernst–Einstein conductivity estimates. Such errors can misrank candidate materials and misdirect computational screening. We examine the local mean-squared-displacement exponent, α(t), as a diagnostic of dynamical convergence and relate it quantitatively to finite-time bias in an MSD-ratio estimator within a caging-diffusion model. This relation estimates a characteristic analysis time for a prescribed accuracy. Independent replicas reduce statistical uncertainty, while selective single-axis expansion mitigates finite-size effects. These findings improve materials ranking and the efficiency of computational screening.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Competitive Coordination of Solvent in Electrolyte to Stabilize Li-Rich Mn-Based Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The practical application of lithium metal batteries equipped with lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxide (LRMO) cathodes is severely impeded by aggressive electrolyte decomposition under operational voltage above 4.5 V. Herein, we discover a unique competitive solvent coordination behavior in the electrolyte solvation structure that enables significant stabilization of LRMO-based batteries. This rarely reported mechanism inspires the design of a low-concentration electrolyte (0.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate, LiPF6), which employs a binary fluorinated solvent system consisting of weakly solvating tris(2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) phosphate (TFP) and ethyl difluoroacetate (EDFA). Benefiting from the optimized solvation structure, the assembled Li||LRMO cells achieve cycling stability, retaining 80.5% of the initial capacity after 450 cycles at 4.8 V and 0.5 C. We further establish a molecular-level interfacial model to elucidate the performance enhancement mechanism. This work provides insights into the unique competitive coordination effect of solvents within solvation structures and offers an innovative strategy for electrolyte design toward LRMO-based battery systems and beyond.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Beyond Current Matching: A Voltage-Matched Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Mini-module as an Alternative to Monolithic Tandems
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Current matching limits the performance of two-terminal (2T) monolithic perovskite-silicon tandems. Voltage-matched (VM) tandems remove this constraint by connecting the perovskite and silicon sub-modules in parallel. Here, we report an area-matched 2T VM perovskite-silicon mini-module with a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.77% at minimal voltage mismatch. Tuning the voltage-matching ratio (VMratio, the ratio of the perovskite to silicon maximum-power-point voltages) through the silicon cell count reveals an asymmetry between the silicon- and perovskite-limited regimes: at equal voltage mismatch, the PCE loss relative to the four-terminal (4T) tandem is 1.1% (absolute) lower in the silicon-limited regime. Under controlled temperature (0–60 °C) and spectral variation, the VM tandem remains within 0.1–1.7% and 0.8–1.2% absolute of the 4T tandem, respectively, demonstrating near-4T performance with a two-terminal connection.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Revealing the Atomic-Scale Degradation of Platinum-Based Intermetallic Nanocatalysts Upon Relevant Fuel Cell Conditions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Platinum-based intermetallic nanomaterials are promising catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in proton-exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, insights regarding their degradation under realistic PEMFC conditions still represent a knowledge gap. Herein, a systematic series of L12-Pt3M (M = V, Cr, or Zn) intermetallics with a similar structure, chemical composition, and morphology were synthesized, and their activity-stability trends were evaluated under conditions relevant to PEMFCs. Time- and potential-resolved catalyst dissolution were acquired and quantified through online ICP-MS using 1 M HClO4 at 65 °C, revealing that the first catalyst/electrolyte contact induces significant catalyst degradation before operation. During electrochemical operation, the anodic dissolution at 65 °C is substantially higher than at 25 °C, and a strong competition between cathodic dissolution and ion redeposition takes place. Identical-location electron microscopy analyses captured atomic degradation processes directly linked to catalyst electrochemical dissolution enhanced by temperature, providing new understanding for developing robust catalysts for PEMFCs.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Thermodynamic Activity Regulation Enables Low-Voltage Alloy-Mediated CO2-to-Carbon Conversion
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Molten-carbonate electrolysis integrates CO2 capture with conversion to storable solid carbon, yet direct carbonate electroreduction suffers from cathodic polarization, raising cell voltage and energy consumption. Here, the cathodic pathway is redesigned by coupling electrochemical alkali-metal alloying with thermochemical carbonate reduction. Alloying with liquid metals lowers the thermodynamic activity of the alkali-metal mediator and shifts its equilibrium alloying potential to more positive values, while sufficient activity must be retained to drive subsequent thermochemical carbonate reduction. These competing constraints define a thermodynamic reactive window that guides liquid-metal screening, identifying Sb as a host. Stepwise experiments separating alloying from open-circuit thermochemical carbon formation directly support the proposed pathway. Liquid Sb sustains CO2-to-carbon electrolysis for 72 h at 700 °C and 2.0 V with 80.9% Faradaic efficiency and 22.08 kWh kg C–1 electrical energy consumption, 36.9% below a reported solid-electrode benchmark. These results establish thermodynamic activity regulation as a strategy for lower-voltage electrochemical–chemical conversion.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Rethinking Creep in Solid-State Batteries: From a Chemo-mechanical Liability to a Design Parameter
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Creep is an inherent time-dependent mechanical response in alkali-metal-based solid-state batteries (SSBs) subjected to sustained stack pressure. Although creep can significantly influence battery performance, its role has often been interpreted narrowly as either a beneficial mechanism for maintaining interfacial contact or a detrimental contributor to cell degradation. In this perspective, we establish a unified conceptual framework by linking sustained loading in the classical definition of creep to stack pressure in SSBs, thereby explaining why creep is intrinsic to their operation. We further argue that creep should be regarded as a chemo-mechanical phenomenon with inherently dual roles, whose competing effects govern the dynamic evolution of electrode–electrolyte interfaces during electrochemical cycling. Finally, we discuss how timescale-based design principles and time-resolved in situ and operando characterization can deepen understanding and guide the rational optimization of creep under practical battery operating conditions, thereby informing the design of durable next-generation alkali-metal SSBs.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Mitigating the Optical-Electrical Trade-Off in Sb2S3 Solar Cells with a Buried Li-Modified ZnO Interlayer
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Thinning CdS electron-selective layers reduces parasitic blue-light absorption in Sb2S3 solar cells but can compromise charge collection and absorber growth. Here, we address this optical-electrical trade-off through crystal-structure-guided buried interface engineering. Exploiting the shared wurtzite structure of ZnO and CdS, we introduce a ZnO interlayer to regulate CdS formation. Reducing CdS thickness from 70 to 30 nm enhances Sb2S3 absorptance at 400–500 nm but decreases internal quantum efficiency (IQE) and increases nonradiative voltage loss, offsetting the optical gain. Undoped sol-gel ZnO improves CdS uniformity and partially restores the cathode contact response without improving long-range structural order. Li modification produces a more ordered ZnO/CdS stack, lowers the ZnO work function, and improves Sb2S3 texture and morphology. Consequently, IQE reaches 94%, with a champion power conversion efficiency of 8.10%. These findings establish a crystallography-guided strategy for integrating optical, electrical, and structural optimization.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Re‐Evaluating the Role of Water in Hexacyanoferrate Cathodes for Sodium and Potassium Ion Batteries
content:
This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the role of water in hexacyanoferrate. By connecting crystal structure, electrochemical behavior, characterization techniques, and regulation strategies, it provides a unified understanding of how water governs structural evolution, electronic structure, ion transport, and interfacial reactions, offering new guidance for rational cathode design.








ABSTRACT
Hexacyanoferrates (HCFs) are among the most promising cathode materials for sodium‐ion and potassium‐ion batteries owing to their open three‐dimensional framework, high operating voltage, and fast alkali‐ion transport. As an unavoidable constituent of hexacyanoferrates (HCFs), water is intimately associated with crystal growth, vacancy formation, local coordination, and framework stability. Water has long been regarded primarily as a detrimental impurity in cathodes because it blocks ion transport, accelerates electrolyte decomposition, and promotes structural degradation. However, recent studies indicate that interstitial and coordinated water exhibit distinct binding strengths, mobilities, and electrochemical reactivities, rendering their roles far more complex than can be described by total water content alone. In this Review, we re‐evaluate the role of water in HCF cathodes by redefining it from a structural impurity to a functional component. We discuss how water governs crystal structure, electronic structure, ion transport, interfacial reactions, and electrochemical performance. We further summarize advanced characterization techniques, particularly neutron methods, for probing the dynamic behavior of water molecules, and highlight regulation strategies. This work establishes a unified framework linking water with crystal, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior, providing guidance for the rational design of high‐performance HCF cathodes.

title: Advances and Perspectives of Cobalt‐Free Li‐Rich Mn‐Based Layered Oxide Cathodes
content:
The cobalt‐free LRMOs exhibit distinctive merits in next‐generation battery technology owing to their high theoretical capacity and low cost. This review systematically summarizes the recently developed cobalt‐free LRMO cathode materials and comprehensively discusses their key challenges, proposed modification strategies, and future perspectives, providing significant support for advancing cobalt‐free LRMOs in the next stage.








ABSTRACT
Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxides (LRMOs) are prioritized for next‐generation batteries due to their high theoretical specific capacity and energy density. In particular, the cobalt‐free LRMOs offer additional competitive advantages due to their lowered production cost and reduced resource dependence. However, the cobalt‐free LRMOs still suffer from persistent structural stability challenges, exhibiting low initial Coulombic efficiency, rapid capacity and voltage decay, and inferior rate capability. To advance cobalt‐free LRMO development, massive research efforts focused on effective regulation strategies have emerged recently. It is therefore imperative to timely summarize these recent works to systematically evaluate the attained achievements, recognize the unresolved issues, and formulate the key optimization approaches in the next stage; however, such related reviews for cobalt‐free LRMOs remain limited. Herein, we carefully examine the fundamental advances in cobalt‐free LRMOs and give a comprehensive review work. Initially, the microstructure of cobalt‐free LRMOs is dissected, and the corresponding electrochemical mechanism is elucidated. In addition, the faced challenges are described and analyzed in detail. More importantly, the currently proposed modification strategies are primarily discussed from the microstructure regulation, element doping and surface coating views. Finally, the significant perspectives are highlighted.

title: Molecular Engineering of Redox Mediator for Accelerated Multi‐Electron Transfer Reactions in Lithium Batteries
content:
This article comprehensively analyzes, from both thermodynamic and kinetic perspectives, how the molecular engineering of RMs affects the redox potential, solubility, stability, and so on. These characteristics strongly dictate the specific capacity and lifespan, elucidating key structure–activity relationships. Finally, we propose systemic strategies expanding beyond isolated liquid‐phase catalysis toward solid–liquid synergistic design and functionalized electrolyte/separator engineering.








ABSTRACT
Lithium–sulfur and lithium–oxygen batteries are highly attractive due to their ultrahigh theoretical energy densities, while their performance is severely constrained by sluggish multiphase reaction rates and limited reaction stability at the cathodes. The conventional solid‐phase catalysts suffer from small interfacial contact area and activity loss of active sites, while the mobile redox mediators (RMs) present a new paradigm for accelerating multi‐electron transfer pathways through a solution‐mediated electron transfer pathway. This review first discusses the critical rate‐limiting factors governing reaction rate at the cathode, and then systematically examines the latest advances in the molecular engineering of RMs for cathode catalysis from the viewpoint of redox potential, solubility, molecular size, and chemical stability. Following these points, we comprehensively analyze, from both thermodynamic and kinetic perspectives, how the molecular engineering of RMs affects the redox potential, solubility, stability, and so on. These characteristics strongly dictate the specific capacity and lifespan, elucidating key structure–activity relationships. Finally, we propose systemic strategies expanding beyond isolated liquid‐phase catalysis toward solid–liquid synergistic design and functionalized electrolyte/separator engineering.

title: Bioinspired Molecular‐Scale Tape Interface Towards Ultrahigh‐Pixel‐Density Flexible Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Devices
content:
Inspired by fish scales, we propose an atomically thin molecular‐scale tape adhering to an indium tin oxide substrate through dynamic bonding, enabling flexible transparent electrodes with preferable stress redistribution, crack bridging, and potential homogenization. This biomimetic transparent‐electrode interfacial strategy offers new insights and promising paths for high‐performance ultrahigh‐pixel‐density flexible quantum‐dot light‐emitting diodes and integrated optoelectronics.








ABSTRACT
Flexible, high‐density integrated optoelectronics underpin emerging wearable information systems and human–machine interfaces. However, as pixel size decreases to a few micrometers, emission uniformity and performance of flexible light emitting diodes (LED) degrade severely due to microscale electrical and optical nonuniformity of electrodes especially after bending, hindering their potential applications. Inspired by fish scales, we propose a molecular‐scale tape interface as a transparent electrode for ultrahigh‐pixel‐density flexible LEDs. An atomically thin MXene layer, assembled via liquid–air interfacial assembly, conformally adheres to indium tin oxide through reversible hydrogen bonding and van der Waals coupling, enabling stress redistribution, crack bridging, and potential homogenization. This electrode enables flexible quantum‐dot LEDs with uniform micro‐area current and emission up to 25 400 ppi and a record external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.4%, maintaining performance after 3000 bending cycles. This biomimetic transparent‐electrode interfacial strategy unites mechanical flexibility with ultrahigh pixel density, advancing high‐density integrated optoelectronic architectures.
journal: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents

title: Trace‐Metal‐Assisted Flash Synthesis for Fast‐Charging Graphite Anodes
content:
Nickel‐assisted flash graphitization transforms petroleum coke into highly ordered graphite in a fraction of a second. During this rapid process, nickel promotes carbon adsorption, rearrangement, and graphite nucleation. The resulting graphite enables fast‐charging lithium–ion battery anodes with excellent cycling stability, retaining 80% of their capacity after 1000 cycles at 15 C.








ABSTRACT
Graphite has remained the dominant anode material in lithium–ion batteries (LIBs), powering portable electronics and electric vehicles (EVs). However, sluggish Li+ diffusion kinetics in natural and synthetic graphite can severely limit charging rates. Overcoming this bottleneck requires the rational design of graphite architectures that enable rapid Li+ transport in LIBs. Here, we disclose a trace‐metal‐assisted flash (TMF) process for the millisecond synthesis of catalytic flashed graphite (CFGr) with exceptionally fast‐charging capabilities. The TMF process induces in situ formation of trace nickel nanoclusters that catalyze ultrafast graphitization of amorphous carbon into highly ordered graphite within <1 s. Raman spectroscopy shows an exceedingly clean graphite material with ID/IG of 0.09, with calculations yielding an interlayer bonding energy (Eb) of −2.297 eV, while diffraction reveals an interlayer spacing (d002) of 3.4 Å. These features enhance structural stability and Li+ accessibility. Consequently, optimized CFGr achieves a high reversible capacity of 347.4 mAh g−1 at 0.25 C and retains 158.8 mAh g−1 at 15 C with 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles, outperforming the rate and cyclability of both commercial graphite and graphite prepared by flash Joule heating. The TMF route can replace conventional energy‐intensive graphitization, reducing energy use and emissions by over 80% and lowering the production cost of premium fast‐charging synthetic graphite by ∼80% to only US$0.84 kg−1. These findings establish a promising pathway to advance fast‐charging graphite anodes into next‐generation LIBs.

title: Strong and Thermally Conductive Graphene‐Bamboo Nanocomposites by Topological Fiber‐Network Engineering Towards Intelligent Energy‐Efficient Floors
content:
A topological fiber‐network engineering and thermorheology‐assisted assembly strategy enables strong, thermally conductive graphene–bamboo composites. Entangled long bamboo fibers provide continuous load‐transfer pathways, while phenol‐formaldehyde (PF) resin facilitates face‐to‐face graphene assembly under low pressure. Integrated into pressure‐sensing smart flooring, these composites enable rapid heat spreading and occupancy‐responsive heating, offering a promising approach to intelligent, energy‐efficient buildings.








ABSTRACT
Smart floor‐heating systems that integrate occupancy sensing with localized thermal regulation offer a promising route toward low‐carbon buildings, yet existing flooring materials cannot simultaneously provide robust mechanical properties and rapid heat delivery. Here, a topological fiber‐network engineering and thermorheology‐assisted assembly strategy is reported that enables continuous thermal‐transport and load‐bearing networks to coexist within a single material. Long bamboo fibers form a topologically entangled framework that simultaneously serves as a mechanically robust scaffold and a three‐dimensional template for graphene nanoplatelet assembly, while thermorheological phenol‐formaldehyde (PF) resin facilitates their rearrangement into ordered face‐to‐face configurations under low pressure. The resulting graphene–bamboo composites (GBC) exhibit metal‐level thermal conductivities of 12.8–116.7 W m−1 K−1 together with outstanding flexural strengths of 75–155 MPa, outperforming conventional flooring materials. When integrated into a pressure‐sensing smart floor‐heating system, the composites enable rapid thermal homogenization and occupant‐responsive localized heating. Whole‐building simulations indicate that nationwide adoption of the composite in pressure‐sensing smart floor‐heating systems in China could reduce annual heating‐electricity consumption by up to ∼208 TWh, corresponding to a ∼37% reduction compared with conventional wood flooring. This work establishes the integration of topological fiber‐network engineering with thermorheology‐assisted assembly as a general strategy for overcoming the thermal–mechanical trade‐off in structural biomass composites and advancing energy‐efficient building materials.

title: Electronic Spin States in Oxygen Reduction: From Identification Divergence to Mechanism Clarification
content:
Based on crystal field theory and molecular orbital theory, this review comprehensively discusses the synergistic modulation of active center spin states on oxygen reduction reaction activity and selectivity, and elucidates the intrinsic origins of the discrepancies in corresponding catalytic reaction mechanisms.








ABSTRACT
The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a cornerstone process in clean‐energy technologies including fuel cells, metal–air batteries, and electrochemical hydrogen peroxide synthesis. Emerging evidence has established the electronic spin states of transition‐metal active centers as a critical descriptor that governs ORR activity and selectivity, yet present studies of the same metal center have reported divergent electronic spin states and ORR pathway selectivity. This review attempts to perform a comprehensive discussion about this divergence. The fundamentals of spin states are first introduced within the frameworks of crystal field theory and molecular orbital theory and the principal characterization techniques for spin states identification. Subsequently, the contradictory correlations between spin states and ORR selectivity reported in different catalytic systems are critically analyzed in terms of d‐orbital occupancy and reaction kinetics. Furthermore, rationally regulating spin states strategies are elucidated to optimize ORR performance. Finally, key challenges and future research directions are outlined, emphasizing the need for in situ characterization, advanced theoretical modeling, and unambiguous identification of active sites. This review will furnish theoretical guidance for subsequent investigations of spin effects, and provide insights into extending spin state engineering to other small‐molecule electrocatalytic reactions.

title: Synergistic Integration of Materials and Design Strategies for Next‐Generation Stretchable Displays
content:
Stretchable materials, structural and micro/nano engineering, and display applications form a closed‐loop roadmap toward uniform, resilient light‐emitting displays for skin‐integrated interfaces, biomedical visualization, soft robotics and AR/VR.








ABSTRACT
Stretchable displays rely on sophisticated integration enabled by materials engineering, structural strategies, and micro‐nano integration, encompassing stretchable substrates, conducting and semiconducting components. This review provides a focused discussion of recent technological advances. We highlight key innovations in stretchable electrodes, interconnects, emissive materials, transistor arrays, circuit layouts, and deformable substrates for their roles in improving electrical uniformity, mechanical resilience, and display performance. Additionally, we summarize the latest strategies for achieving stretchability, either by using intrinsically elastic electronic materials or by structurally engineering rigid components. We introduce emerging applications with substantial potential, including epidermal human‐machine interfaces, conformal biomedical monitoring and visualization, soft robotics with distributed optical feedback, and skin‐integrated augmented reality (AR)/virtual reality (VR) systems, to illustrate the transformative opportunities ahead for stretchable display technologies.

title: Influence of Local Curvature and Structural Chirality on Magnetic Spin Textures in Fe Thin‐Film Möbius Bands
content:
Magnetic Möbius bands with left‐ and right‐handed chirality were fabricated using two‐photon lithography, with SEM imaging confirming the physical geometry. Combined magnetic imaging and micromagnetic simulations reveal how the 3D curvature governs the resulting spin configurations. Geometric chirality breaks rotational symmetry to set a vortex circulation sense based on the initial magnetic state, while high mean curvature drives domain fragmentation.








ABSTRACT
The Möbius band is a fascinating three‐dimensional (3D) architecture that exhibits a geometric chirality where left‐ and right‐handed twists cannot be interchanged via continuous rotation, along with a varying extrinsic curvature. Here, we demonstrate that spin textures in arrays of Fe magnetic Möbius structures are fundamentally governed by their geometric chirality and extrinsic curvature. Magnetic full‐field soft x‐ray transmission microscopy reveals that the unique geometry drives domain fragmentation into nontrivial arrangements in regions of maximal curvature, along with the formation of nontrivial vortex domains. Magnetometry and first‐order reversal curve measurements reveal a complex magnetization reversal process, as the lateral and vertical portions of the Möbius structures respond differently to in‐plane and out‐of‐plane applied fields. Micromagnetic simulations confirm a vortex state with geometry‐driven preferred circulation direction. The resulting spin textures propagate either clockwise or counterclockwise along the Möbius structures, depending on the direction of an in‐plane magnetic field applied along the primary bend of the structure. These geometric‐chirality‐driven effects are manifested in the experimentally captured evolution of the remanent magnetization. Our results demonstrate a new platform where curvature and real space topology of 3D nanostructures may be used as degrees of freedom to tailor spin textures.
journal: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents

title: Suspended TiO2/AlGaN/GaN Synaptic‐Like Photodetectors With Integrated Microheaters for Spatially Resolved UV Discharge Monitoring
content:
A suspended TiO2/AlGaN/GaN synaptic‐like photodetector array with an on‐chip Pt microheater is presented, which possesses the capability to achieve ultrahigh sensitivity and rapid conductance reset via localized Joule heating enabled by the thermal isolation of the suspended architecture for spatially resolved continuous frame‐by‐frame imaging and high‐cycle partial discharge power grid inspection. This device demonstrates ultrahigh sensitivity via photoconductance accumulation, and exhibits a rapid thermal reset in which the capture of the channel electrons at the DX centers and the release of the trapped holes restore the conductance to the dark state. Taking advantage of these unique properties, the photodetector has been successfully applied in spatially resolved continuous frame‐by‐frame imaging UV sensing and high‐cycle high‐voltage partial discharge monitoring for power grid inspection.








ABSTRACT
Partial discharge in power grids emits weak ultraviolet (UV) signals, yet continuous spatial imaging with sensitivity remains challenging for conventional sensors. Although standard photodetectors suffer from low signal‐to‐noise ratio (SNR) and high‐power consumption, synaptic‐like designs utilizing persistent photoconductance (PPC) address these issues through in‐sensor integration but face difficulty in resetting the conductance state. We demonstrate a suspended TiO2/AlGaN/GaN synaptic‐like UV photodetector with an on‐chip Pt microheater. Oxygen vacancies in TiO2 and donor‑impurity X (DX) centers in AlGaN serve as optically writable and thermally erasable traps that modulate the AlGaN/GaN two‑dimensional electron gas (2DEG), enabling time‑integrated sensing and thermal reset. The suspended membrane confines Joule heating to the active region, allowing reset within 2 s. Under 365 nm at 0.42 µW/cm2, the device exhibits a photoconductive gain of 2.8 × 107 and a responsivity of 2.12 × 106 A/W, with stable operation over 120 cycles. A 3 × 3 array enables spatially resolved detection with improved contrast, and a convolutional neural network (CNN) distinguishes corona‑ and arc‑like patterns from simulated images. These results support the use of this detector array for partial discharge inspection in power systems.
journal: Wiley: Small Methods: Table of Contents

title: Leaf‐Inspired Porous Cement‐Based Solar Evaporator With Integrated Water Transport and Thermal Insulation for Stable Wastewater Purification
content:
A leaf‐inspired porous cement‐based evaporator uses a carbon black photothermal surface to absorb sunlight and generate heat for evaporation. Its hierarchical porous structure simultaneously enables thermal insulation and water transport. The device produces clean water from simulated industrial wastewater and effectively removes nonvolatile pollutants, including heavy metal ions and dye molecules.








ABSTRACT
Solar interfacial evaporation offers a highly promising sustainable strategy for wastewater purification, while existing evaporators still face challenges such as wet‐state structural instability and the difficulty of simultaneously achieving efficient water transport and thermal insulation. To address these limitations, a plant‐leaf‐inspired biomimetic porous cement‐based evaporator consisting of a carbon black photothermal conversion layer and a porous cement‐based matrix is designed in this work. The upper layer is responsible for converting light energy into thermal energy, while the lower matrix integrates capillary water transport, thermal insulation, and structural support. The rough porous structure and carbon black synergistically enhance light capture, achieving a solar absorptance of approximately 98%. Meanwhile, the interconnected porous structure continuously delivers water to the evaporation interface, whereas closed pores suppress heat dissipation. The evaporator achieves an evaporation rate of 1.83 kg m−2 h−1 under an irradiation intensity of 1 kW m−2. Simulated industrial wastewater tests further demonstrate its effective retention of heavy metal ions and dye molecules, highlighting its potential for low‐cost and scalable wastewater treatment.
journal: Wiley: Small Methods: Table of Contents

title: Trigger and Measurement of Lattice Temperature Increase in the Phonon Ballistic Regime Over the 70 Ps Timescale for Bulk BaF2
content:
A novel synchrotron‐based method is used to measure heating in a bulk crystal over tens of picosecond timescale, using the same X‐ray pulse as both heat source and probe. Lattice expansion of BaF2 reveals a transient temperature rise governed by ballistic phonon transport at the speed of sound, which sets between the adiabatic and the Fourier limits for heat transfer.








ABSTRACT
We have used a novel approach to quantify the temperature increase of a crystal over the time scale of a single synchrotron x‐ray pulse. The same radiation pulse 73 ps long, has been used both as the source of heat delivered to the crystal and as the probe to measure its lattice expansion via XRD. Synchrotron radiation at 8.5 keV in 16‐bunch filling mode, focused over a circular spot 400 nm in diameter, has been used for high‐resolution measurements of the (4 4 4) peak of BaF2 with fluxes ranging between 2.4×108 and 1.59×1011 photons/s. Data analysis based on a two‐lattice model proves that a temperature increase ΔT = 7.2±0.2 K takes place when the flux is maximum. Numerical simulations based on a combination of Monte Carlo and Finite Element Method show that this experimental result lies between the two limits of zero and infinite velocity for heat transport. A ballistic model of phonon propagation at the average sound velocity of BaF2 shows that an unusual linear energy transfer is expected in the 193 nm‐thick surface layer of the crystal, supporting the presence of two lattice temperatures assumed by data analysis. This model predicts the observed temperature increase with a discrepancy of 19%.

title: Gold Nanoparticle X‐ray Scattering to Detect Small Molecule Effectors of Enzyme‐DNA Allostery
content:
We developed a high‐throughput small‐angle X‐ray scattering assay that utilizes DNA‐conjugated gold nanoparticles to detect allosteric changes in DNA‐binding proteins, while greatly reducing the required protein amount. As a proof‐of‐concept, we screened the DNA repair protein PARP1 against the PEITHO library and identified compounds that altered DNA‐PARP1 conformations. Analyses of PARP1 truncations, surface plasmon resonance, and SDS‐PAGE provided additional validation.








ABSTRACT
Nanomolar‐sensitive, gold nanoparticle‐DNA small‐angle X‐ray scattering (AuNP‐DNA SAXS) was coupled with a single‐day screenable PEITHO small molecule library and identified small molecules that modulate protein allostery on DNA. SAXS is an accurate measure of intra‐macromolecular distance distributions in solution and can be collected in high throughput, but it has rarely been used to screen for small molecule effectors of macromolecular conformation. AuNP‐DNA SAXS reduces sample requirements 200‐fold, enabling nanomolar sensitivity for small molecule screening. We demonstrated the potential of the method using AuNP‐DNA SAXS for screening of a small molecule library with the protein PARP1, as it participates in DNA damage repair (DDR). PARP1 post‐translationally attaches poly‐adenosine diphosphate‐ribose (PAR) to macromolecules, which gathers DDR machinery. By screening the PEITHO library against PARP1 using AuNP‐DNA SAXS, we identified four new, cell permeable, inhibitor leads and differentiated their binding effects. Differentiated binding for multiple PARP1 inhibitors (PARPi) supports the development of precision cancer therapies by directing PARP1 processes down specific pathways and addresses PARPi clinical resistance. The biochemically validated non‐canonical AuNP‐DNA and PEITHO library combination fills a gap in existing methods to identify orthogonal allosteric effectors of DNA binding proteins.

title: Unveiling the Magnetic‐Driven Evolution of Fe3O4 Nanoparticles via Time‐ and Spatially‐Resolved Liquid‐Phase X‐Ray Microscopy
content:
Operando liquid‐cell STXM reveals magnetic‐field‐driven self‐assembly of Fe3O4 nanoparticles in liquid enabling nanometer‐scale, real‐time visualization of magnetic self‐assembly dynamics.








ABSTRACT
Understanding the dynamics of field‐driven self‐assembly in liquids remains challenging because existing characterization techniques generally provide either ensemble‐averaged information or limited compatibility with external stimuli. Here, we introduce an operando liquid‐cell scanning transmission x‐ray microscopy (STXM) platform that enables direct nanoscale visualization of magnetic‐field‐driven nanoparticle dynamics under externally applied and continuously tunable magnetic fields. The methodology combines a custom magnetic actuation stage, liquid‐cell STXM imaging, and molecular dynamics simulations to correlate local structural rearrangements with magnetic stimulation in real time. Using Fe3O4 nanoparticles dispersed in glycerol as a model system, we directly observe magnetic‐field‐induced elongation, fragmentation, coalescence, and large‐angle rotational transitions. Quantitative comparison with analytical model and molecular dynamics simulations reveals the critical role of dipolar interactions, cluster morphology, and collective magnetic amplification in determining the observed dynamic pathways. The methodology further enables the identification of field thresholds associated with structural transitions and provides access to transient configurations that are inaccessible through ensemble‐averaged techniques. This work establishes operando liquid‐cell STXM as a versatile platform for investigating field‐driven nanoscale dynamics in liquid environments and opens new opportunities for studying responsive colloidal, magnetic, and soft‐matter systems.

title:
Cascade
Synthesis of Alternating Thiolactone–Episulfide
Copolymers via Multi-Site Single-Unit Monomer Insertion
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Alternating copolymers are fundamental sequence-controlled polymers, but their synthesis from two independently polymerizable monomers remains challenging because conventional methods rely on selective cross-propagation, limiting monomer combinations and structural diversity. Here, we report a two-step cascade strategy that decouples sequence control from direct alternating copolymerization. We target thiolactones and episulfides, important sulfur-containing heterocycles accessible from biobased or low-cost feedstocks. However, competing homopolymerization pathways in many thiolactone–episulfide combinations complicate their direct alternating copolymerization. In our approach, controlled thiolactone ring-opening polymerization affords well-defined polythioesters, followed by selective episulfide single-unit monomer insertion (SUMI) at every thioester linkage to yield perfectly alternating poly(thioether-thioester)s. This transformation is enabled by S-aryl thioester-mediated SUMI, wherein facile aryl thiolate departure promotes efficient single insertion while suppressing further propagation. Using inexpensive quaternary onium salts without stringent stoichiometric or reaction-time control, the method furnishes 23 new sulfur-rich alternating copolymers with molecular weights up to 157.1 kDa, tensile strengths up to 75.2 MPa, and Young’s moduli up to 2.24 GPa. This cascade route expands the accessible sequence-defined polymer space and creates new opportunities to tailor their properties and functions.</jats:p>

title:
Water-Soluble Pd12 Multicomponent Cage
Enables Selective Separation of 1,4-Dibromonaphthalene from 1,5-Dibromonaphthalene
and Regioselective Bromination of Naphthalene
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The synthesis of intricate supramolecular architectures is driven by the desire to translate structural complexity into functional specificity. Herein, we report the formation of an unusual M12L4L′4 cage (MCC) with double-walled knotted architecture via multicomponent self-assembly of a tripyridyl ligand (L), a tricarboxylate ligand (L′), and a cis-Pd(II) acceptor (M). The structure of the MCC resembles a truncated tetrahedron with two overlaid walls enclosing a distorted cavity. The cavity selectively encapsulates polyaromatic hydrocarbons with two fused rings like naphthalene (G1) and its derivatives [1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5) and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6)], while it is repellent to larger guests in aqueous media. Interestingly, it shows high selectivity for 1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5), which enabled the purification of 1,4-dibromonaphthalene and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6) from their mixture in aqueous media. Furthermore, selective bromination of naphthalene to 1,4-dibromonaphthalene could be achieved within the hydrophobic cavity of MCC in aqueous media under ambient reaction conditions driven by the high specificity of the cavity for G5, while the same bromination in the absence of the cage yields a mixture of dibromo and monobromo derivatives. Thus, the newly designed cage (MCC) could be utilized for developing an efficient strategy for the regioselective bromination of naphthalene, overcoming the challenges associated with separating the product mixture generated in conventional bromination. Moreover, the cage enables efficient separation of the dibromo isomers of naphthalene formed in conventional synthesis.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
A Cryptic
Cytochrome P450 Radical Cyclase Catalyzes
Naphthalene-Ring Closure in Rifamycin Biosynthesis
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The enzymatic assembly of the 8-hydroxynaphthalene chromophore in rifamycins presents a classic biosynthetic paradox: the off-PKS precursor, prorifamycin A (1a), readily suffers nonenzymatic deoxygenative collapse in solution into the aberrant product 8-deoxynaphthoquinones. Here, using in cellulo genetic manipulation, stepwise pathway reconstitution, in vitro enzymatic assays, molecular docking, and DFT calculations, we identified Rif-Orf0 to be a cytochrome P450 radical cyclase. Rif-Orf0 converted 1a to the 8-hydroxy-7,8-dihydronaphthalenoid intermediate prorifamycin B (1b) through a low-barrier biradical cyclization, and the RifS/RifT dehydrogenase pair rapidly captured and oxidatively aromatized 1b to 34a-deoxyrifamycin W (2). This Rif-Orf0 and RifS/RifT enzymatic cascade outcompeted the spontaneous deoxygenative shunting that afforded 8-deoxynaphthalene-type rifamycins, thereby enforcing the production of 8-hydroxynaphthalenoid rifamycins. This study expanded the catalytic repertoire of cytochrome P450 enzymes and resolved a long-standing question in rifamycin biosynthesis by characterizing how tailoring enzymes canalized reactive intermediates from spontaneous reactions toward defined natural product architectures.</jats:p>

Chemical Society

title: Tuning the Reversible E – Z Photoisomerization of a Stilbene-like Ligand via Lanthanide Complexation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The segmental stilbene-like ligand E- DiL1 displays only an irreversible E → Z photoisomerization under UV-light irradiation due to the overlapping of its absorption spectrum with that of its isomer Z-DiL1, which is further hampered by competing prejudicial intra/intermolecular photoreactions. These limitations can be overcome by exploiting the conformational and electronic changes induced upon connecting E-DiL1 to [Y(hfac)3] rare earth cargoes. In the target {E-DiL1[Y(hfac)3]2} adduct, the connection of the electron-withdrawing Y(III) guest extends the aromatic delocalization and shifts the absorption band to the red. This restores a clean E-to-Z isomer switching of the bridging stilbene-like unit upon visible light irradiation at 420 nm or by simple exposition to room light. The steric hindrance induced by the [Y(hfac)3] containers also prevents detrimental competing photoreactions. The electronic decoupling of the two terimine units in the photoisomerized {Z-DiL1[Y(hfac)3]2} adduct gives rise to a blue shift of the ligand-centered 1π* ← 1π transition and the operation of reverse Z-to-E photoisomerization upon selective near-UV excitation at 380 nm. The guest-induced enlargement of the amplitude of specific excitation wavelengths for inducing E-to-Z and Z-to-E photoisomerizations paves the way for selective signaling in biocompatible environments.</jats:p>

Chemical Society

title:
Cu Aerogel Doped with
Dual-Functional AgNi Sites Enables
Selective CO2 Electroreduction to Ethanol via Boosted *CO
and *OH Generation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Selective electrocatalytic CO2-to-C2H5OH conversion remains challenging, due to intricate multielectron transfer, complex C–C coupling, and Cu-based catalysts inherently favoring C2H4 over C2H5OH for lack of *OH-generating sites. Herein, we propose a bifunctional dual-doping strategy that simultaneously stabilizes *CO intermediates and facilitates *OH generation to regulate bond cleavage toward selective C2H5OH. As a prototype, Cu metal aerogel doped with Ag and Ni atoms is designed, in which Ag sites facilitate *CO formation with enhance *CO adsorption strength, while Ni sites boost *OH generation through water dissociation. Their synergy shifts *CHCOH bond cleavage preference from C–O to Cu–C bonds, thus switching the dominant C2 product from C2H4 to C2H5OH, confirmed by in situ infrared spectroscopy and in situ Raman spectroscopy. Thus, AgNi dual-doped Cu aerogel achieves a C2H5OH Faraday efficiency of 47.4%, with C2H5OH/C2H4 ratio of 3.1, outperforming most state-of-the-art Cu-based catalysts under constant current density. This work provides critical insights for designing high-performance Cu-based aerogel catalysts with precisely regulated bond cleavage, advancing practical CO2-to-C2H5OH technology.</jats:p>
journal:
