Chemical Society

title:
From “KGeP”
to the Protonated P4-like Anion (HGe3P)2– and
the Endohedral Zintl Cluster [Mn@Ge10P2]3–
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>P4-like Zintl anions (Tt2Pn2)2–, which combine the properties of the formally underlying homoatomic units, Tt44– or Pn4 (Tt = tetrel, group 14 element; Pn = pnictogen, group 15 element), are versatile starting materials for ternary clusters. However, not all of the theoretically possible Tt/Pn elemental combinations are accessible, and not all of them show decent reactivity. A particularly challenging elemental combination is that of Ge and P, in contrast to homoatomic P4 or Gen4– (n = 4, 9) that are widely used for corresponding reactions. The only report on a trinuclear complex, [Cd3(Ge3P)3]3–, obtained by reacting a “(Ge2P2)2–” anion, raised questions about the assumed 2:2 ratio of the atoms in the starting material. Herein, we aimed at clarifying the mystery about the composition and identifying a means of accessing new M/Ge/P-based cluster architectures. Regarding the first, we disclosed that the anion is actually not a 2:2 unit, but the first protonated version of a binary P4-like Zintl anion, (HGe3P)2–, which finally rationalizes the composition of the previously reported trinuclear complex. The anion was obtained as its [K(crypt-222)]+ salt by the extraction of “KGeP” with ethane-1,2-diamine (en), acting as a Brønsted acid toward the Zintl anion. 1H NMR spectroscopy and computations of NMR chemical shifts confirmed the presence of the protonated anion in the salt and in solution. As (HGe3P)2– did not show the desired reactivity, we used the more reductive extraction solution of “KGeP” in situ for a follow-up reaction with [Mn(Cp*)2], yielding the first Ge/P-based endohedral Zintl cluster, [Mn@Ge10P2]3–.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Ligand Curvature Controls
the Size of Self-Assembled
Twisted Metallacycles
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Coordination-driven self-assembly often yields dynamic libraries of metallacycles whose size distribution is difficult to control, and ligand-design strategies for directing such equilibria have so far been limited to discrete changes in coordination angles. Here we introduce the first twisted metallacycles, in which ligand curvature is tuned through the tether-to-twist approach. Two twistacene dipyridyl ligands with only a 6° difference in the overall bend: the nearly planar Pl (14° twist) and the twisted Tw (34° twist) assemble with (dppp)Pd(II) and (dppp)Pt(II) corners {M} into dynamic equilibria between rhomboidal {M}2L2 and hexagonal {M}3L3 metallacycles. NMR, nanoESI-MS and X-ray crystallography show that racemic ligands self-sort with high fidelity: socially, into heterochiral meso {M}2L2 rhomboids, and narcissistically, into homochiral {M}3L3 hexagons. Van ‘t Hoff analysis shows ring expansion to be endothermic and entropy-driven throughout, with an enthalpic cost rising from 6–10 kJ mol–1 for Pl to 17–18 kJ mol–1 for Tw. This is explained by increased strain energy for mismatched planar ligands in {M}2L2 assemblies. A few degrees of backbone curvature therefore reshape the free-energy landscape of coordination-driven self-assembly.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Hydroxamate Reticular
Chemistry beyond Metals: Single-Crystalline
Two- and Three-Dimensional Boron–Hydroxamate Covalent Organic
Frameworks
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydroxamate chelation has already enabled robust metal–organic frameworks. Here, to move the corresponding reticular chemistry beyond metal nodes, hydroxamate chelation has been integrated within heteroleptic tetracoordinate B(O,O)(N)(C) centers to construct four single-crystalline boron–hydroxamate covalent organic frameworks, namely SUM-306–SUM-309. Bayesian optimization enabled the growth of diffraction-quality SUM-306 single crystals, while linker isomerism and functionalization yielded a series spanning two-dimensional hcb and three-dimensional pcu-h frameworks. Structural comparison reveals extended anti-B–phenylene–B arrangements in SUM-306 and SUM-307 and folded syn arrangements in SUM-308 and SUM-309, associated with their respective two- and three-dimensional propagation. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy, B K-edge XANES, and electronic-structure calculations support tetracoordinate boron formation and differentiated yet substantial bonding throughout the B(O,O)(N)(C) environment. As a representative of the series, SUM-308 retains accessible microporosity, exhibits a BET surface area of 1279.9 m2 g–1, and preferentially adsorbs and dynamically separates CO2 from N2. These results extend hydroxamate reticular chemistry beyond metals and establish a mixed-linkage strategy combining chelation, donor–acceptor coordination, and covalent anchoring for single-crystalline boron-based framework construction.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Dopant-Free
Octahedral-Distorted Spinel Cobalt Oxide
for High-Performance Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Developing efficient and stable transition-metal catalysts for acidic water oxidation requires the exploration of multiple structural regulation factors. Although foreign-element doping and morphological engineering have been widely employed, they often complicate the catalyst structure and obscure the origin of activity. Here, we demonstrate that octahedral cobalt–oxygen–octahedral cobalt bond-angle distortion is a key structural parameter correlated with the intrinsic OER activity of spinel cobalt oxides. Through in situ X-ray spectroscopic and imaging techniques, we identify that this long-overlooked Co-octahedra-distortion-induced structural regulation can effectively modulate Co-3d electronic structures and Co–O hybridization. This optimization weakens the adsorption of key oxygen intermediates and increases the propensity toward the oxide path mechanism. The resulting undoped cobalt oxide exhibits high activity in the acidic oxygen evolution reaction, achieving 2.31 V at 3 A cm–2 in a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer. This discovery provides a new perspective to reevaluate cobalt spinel oxides and establish a novel structure–activity relationship between bond angle distortion and performance.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Electrothermal
Coupling Strategy Enables Catalytic
Unsaturated Acid Production through Highly Selective Oxidation on
Modified Heteropolyacids
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>High-value unsaturated acid production from thermally catalytic oxidation of unsaturated aldehydes still faces difficulty in controlling undesired deep oxidation on metal oxide composites or simple P–Mo–V heteropolyacids. Herein, we propose an effective electrothermal coupling strategy by combining a mild electric field with the traditional fixed-bed reactor, without an elaborate catalyst design, to improve selective oxidation. Using the methacrolein oxidation to methacrylic acid on a Keggin-type pyridine-modified P–Mo–V heteropolyacid in steam as a probe, the catalytic rate (0.62 mmol·gCat–1·h–1) and selectivity (95.7%) are, respectively, promoted by ∼25% and ∼15% under an electric field (0.2 W), exceeding comparable literature benchmarks. Mechanistic studies reveal the favorable influence of the applied electric field on the surface adsorption/desorption and diffusion kinetics, catalyst structure and properties, interfacial H2O structure (competitive adsorption with aldehydes/acids), and activation barrier. Additionally, techno-economic analyses reveal that the operation cost, energy consumption, and carbon emission are reduced by ∼22%, ∼21%, and ∼95%, respectively, while the profit is increased by ∼31%, compared with conventional thermal catalysis. This strategy also shows generality across diverse heteropolyacid catalysts and substrates, offering a feasible avenue to improve oxidation selectivity.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Exceptionally
Strong Helix Induction Translates a
Fast Negative Photochromic Response into Rapidly Self-Erasing Structural
Color
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dynamic modulation of structural color in cholesteric liquid crystals requires strong helix induction to achieve visible selective reflection and rapid, reversible modulation of the helical pitch. Although photochemical control of selective reflection is well established, achieving large wavelength shifts at low dopant concentrations with rapid spontaneous recovery remains challenging. Here, we investigate the structural features associated with the exceptionally high helical twisting power (HTP) of a binaphthyl-based chiral dopant. Systematic structural comparisons reveal that mesogenic substitution at the 7,7′-positions and the presence of imidazole units at the 2,2′-positions are associated with strong helix-inducing ability. The resulting dopant exhibits an HTP of 827 μm–1, enabling red, green, and blue selective reflection at concentrations below 0.5 mol %. Combining this high-HTP dopant with a fast negative photochromic binaphthyl-bridged imidazole dimer enables large, reversible shifts in the selective-reflection wavelength under visible-light irradiation. Upon cessation of irradiation, spontaneous thermal recovery of the photochromic dopant restores the helical pitch on a time scale of seconds, resulting in rapid self-erasure of photopatterned structural colors without an additional stimulus. These findings demonstrate how exceptionally strong helix induction can be combined with rapid negative photochromism to achieve dynamically tunable and spontaneously self-erasing structural colors in cholesteric liquid crystals.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Elucidation of the
Final Step in the Biosynthesis
of Bacillithiol Reveals tRNA-Dependent Ligation of Cysteine
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bacillithiol is a physiologically significant low-molecular-weight thiol that contributes to the maintenance of redox homeostasis in most Gram-positive bacteria. While the biosynthesis of its sugar scaffold (GlcN-Mal) has been established, the final cysteine–transfer reaction remains unresolved. In this study, a chemical synthesis of bacillithiol and the GlcN-Mal intermediate is achieved in order to characterize the cysteine incorporation reaction catalyzed by BshC, which is encoded outside the bacillithiol biosynthetic gene cluster. Our results show that BshC requires cysteinyl-tRNA derived from the translational machinery to mediate amide bond formation with the sugar scaffold. In fact, BshC appears to be the first characterized enzyme that utilizes tRNA for carboxylate activation during amide bond ligation between the cysteinyl-tRNA electrophile and a nucleophilic substrate outside of ribosomal protein synthesis. Further analysis reveals that BshC exhibits selectivity with regard to both the stereochemistry of malate and the aminoacyl-tRNA donor, likely reflecting precise substrate binding and tRNA recognition. Collectively, this study completes the biosynthetic description of bacillithiol and reveals a rare tRNA-dependent amidation reaction in thiol metabolism that underpins bacterial redox homeostasis.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Co-Oriented Fusion
Enables Ultrafast Epitaxial Growth
of Single-Crystal Perovskite Films
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Single-crystalline halide perovskite films are attractive for high-performance optoelectronics, yet their scalable synthesis is limited by the intrinsic trade-off between rapid growth and the preservation of single crystallinity: increasing supersaturation accelerates film formation but typically triggers misoriented nucleation and polycrystalline coalescence. Here, we report a co-orientation-driven fusion growth strategy that enables ultrafast epitaxial formation of single-crystal perovskite films under high-supersaturation conditions. Guided by sapphire step edges, multiple nuclei adopt identical crystallographic orientations, evolve into aligned nanosheets, and subsequently fuse into a continuous single-crystal film. This approach yields high-quality films with lateral dimensions up to 6 mm within minutes, corresponding to growth rates as high as 2000 μm min–1. The strategy is applicable to multiple A3B2X9-type halide perovskites, including Cs3Bi2I9, Cs3Bi2Br9, Cs3Sb2Br9, and MA3Bi2I9. Photodetectors based on single-crystal Cs3Bi2I9 films exhibit a responsivity of 138.5 mA W–1 and a specific detectivity of 4.62 × 1011 Jones, demonstrating the potential of this approach for scalable optoelectronic applications.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Hot-Air-Driven Postdeposition
Crystallization of Colloidal
Photonic Paints for Freeform Structural Coloration
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Colloidal photonic crystals display vivid and iridescent structural colors through wavelength-selective reflection from periodic particle arrays, offering an attractive alternative to conventional pigment-based coloration. However, most colloidal photonic crystals are fabricated as films under well-controlled assembly conditions, whereas freehand deposition generally produces poorly ordered particle arrays. In this study, we demonstrate structural-color colloidal paints composed of silica particles dispersed in a photocurable acrylate resin, in which hot-air blowing induces particle rearrangement and long-range crystallization after coating, achieving both paintlike processability and pronounced structural colors. Elevated temperature enhances particle mobility, while airflow-induced shear promotes collective particle rearrangement, enabling crystallization without predefined film geometries or confined shear processing configurations. Hot-air blowing dramatically increases the reflectance peak height and narrows the peak width under optimized conditions. The particle volume fraction and coating thickness further regulate the macroscopic paint flow, enabling either the preservation of brush-defined patterns or the generation of stochastic-flow-induced textures. The structural colors can be adjusted by varying the particle size and volume fraction, and the structural-color paints are applicable to diverse substrates. By decoupling freeform deposition from subsequent colloidal crystallization, the proposed strategy establishes a versatile paintlike platform for artistic expression, decorative coloration, and spatially programmed optical surfaces.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Low-Temperature
Growth of Nanostructured Ti–Si–C
MAX Phase Coatings Enabled by Highly Ionized Reactive Physical Vapor
Deposition
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>MAX phases are a unique class of layered compounds that combine metallic and ceramic properties, making them highly attractive as multifunctional materials for next-generation technologies. However, their synthesis typically requires elevated temperatures, posing a major challenge, particularly for thin film growth, where substrate limitations and integration constraints hinder widespread technological implementation. This work demonstrates that highly ionized physical vapor deposition (PVD) techniques can significantly lower the growth temperature required for direct, single-step MAX phase synthesis. Using the archetypal Ti–Si–C system as a benchmark, coatings deposited by reactive cathodic arc evaporation (r-CAE) and reactive high-power impulse magnetron sputtering (r-HiPIMS) at a growth temperature of 550 °C are systematically investigated. By integrating ab initio simulations, synchrotron X-ray diffraction, and atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, this study reveals that phase competition and defects are critical factors governing MAX phase formation under kinetically constrained growth conditions. Notably, r-CAE yielded indirect evidence consistent with the formation of a Ti2SiC MAX nanostructure (estimated phase fraction ∼4.5%) embedded within a Ti5Si3Cx matrix, while r-HiPIMS produced a Ti3SiC2 coating with an unconventional in-plane c-axis orientation at a 200 °C lower growth temperature than conventional direct current magnetron sputtering. These findings underscore the potential of highly ionized PVD growth methods to reduce MAX phase synthesis temperatures and expand substrate compatibility, thereby facilitating the broader application of MAX phase coatings.</jats:p>

title:
A Dynamic W-VO2/Nb2C
Heterostructure-Integrated Scaffold for Photothermally Amplified Sonodynamic
Osteosarcoma Therapy and Bone Regeneration
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The comprehensive clinical management of osteosarcoma requires an integrated approach to eradicate malignancies and subsequently reconstruct critical-sized bone defects. Herein, a spatiotemporally responsive therapeutic scaffold (WVM@GM) is engineered by embedding a tungsten-doped vanadium dioxide (W-VO2)/niobium carbide (Nb2C) Schottky heterojunction within a porous gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA). Upon near-infrared II (NIR-II) irradiation, the localized temperature rise triggers the metal–insulator phase transition (MIT) in W-VO2, narrowing the bandgap and strengthening the built-in electric field of the heterostructure. This dynamic electronic modulation effectively elevates the density of carriers under ultrasound (US) irradiation, thereby amplifying reactive oxygen species (ROS) production to achieve a highly efficient sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Following neoplastic clearance, modulating the external physical stimuli shifts the scaffold into a proregenerative mode. Specifically, the engineered biophysical microenvironment synergizes with the mechanical stimulation of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) to drive bone tissue regeneration. Transcriptomic profiling reveals the activation of focal adhesion, Wnt, and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways, actively regulating the coupling of angiogenesis and osteogenic differentiation. In vivo evaluations validate that this platform effectively ablates tumors and successively rebuilds bone defects. Overall, this photothermally modulated heterojunction strategy establishes a rational and sequential paradigm for osteosarcoma therapy and bone tissue regeneration.</jats:p>

title:
Noncontact Neuromorphic
Emotion Inference via Gaze
Interaction
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Understanding social emotion through physiological signals remains highly challenging, as it requires bulky devices and computer systems, limiting its practicality in real-world applications. Here, we propose a neuromorphic approach that decodes affective states from pupillary responses by integrating physiological feature extraction, spiking neural computation, and memristive hardware simulation. Pupil dynamics provide a noncontact physiological signal for studying social-interaction and attentional demands. We derived individual and dyadic features from infrared pupil-diameter recordings from 108 participants and encoded them as spikes for classification by a spiking neural network (SNN). The framework was evaluated in four independent binary tasks defined by the experimental protocol. These tasks examined familiarity and an empathy-related contrast, as well as competition versus cooperation and low versus high attentional demands. With solid spike encoding and a spike-event loss, the SNN trained on combined individual and interactive features achieved performance comparable to the strongest conventional machine learning baselines with an accuracy of 95.4%. We also fabricated h-BN/WSe2 memristors and used their measured conductance characteristics to calibrate a model of RRAM weight mapping and variability. Software-based inference with this model linked the measured device behavior to network performance. A variation-aware training (VAT) strategy that incorporates device-inspired noise during software training improved simulated postmapping accuracy by up to approximately 9 percentage points across the evaluated tasks. Operation-based calculations provided highly efficient estimates of arithmetic and RRAM array-core read energy, achieving approximately 11.28–11.30 fJ per synaptic operation. These results support the use of dyadic pupil features for classification of the studied conditions and demonstrate the benefit of accounting for measured device variability during software training.</jats:p>

title:
Inhalable Redispersible
Gallium-Phenolic Complex Reprograms
Lung Microbiota and ROS-NETs Crosstalk to Prevent Radiation-Induced
Lung Injury
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>RILI remains a major complication of thoracic radiotherapy, in which reactive oxygen species (ROS) and altered pulmonary microbial signatures may contribute to neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation and tissue injury. Current preventive and therapeutic strategies fail to adequately address these interconnected pathways. Here, we report an inhalable, redispersible gallium-luteolin-PVP complex (PLGa) designed to prevent RILI by targeting ROS and lung microbiota-associated inflammatory signaling linked to NET formation. The PVP-stabilized metal-phenolic network confers exceptional colloidal stability, enabling PLGa to efficiently penetrate airway mucus, reach distal lung regions, including alveolar spaces, and achieve prolonged retention after inhalation. Gallium within PLGa restores pulmonary microbial homeostasis by suppressing pathogenic bacteria while promoting short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production derived from potential probiotics, thereby inhibiting LPS-TLR4-NF-κB-NETs-associated inflammatory signaling. Concurrently, luteolin effectively scavenges ROS and directly suppresses NETosis. These synergistic actions protect mitochondrial homeostasis and modulate radiation-induced damage. In a murine RILI model, inhaled PLGa, administered prophylactically, significantly mitigated acute inflammation, reduced NET formation, and attenuated the progression of chronic pulmonary fibrosis, as validated by multiomics analyses (transcriptomics, metabolomics, and 16S rRNA sequencing). Importantly, PLGa demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and minimal systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study identifies PLGa as a locally deliverable dual-pathway preventive platform that modulates the ROS-lung microbiota-NETs crosstalk. This work provides mechanistic insights and a promising translational strategy for the prevention of radiation-induced lung injury.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Iron–Sulfur
Nanonutrition by FeS2 Nanoparticles Alleviates Iron Deficiency
in Plants
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Iron (Fe) deficiency disrupts plant growth, photosynthesis, redox homeostasis, and metabolism. In this study, pyrite-type FeS2 nanoparticles were investigated as a coupled Fe–S nanonutrition platform for alleviating Fe deficiency. Using Arabidopsis thaliana and tomato, FeS2 was benchmarked against EDTA-Fe and soluble Fe and/or S sources. FeS2 restored growth, chlorophyll accumulation, photosynthetic performance, and redox balance, while exhibiting sustained Fe/S release and preferential association with root surfaces and near-membrane regions. Nutrient dissection experiments showed that FeS2 produced more consistent recovery of Fe-responsive, S-assimilation, and redox processes than soluble Fe, S, or Fe+S supplementation. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed reversal of Fe-deficiency-associated programs and coordinated normalization of Fe acquisition, sulfur metabolism, and redox pathways, generating a recovery state distinct from that induced by EDTA-Fe. FeS2 also showed no detectable phototoxicity toward photosystem II. Multilevel biosafety assessment showed no detectable impairment of PSII photochemistry and limited acute toxicity in earthworm and zebrafish models. Together, these findings establish FeS2 as a mineral nanonutrition platform linking root-interface Fe/S delivery with coordinated physiological restoration under Fe deficiency.</jats:p>

title:
A Seawater-Compatible
Nanocluster Dilute Electrolyte
for Low-Cost Long-Lifespan Four-Electron Zn–I2 Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Four-electron aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (4eAZIBs) offer high energy density and intrinsic safety, but their application is limited by poor reversibility of the I0/I+ redox and instability of the Zn anode in aqueous electrolytes. Here, we propose a low-cost dilute domain-segregated nanocluster electrolyte (DSNE) based on sulfobetaine methacrylate (SBMA) for high-performance 4eAZIBs. In the bulk, SBMA self-assembles into nanoclusters with hydrophobic interiors and hydrophilic surfaces, partitioning the electrolyte into activated and nonactivated water domains. The nanoclusters disrupt the hydrogen-bond network of water, suppress water activity, and maintain fast ion transport through dynamic Zn2+ adsorption on their surfaces. SBMA also preferentially adsorbs on both electrodes. At the iodine cathode, its quaternary ammonium groups strongly coordinate with ICl2–, raising the hydrolysis barrier of I+ and enabling reversible I0/I+ conversion. At the Zn anode, interfacial SBMA reduces active water and anion accumulation, suppressing side reactions. Consequently, a 4eAZIB full cell with DSNE achieves stable cycling for over 16,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Moreover, using natural seawater as the solvent (providing the Cl– source), the DSNE system sustains over 12,000 cycles at 10 A g–1, demonstrating potential for sustainable, low-cost energy storage. This work offers a viable strategy for low-cost, high-performance 4eAZIBs.</jats:p>
