title: Heterogeneous Integration: Design Principles for Advanced Liquid Crystal Elastomers With Spatially Programmable Properties and Functionalities
content:
Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are advancing beyond simple uniform deformation toward spatially programmable properties and integrated functionalities, driven by heterogeneous integration. This review organizes these strategies into three hierarchical levels: mesogen orientation heterogeneity, polymer network architectural heterogeneity, and macroscopic modular assembly, and outlines potential directions toward functionally integrated LCE systems.








ABSTRACT
Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) uniquely merge liquid crystal anisotropy with rubbery elasticity, positioning them as cornerstone materials for soft actuators. As the field is progressing from laboratory demonstrations toward practical applications in soft robotics and biomedical devices, it is moving beyond the simple, uniform deformations toward advanced spatially programmable properties and integrated functionalities. The design principles underlying these advances lie in heterogeneous integration, defined as the intentional spatial design of chemical, structural, or orientational differences across a unified LCE system, permitting precise programming of differentiated actuation directions, mechanical gradients, and sequential responsiveness unattainable in homogeneous LCEs. Heterogeneous integration pervades almost all advances in alignment techniques, network engineering, and device assembly. This review categorizes the diverse achievements into three hierarchical strategies: heterogeneity in orientation, heterogeneity in polymer network architecture, and heterogeneous modular assembly. We systematically summarize the mechanistic origins, achievable precision, and functional outputs of each approach. Furthermore, we outline future directions from discrete patterning to continuous gradients, from single‐dimensional to multidimensional integration, and from static programming to adaptive evolution. This review establishes a coherent conceptual blueprint to guide the rational design of next‐generation intelligent LCE systems.

title: Bioinspired Low‐Power Mechanical Sensing Technologies
content:
Low‐power mechanical sensing technologies, spanning signal acquisition, processing, and actuation, provide promising solutions for energy‐efficient sensing systems in healthcare and environmental monitoring. Drawing inspiration from biological mechanosensory systems, this article systematically summarizes bioinspired strategies for structure‐enabled signal acquisition, neural‐inspired signal processing, and closed‐loop actuation. The representative applications, challenges and future perspectives of bioinspired low‐power mechanical sensing technologies are also discussed.








ABSTRACT
Bioinspired low‐power mechanical sensing technology offers a promising solution to address the escalating energy consumption challenges faced by conventional sensing systems. Traditional mechanical sensing architectures, relying on dense sensor arrays and continuous data acquisition, suffer from substantial power consumption and limited long‐term deployability. In contrast, biological mechanosensory systems achieve high sensitivity, robustness, and adaptive intelligence with minimal energy expenditure through structure‐enabled signal acquisition, efficient neural processing, and closed‐loop actuation. Accordingly, this article evaluates recent advances across the entire bioinspired mechanical sensing pipeline, encompassing signal acquisition, processing, and actuation. At the acquisition frontier, bioinspired sensing strategies based on web‐like, slit‐organ, lever‐based, and skin‐inspired topologies are reviewed, illustrating how structural amplification, intrinsic filtering, and directional selectivity enable efficient signal capture with ultralow energy overhead. Building upon these front‐end mechanisms, low‐power signal processing strategies inspired by biological nervous systems are discussed, emphasizing efficient signal transduction and event‐driven, neuromorphic computation to mitigate redundant data handling. Subsequently, biological actuation mechanisms and their engineered counterparts are summarized, highlighting sensorimotor coupling and closed‐loop feedback as critical routes to further energy optimization. Finally, representative applications in healthcare and environmental monitoring are presented, alongside current challenges and future trajectories, providing a comprehensive framework for developing next‐generation mechanical sensing platforms.

title: Redefining Water Oxidation Selectivity Through Electrolyte Microenvironment Engineering
content:
This review systematically summarizes the reaction mechanisms of electrolyte engineering in regulating two‐electron water oxidation (2e− WOR) for hydrogen peroxide production. The research focuses on carbonate systems as well as inorganic and organic hybrid systems, comprehensively analyzing the advantages and disadvantages of each system in terms of catalytic activity, operational stability, and side‐reaction suppression. Furthermore, this review outlines prospective frontier strategies including the construction of composite micro‐systems, carbon cycle‐coupled coproduction, and integrated in situ H2O2 separation, aiming to provide theoretical guidance for breaking thermodynamic limits and achieving efficient green electrosynthesis.








ABSTRACT
The two‐electron water oxidation reaction (2e− WOR) offers a sustainable route to in situ H2O2 production from water, distinct from the anthraquinone process and direct H2/O2 synthesis. Its central challenge is the competition between H2O2 formation and the four‐electron oxygen evolution reaction (OER), governed by water polarization, hydroxyl‐intermediate formation, O─O bond construction, peroxy‐species desorption, and product stability. Because catalyst‐site regulation alone rarely optimizes selectivity, stability, and productivity simultaneously, the electrolyte microenvironment becomes a critical reaction variable. Through specific ion adsorption, electric‐double‐layer reconstruction, local pH control, solvation and hydrogen‐bond‐network regulation, and interfacial electric fields, electrolytes reshape intermediate configurations, proton‐electron transfer barriers, and H2O2 decomposition. This Review introduces the framework of “electrolyte‐encoded reaction pathways” to describe how electrolyte‐derived interfacial states differentially regulate competing H2O2‐forming channels. It distinguishes direct surface‐mediated 2e− WOR, electrolyte‐assisted direct 2e− WOR, and indirect electrolyte‐mediated anodic H2O2 synthesis, thereby separating pathway regulation from reaction‐network reconstruction. By linking electrolyte descriptors and catalyst‐electrolyte coupling to selectivity, H2O2 stability, and system‐level performance, this framework redefines the electrolyte as an active variable in reaction‐network design.

title: Radiative Thermal Management for Extreme Environments: Mechanisms and Design Strategies
content:
In this review, we discuss the fundamental mechanisms of radiative cooling and solar heating, material and structural design strategies, hybrid approaches integrating additional heat transfer pathways, and durability‐oriented designs addressing environmental stresses. Key challenges including environmental durability, multifunctional integration, performance trade‐offs, and scalable manufacturing are highlighted to guide the development of practical passive thermal regulation systems.








ABSTRACT
The energy‐intensive and environmentally unsustainable nature of conventional air‐conditioning systems, combined with the accelerating impacts of climate change, has underscored an urgent need for environmentally friendly and durable thermal regulation technologies. In response, radiative thermal management technologies, including radiative cooling and solar heating, have emerged as promising passive approaches. However, conventional standalone radiative thermal management systems often exhibit performance limitations under extreme thermal conditions and diverse environmental stressors, highlighting the need for comprehensive and adaptive approaches. In this review, we discuss the fundamental physical mechanisms and material engineering strategies of radiative thermal management, encompassing intrinsic material properties and structural design principles. Furthermore, we introduce hybrid approaches that integrate radiative thermal management with thermal conduction, thermal insulation, phase change materials, and evaporative cooling, as well as dual‐mode radiative thermal management strategies designed to cope with extreme thermal environments. Additionally, we explore environment‐adaptive design strategies that address complex environmental stressors by improving self‐cleaning ability, ultraviolet (UV) resistance, fire retardancy, and mechanical robustness. Finally, we outline key challenges and future research directions, including material limitations and device trade‐offs, the expansion toward multifunctional applications, and scalable manufacturing. Collectively, this review provides a comprehensive perspective on the practical realization of next‐generation radiative thermal management technologies.

title: Advanced Separators for High‐Safety and High‐Energy‐Density Rechargeable Batteries
content:
Separators govern battery safety and energy density via structural stability, pore/wettability, and ion transport efficiency. This review compares separator differences of monovalent (Li+/Na+/K+) and multivalent (Mg2+/Zn2+/Ca2+) batteries, summarizes safety strategies including dendrite suppression, thermal runaway mitigation, overcharge protection, side‐reaction inhibition, and energy density advances like ultrathin, lightweight, high‐voltage, and electrochemically active, and outlines intelligent design for intrinsically safe high‐energy‐density batteries.








ABSTRACT
The growing dependence of modern society on batteries places higher demands on safety and energy density. Separators are a key component for electrical insulation and structural stability to ensure battery safety. Their inactive volume, ability to regulate solvated ions and transport efficiency also directly impact the energy density of batteries. This review elucidates the relationship between the thermal stability of linear/cyclic polymers and thermal runaway onset, and discusses how organic/inorganic materials enhance safety and energy density by tuning pore structure, thickness, wettability, and mechanical properties. The differences between monovalent (Li+/Na+/K+) and multivalent (Mg2+/Zn2+/Ca2+) ions are compared, and how the polar separator‒electrolyte interaction regulates ion solvation is revealed. Safety‐oriented separator strategies, including thermal runaway mitigation, dendrite suppression, ion flux homogenization, overcharge protection, and aging analysis, are evaluated. Recent advances in separators for high‐energy‐density batteries, such as ultrathin, lightweight, high‐voltage‐stability, electrochemically active, integrated separator‒electrolyte, are summarized. The challenges of balancing safety and energy density are highlighted, specifically porosity and mechanical strength, safety responses compromising energy density, lab‐to‐factory translation gap. Forward‐looking perspectives are outlined through advanced processing, intelligent design, and integration, paving the way for high‐energy‐density intrinsically safe batteries.

title: Direct Recycling of Lithium‐Ion Batteries With Aqueous Relithiation: Mechanistic Insights and Recent Advances
content:
As lithium‐ion battery (LiB) direct recycling moves from established lab‐scale feasibility toward scale‐up, this review outlines the mechanistic understanding needed to establish universal process parameters for aqueous relithiation (AR). Fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic principles are developed alongside key literature findings on lithium restoration, morphology retention, and impurity control. These mechanistic insights, standardized reporting, and experimentally grounded modelling can guide AR toward commercial scale.








ABSTRACT
This review explores the advances and challenges in direct recycling of lithium‐ion battery (LiB) cathode materials via aqueous relithiation (AR), with emphasis on the thermodynamic and kinetic factors governing lithium migration and reintegration into degraded active materials across ternary layered oxides, olivine, and spinel crystal structures. While aqueous treatments, mainly hydrothermal relithiation (HR), demonstrate strong potential for restoring electrochemical performance, scalability remains a critical barrier. The advantages and limitations of batch studies in defining thermodynamic boundaries are evaluated, and pathways toward continuous processing, compositional upcycling to emerging chemistries, and standardized impurity reporting are proposed. The success of this method further relies on effective cathode sorting, advanced data‐driven process controls, and the establishment of unified benchmarks to enable fair comparison across studies. Ultimately, aqueous relithiation lies at the intersection of scientific discovery and industrial application, where operational boundaries, logistical frameworks, and regulatory alignment will shape its transition into industry.

title: Voltage Hysteresis Induced by Fragile Quasi‐Flat Bands in Oxygen‐Redox Cathodes
content:
Focusing on the long‐standing challenge of large voltage hysteresis (>1 V) in oxygen‐redox cathodes for lithium‐ and sodium‐ion batteries, this work proposes a unified framework centered on the instability of quasi‐flat‐band electronic states. It rethinks the electronic origin and mitigation of voltage hysteresis, providing a new physical picture for enabling more reliable operation of oxygen‐redox cathodes at high voltages.








ABSTRACT
Cathodes exploiting oxygen redox chemistry underpin the realization of lithium battery systems with specific energies beyond 600 Wh kg−1. However, voltage hysteresis exceeding 1 V, especially during the first cycle, remains a long‐standing and unresolved challenge, severely limiting energy efficiency and practical deployment. Here, we propose a quasi‐flat‐band framework in which oxygen 2p states near the Fermi level are intrinsically sensitive to perturbations. Even weak perturbations, such as minor lattice distortions during delithiation or thermal vibrations at room temperature, can disproportionately amplify band dispersion and induce hysteresis. This insight reframes the long‐standing design strategy by extending it beyond suppressing structural reconstructions to include control of perturbation‐driven electronic instability. Future materials design should pursue two principles: stabilizing symmetry to sustain quasi‐flat‐band characteristics and engineering orbital hybridization to enhance their robustness against perturbations. This work rethinks the origin and mitigation of voltage hysteresis, bringing oxygen‐redox cathodes closer to reliable operation at high voltages.

title: Fano‐Engineered Au@Se Core–Shell Colloidal Pigments for Dual‐Mode Structural Color
content:
High‐index selenium shells turn gold nanospheres into visible‐range hybrid resonators. Electric‐dipole coupling between the Se‐shell Mie mode and Au‐core plasmon generates a Fano‐like spectral dip, allowing one colloidal pigment to transmit and reflect different colors. The solution‐processable Au@Se particles form UV‐curable color filters, writable structural‐color inks, and polarization‐selective optical readout.








ABSTRACT
Colloidal structural colorants are attractive because they are substrate‐free and solution‐processable, but single‐component plasmonic or dielectric colloids usually exhibit broad visible resonances that limit chroma. Here we report Au@Se core–shell colloidal pigments in which a plasmonic Au core is embedded within a visible‐range Mie‐resonant Se shell. The key signature is not the gradual red shift expected from passive dielectric loading, but an asymmetric hybrid feature with compressed linewidth, consistent with Fano‐like interference between the broad electric‐dipole response of the Se shell and the narrower Au‐core electric‐dipole response. The hybrid mode yields Q factors up to ≈15 in freely dispersed colloidal pigments, producing narrow transmission windows and spectrally separated reflection bands from the same liquid dispersion. By independently tuning the Au core diameter and Se shell thickness in a benchtop synthesis, we achieve broad visible color tuning in transmission and reflection and enlarge the accessible international commission on illumination chromaticity (CIE) area relative to single‐component Au or Se colloids. The particles are formulated into ultraviolet (UV)‐curable resins and writing inks for 254‐ppi color filters, freeform paper deposition, and polarization‐selective readout. This work establishes a colloidal design rule in which the shell acts as an active visible resonator rather than a passive refractive‐index coating.

title: Nonlinear Electro‐Optic Visible Photonic Circuits for Solid‐State Quantum Defects
content:
Integrated visible photonic engines are central to scalable control of solid‐state quantum defects. A monolithic thin‐film lithium niobate circuit integrates nonlinear frequency conversion and GHz‐bandwidth electro‐optic switching, generating milliwatt‐level off‐chip 532 nm light with a 42.2 dB extinction ratio. Nanosecond‐gated excitation addresses a nitrogen‐vacancy center in diamond, providing optical initialization and readout for coherent spin manipulation and time‐resolved fluorescence detection.








ABSTRACT
Integrated visible photonic engines for solid‐state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt‐scale visible light generation and high‐contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip‐scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high‐fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic thin‐film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform integrating periodically poled frequency conversion with GHz‐bandwidth electro‐optic (EO) switching. The device delivers off‐chip green‐light power exceeding 1 mW with an extinction ratio (ER) of 42.2 dB, enabling coherent spin control and time‐resolved lifetime measurements of individual nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) centers in diamond through nanosecond gating. System performance is validated through pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), Rabi oscillations, and Ramsey interference, supported by time‐tagged photon counting with nanosecond resolution. By unifying sufficient nonlinear light generation with high‐speed active manipulation, this platform establishes a scalable framework for the realization of high‐rate quantum communication nodes.

title: Demagnetization‐Driven Nanoscale Chirality‐Selective Phonon Transport
content:
Chiral heat flow is switched in a ferromagnet/chiral α‐SiO2 heterostructure by controlling the angular momentum of demagnetization‐driven chiral phonons. When phonon handedness matches the crystal chirality, nanoscale thermal transport is enhanced; the opposite handedness suppresses transport, establishing a magnetization‐tunable chiral phonon diode.








ABSTRACT
Chiral‐lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality‐selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality‐selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α‐SiO2. Using magneto‐optic thermometry, we show that the effective thermal conductivity of α‐SiO2 depends systematically on both the magnetization direction of [Co/Pt] and the structural handedness of α‐SiO2. This behavior is supported by first‐principles‐based molecular dynamics simulations, which reveal chirality‐dependent phonon transport across the ferromagnet/chiral‐material interface. The magnetization‐dependent thermal on/off ratio reaches 1.07 at room temperature and increases to approximately 1.2 at 50 K, reflecting reduced Umklapp phonon–phonon scattering. These results establish a ferromagnet/chiral‐material platform for controlling nanoscale heat flow through chiral phonons.

title: Pulsed Oxidative–Reductive Electrolysis Over Dual Cu and Co Single‐Atom Sites for Urea Electrosynthesis
content:
Alternating oxidative–reductive pulses synchronize CO2‐derived *CO and NH3‐derived *NHx intermediates over dual Cu and Co single‐atom sites, enabling urea and ethyl urea formation with a total C─N Faradaic efficiency of 42 ± 4%. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations elucidate complementary Cu and Co functions, while oxidative controls suggest an additional Wöhler‐type pathway to urea formation.








ABSTRACT
Electrochemical C─N coupling of CO2 with nitrogen species offers a sustainable route to urea and related chemicals but is constrained under steady‐state electrolysis by mismatched reaction kinetics. Here, pulsed oxidative–reductive electrolysis temporally coordinates CO2 reduction and NH3 oxidation, regulating the generation and coexistence of carbon‐ and nitrogen‐derived intermediates. Co/CuNC, containing atomically dispersed Co and Cu sites within a nitrogen‐doped carbon (NC), achieves a total C─N faradaic efficiency of 42 ± 4%, dominated by urea (20 ± 2%) and ethyl urea (16 ± 2%), with respective yield rates (YR) of 295 ± 25 and 50 ± 5 mmol h−1 gcat−1. In situ synchrotron x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals potential‐dependent changes in Cu and Co oxidation states and coordination environments, while in situ infrared spectroscopy identifies pulse‐regulated *CO and *NHx intermediates and suggests concurrent electrochemical and Wöhler‐type pathways. Density functional theory calculations reveal complementary site functions: Cu favors *NH2 formation, whereas Co more strongly stabilizes *NHx and *CO intermediates, with *CO also accessible at Cu sites. These findings establish temporal coordination of reactant activation, intermediate populations, and active‐site states as a mode‐enabled strategy for accessing higher‐order C─N products.

title: Conductivity‐Engineered Polymeric Rear Contacts for Bifacial Sb2(S,Se)3 Solar Cells and 4T Tandem Photovoltaics
content:
ABSTRACT
Transparent rear contacts that combine efficient charge extraction with low optical loss are essential for extending Sb2(S,Se)3 photovoltaics toward bifacial and tandem applications. Here, a solution‐processed 2,2′,7,7′‐tetrakis(N,N‐di‐p‐methoxyphenylamine)‐9,9′‐spirobifluorene (Spiro‐OMeTAD)/poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) bilayer is introduced as a polymeric transparent rear‐contact architecture for bifacial Sb2(S,Se)3 solar cells. Established dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) solvent engineering reduces the sheet resistance of PEDOT:PSS by nearly four orders of magnitude while preserving its high transparency, enabling front‐ and rear‐side power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 8.2% and 3.3%, respectively. Under 1‐sun front plus 0.3‐sun rear illumination, the bifacial device delivers a power generation density of 9.7 mW cm−2. Combined optical and electrical analyses reveal that the lower rear‐side response arises from asymmetric photogeneration, direction‐dependent carrier transport, depth‐dependent absorber inhomogeneity, and enhanced recombination associated with the transparent rear interface. The device is further integrated as the top cell in an electrically independent Sb2(S,Se)3/CuInSe2 four‐terminal tandem, achieving a combined standard‐condition PCE of 12.32%. This work demonstrates a solution‐processable polymeric rear‐contact strategy complementary to conventional inorganic transparent contacts and identifies the optical and interfacial factors governing bifacial Sb2(S,Se)3 photovoltaics.

title: Empirical Understanding of Li‐Ion Transport Through Hetero‐Grain Boundaries Within Li‐Electrolyte Interface for Stable Li Metal Anodes
content:
This study experimentally clarifies the origin of preferred Li‐ion transport across hetero‐grain boundaries, bridging the theoretical gap. Optimizing the MgO/MgF2 heterointerface provides direct evidence of enhanced ionic conductivity.








ABSTRACT
Understanding the Li‐ion transport mechanism across the Li/electrolyte interface (LEI) is fundamental for stabilizing Li‐metal batteries (LMBs). In particular, hetero‐grain boundaries (h‐GBs) such as Li2O/LiF or Li2CO3/LiF are theoretically recognized to provide favorable Li‐ion pathways within inorganic LEI; however, experimental verification of h‐GB‐mediated Li‐ion transport remains elusive. In this study, we provide experimental evidence for favorable Li‐ion transport associated with h‐GBs using a tailored h‐GB‐rich MgO/MgF2 heterostructure (MgO/F). Multifaceted analyses indicate that the MgO/MgF2 heterointerfaces establish a favorable Li‐ion transport environment through coupled interfacial effects, with the enhanced defect population potentially contributing to increased Li‐ion carrier availability. Furthermore, upon contact between the Li substrate and the MgO/F layer acting as the LEI, the MgO/F layer spontaneously constructs a dual‐interfacial architecture: an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase abundant in h‐GB‐rich Li2O/LiF and a Li/substrate interphase consisting of a Li–Mg alloy with rapid Li surface migration. This synergistic interfacial architecture maximizes the practical efficacy of h‐GB‐rich MgO/F for stabilizing Li metal anodes. Consequently, the h‐GB‐rich MgO/F demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, significantly outperforming bare Li in both symmetric and full cells. This study provides experimental insight into the role of h‐GBs in inorganic interfaces and provides a strategic blueprint for designing highly stable LMBs.

title: Thickness‐Defined Transport Regime Toward Near‐Ideal Area‐Type Switching
content:
By thinning the oxide layer, memristors pass from diode‐like and battery‐effect‐dominated behavior toward eventual short‐circuit failure. Within the intermediate 5–6 nm window, they reach a near‐ideal analog area‐type switching regime, featuring symmetric hysteresis, area‐dependent conductance, and continuous linear programming of HRS and LRS with minimal disturbance to the counterpart state.








ABSTRACT
Area‐type memristors are attractive for analog in‐memory computing, but their use is often limited by parasitic charge storage, causing readout drift, non‐pinched hysteresis, and degraded readout fidelity. We show that near‐ideal area‐type switching emerges within a tunneling‐governed transport regime in ultrathin layers that suppresses charging‐related readout artifacts. By varying the thickness in TiN/Ta2O5/Pt in a range of 3–10 nm, we reveal the transition from filamentary switching to near‐short‐circuit transport with two gradual‐switching modes with different readout stability. The 5–6 nm thickness window suppresses non‐pinched hysteresis and short‐time drift while preserving analog switching, yielding nearly polarity‐symmetric hysteresis and readout, clear area scaling, and continuous near‐linear conductance modulation. Our analysis indicates that trap‐assisted tunneling dominates the stabilized‐state response, whereas ionic redistribution governs pristine‐state reconstruction and the stability boundaries. A compact model is derived for the 5 nm device which reproduces the quasi‐static I–V behavior and the dynamic resistance evolution based on pulse‐width‐dependent characteristics. The verified model is provided as Verilog‐A code enabling simulation in circuit design tools. Our results demonstrate that ultrathin scaling is a regime‐defining design rule for near‐ideal area‐type operation in oxide memristors, implying a fundamental approach to fabricating robust multi‐state memristors for in‐memory computing applications.

title: Cyclic Nonequilibrium Processing of Halide Solid Electrolytes for Low‐Pressure Operation of all‐Solid‐State Batteries
content:
A cyclic nonequilibrium processing strategy is developed to regulate structural disorder in halide SSEs through repeated quenching. Sequential grain refinement, localized amorphization, and defect modulation simultaneously enhance ionic transport and mechanical compliance, enabling ASSBs to achieve stable operation at a low pressure of 2 MPa with high areal capacity.








ABSTRACT
Sluggish ionic transport and high rigidity of inorganic solid electrolytes (SSEs) necessitate ultra‐high external pressures in all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs), posing a major barrier to their deployment. Herein, we propose a cyclic nonequilibrium thermal process for Li3InCl6 (LIC) solid electrolyte, which is implemented through repeated quenching to concurrently optimize ionic transport and deformability. The initial quench refines particle size, whereas subsequent quenching induces local amorphization, thereby suppressing grain boundary resistance and enhancing compressibility. Meanwhile, additional Li vacancies are introduced, accelerating bulk phase ionic transport. These coupled mesoscopic and microscopic structural evolutions increase the room‐temperature ionic conductivity (IC) of LIC from 1.3 to 6.8 mS/cm, while reducing the Young's modulus from 42.3 to 17.6 GPa. The optimized LIC enables a stable cycling of ASSBs at a low operation pressure of 2 MPa with a high areal capacity of 7.7 mAh/cm2, highlighting cyclic nonequilibrium processing as a promising route for practical ASSBs.

title: Boundary Guided Liquid‐Bridge Adhesion for Robotic Pick‐and‐Release
content:
A composite‐structured stamp with two‐tiered geometry and patterned wettability enables controlled liquid‐bridge formation and retraction. Contact‐line pinning at the tier boundaries confines liquid spreading and guides retraction toward bridge breakup, enabling switchable adhesion without mechanical preload. The stamp supports manipulation of objects with different surface properties and geometries, preserves fragile microstructures during contact, and enables robotic pick‐and‐place operations.








ABSTRACT
Liquid‐bridge‐mediated adhesion provides conformal contact with rough surfaces and gentle interaction with fragile microstructures, making it attractive for object manipulation. However, controlling liquid‐bridge formation and retraction under non‐ideal interfacial conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a switchable liquid‐bridge adhesion strategy using a two‐tiered stamp with spatially patterned wettability. Boundary‐guided pinning confines liquid spreading to form a stable bridge for pickup and guides liquid retraction toward bridge breakup for controlled release. This design converts liquid‐bridge adhesion from an uncontrolled capillary phenomenon into a controllable interfacial mechanism. The strategy enables preload‐free adhesion switching, tunable adhesion forces, robust manipulation across surfaces with diverse roughness and wettability, and damage‐free contact with fragile microstructures. Integrated with a robotic platform, the stamp functions as a liquid‐bridge‐based robotic end effector for pick‐and‐place manipulation and robotic placement, providing a route toward ultra‐gentle manufacturing and microelectronic assembly.

title: Rare‐Earth‐Cluster‐Mediated Long‐Range Electronic Modulation Activates Zn Atomic Sites for Oxygen Reduction Catalysis
content:
Rare‐earth oxide clusters anchored near Zn single atoms remotely tune the electronic structure of the Zn sites, transforming normally inert d10 Zn centers into efficient oxygen‐reduction sites. This long‐range modulation optimizes intermediate adsorption, accelerates charge transfer, and enables high‐performance alkaline oxygen reduction and zinc–air batteries, offering a general strategy for activating non‐precious single‐atom catalysts.








ABSTRACT
Activating the inert Zn (d10) centers via precise ligand‐field engineering to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance is highly appealing yet challenging. Herein, we report a general long‐range electronic structure regulation strategy to construct ultrafine rare‐earth oxide clusters anchored proximal to Zn single‐atom sites (LaOx‐Zn‐SA/CNCl), aiming at boosting ORR activity. Benefiting from the tailored long‐range electronic modulation by LaOx clusters and the hierarchical porous carbon support that maximizes Zn atom utilization, the catalysts exhibit a high half‐wave potential of 0.90 V along with remarkable stability in alkaline media. This represents a non‐precious‐metal, rare‐earth‐based electrocatalyst among the best reported so far. A zinc–air battery (ZAB) integrating LaOx‐Zn‐SA/CNCl as the cathode catalyst delivers a maximum power density of 177.3 mW cm−2 at 225 mA cm−2. Theoretical calculations reveal that the proximal LaOx clusters remotely modulate the electronic structures of Zn sites, enhancing electron‐transfer efficiency by strengthening electronic interactions. With the optimized electronic state of Zn sites, the adsorption of key intermediates is balanced to alleviate the energy barriers of the rate‐determining step. This work provides insights into the long‐range electronic regulation of transition‐metal single‐atom sites within a hierarchical rare‐earth cluster‐coupled microenvironment for efficient electrocatalysis.

title: Graphene Materials With Anomalous Infrared Emissivity Yet Superb Chemical Stability
content:
Surface chemistry engineering and halogen doping transform graphene oxide into a metallic‐like graphene material with suppressed infrared radiation. The low‐defect graphitic framework and ordered multiscale architecture enhance carrier density and electrical conductivity, yielding an ultralow emissivity of 0.15 in the 8–14 µm range while maintaining excellent chemical stability and scalable processability.








ABSTRACT
Low infrared emissivity materials (i.e., metallic materials) are of significance for thermal radiation regulation. However, the easy‐corrosion susceptibility and poor chemical stability are common bottleneck issues that affect their applications. We report a versatile electronic structure modulation strategy for low infrared (IR) emissivity graphene by engineering the surface chemistry of precursor graphene oxide and the followed reduction/doping process. The fabrication protocols minimize the irreparable disruption of the intrinsic graphitic structure and enable controllable assembly of nanosheets by suppressing formation of carboxyl groups. More significantly, the convenient reduction and halogen doping effects synergistically minimize electron scattering and enhance interfacial charge transport. The low‐defective graphitic structure and the ordered multiscale architecture, as well as halogen doping effect, afford exceptional carrier mobility (∼27.1 cm2 V−1s−1), carrier density (5.73 × 1020 cm−3), and electrical conductivity comparable to highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Surprisingly, the anomalous metallic response gives the lowest IR emissivity (0.15, 8–14 µm) for carbon materials, comparable to MXene and traditional metallic materials. The large‐scale processability and outstanding long‐term stability under chemical conditions offer new insights for the potential infrared applications of graphene materials.

title: Ferrocene‐Based Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enable Ultra‐High Specific Detectivity in Perovskite Photodetectors
content:
We report perovskite photodetectors with record specific detectivities exceeding 1013 Jones with a novel molecular design strategy to functionalize self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) with ferrocene (Fc) derivatives. Fc‐SAM‐based devices also exhibit strong operational stability and enable data transmission rates exceeding 1 Mbps in a LiFi system, highlighting their suitability for commercialization.








ABSTRACT
Molecular design of self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) for perovskite photodetector (PD) applications has largely been inherited from photovoltaics, where molecules have been designed to maximize charge extraction rather than to minimize dark current density (Jd). Here, we move beyond conventional carbazole‐core SAMs and introduce ferrocene (Fc)‐based SAMs (Fc‐SAMs) as hole transport layers specifically designed for PD operation. These Fc‐SAMs enable a unique energy alignment strategy where the work function of ITO is modified to misalign with the valence band maximum of an adjacent metal halide perovskite. In doing so, interfacial band bending is reduced, suppressing thermally activated charge injection. Simultaneously, the Fc moiety passivates interfacial defects, lowering defect density two‐fold when compared to a benchmark SAM. These effects enable an ultralow Jd of 2.52 × 10−10 A cm−2 and a noise current of 3.80 × 10−15 A Hz−1/2, which generates a state‐of‐the‐art specific detectivity (D*) of 2.56 × 1013 Jones at 680 nm and −0.5 V. We also establish that Fc‐SAM performance is independent of alkyl chain length (0 ≤ n ≤ 6), contrasting established SAM design rules. Moreover, Fc‐SAM devices exhibit excellent operational stability, supporting LiFi communication rates exceeding 1 Mbps and highlighting their potential for commercial optoelectronic applications.

title: Enhanced Permittivity in Wurtzite ScAlN Through Nanoscale Sc Clustering
content:
In alloy materials, local correlations between the alloying elements can affect material properties. Here, we show that nanoscale Sc clustering in the semiconductor ScAlN can dramatically influence the dielectric permittivity and that the growth conditions influence the degree of Sc clustering. Our results highlight the importance of Sc clustering in ScAlN, with implications for piezoelectric, ferroelectric, and optical devices.








ABSTRACT
ScN alloyed AlN (ScxAl1‐xN, ScAlN, or AlScN) is a wurtzite semiconductor with attractive ferroelectric, dielectric, piezoelectric, and optical properties. Here, using electron ptychography in combination with a suite of experimental and theoretical methods, we show that ScAlN films (with x spanning 0.18 to 0.36) contain nanoscale Sc‐rich clusters which maintain the wurtzite crystal structure. While both molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and sputter deposited Sc0.3Al0.7N films show Sc clustering, the degree of clustering is significantly stronger for the MBE‐grown film, offering an explanation for some of the discrepancies between MBE‐grown and sputtered films reported in the literature. Moreover, the MBE‐grown Sc0.3Al0.7N film exhibits a dispersive and anomalously large dielectric permittivity, roughly double that of sputtered Sc0.3Al0.7N. We attribute this result to the Sc‐rich clusters locally reaching x ∼ 0.5 and approaching the predicted ferroelectric‐to‐paraelectric phase transition, resulting in a giant (local) enhancement in permittivity. The Sc‐rich clusters should similarly affect the piezoelectric, optical, and ferroelectric responses, suggesting cluster‐engineering as a means to tailor ScAlN's functional properties.

title: Nanocavity Confining Platinum Nanoclusters Enhances Photocatalytic Two‐Electron Oxygen Reduction for Wound Healing
content:
By facilitating efficient Pauling‐type O2 adsorption and enhancing 2e− ORR selectivity, engineered nanocavity‐confined Pt nanoclusters markedly improve the selectivity to 86% and formation kinetics of 3.12 × 10−3 mol L−1 h−1) of photocatalytic H2O2 production, and thereby deliver outstanding bactericidal performance and promote effective wound healing.








ABSTRACT
Photocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) toward H2O2 synthesis is a compelling approach for clinical antibacterial applications. Yet its selectivity is hampered by the competing four‐electron ORR, which compromises both H2O2 generation kinetics and antibacterial efficiency. Herein, we report a new nanoscale confinement strategy for the controllable synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) confining isolated platinum nanoclusters (NCs) to enhance Pauling‐type of O2 adsorption to achieve two‐electron oxygen reduction for efficient antibacterial therapy. The resulting Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt NCs exhibits a significantly higher H2O2 formation kinetics (3.12 × 10−3 mol L−1 h−1) than Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt nanoparticles (1.55 × 10−3 mol L−1 h−1), with 2e− ORR selectivity increased from 45.0% to 86.0%. Experimental and theoretical results reveal a two‐step single electron oxygen reduction pathway for H2O2 photosynthesis over Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt NCs. The Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt NCs exhibits excellent sterilization efficiencies of 5.0 log10CFU mL−1 and 5.2 log10CFU mL−1 against S. aureus and E. coli, respectively, exceeding most reported materials. Furthermore, Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt NCs facilitate the regeneration of infectious wounds, with the efficiency of nearly 100% on day 10, outperforming previously reported bionanomaterials. Collectively, this work presents a new strategy for regulating the Pauling‐type of O2 adsorption to enhance the photocatalytic H2O2 formation for wound healing application.

title: Time‐Resolved Physically Unclonable Functions Enabled by Solvent‐Free Scalable Boron‐Based Ultralong Phosphorescent Systems for Machine‐Learning‐Resilient Optical Encryption
content:
A time‐resolved physically unclonable function (TR‐PUF) is enabled by kilogram‐scale, solvent‐free synthesized boron‐based room‐temperature phosphorescent materials, transforming static optical security into high‐dimensional temporal encoding. Structurally isolated emissive units generate independent decay channels for dual spectral–temporal entropy, while a time‐gated artificial intelligence framework enables rapid and reliable authentication, offering a scalable route toward dynamic, machine‐learning‐resistant anti‐counterfeiting systems.








ABSTRACT
Anti‐counterfeiting technologies are increasingly challenged by advances in imaging and machine learning, exposing the fundamental limitations of conventional static optical security systems. Here, a time‐resolved physically unclonable function (TR‐PUF) system is established, transforming optical authentication from static pattern recognition to high‐dimensional temporal encoding. Central to this approach, boron‐based room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) materials are developed via covalent coupling with coumarin derivatives using a solvent‐free strategy that is readily scalable to kilogram‐level production, exhibiting a maximum phosphorescence lifetime of over 2 s, an ultralong afterglow visible for up to 30 s, and color‐tunable emission. The formation of rigid B‐O‐C linkages spatially isolates emissive centers, suppressing energy transfer and preserving temporally independent decay channels–an essential prerequisite for high‐entropy time‐resolved encoding. Randomly embedding these multi‐emissive RTP units into a polymer matrix forms a complex encryption structure that enables a dual‐entropy encoding mechanism with both spectral and temporal dimensions, generating dynamic time keys for authentication. Moreover, we propose a matched time‐gated authentication framework that achieves >99% identification accuracy within 1.2 s while exhibiting resistance against the tested generative machine‐learning attacks. This work proposes a practical materials platform and a time‐gated authentication strategy, offering a scalable technological path for the development of dynamic optical encryption tags.

title: Unlocking the Interfacial Activity of Insoluble Lithium Salts for Stable Lithium Batteries
content:
An immobilized functional platform deploys insoluble Li2SO4 (IFP‐LS) on an aramid‐scaffolded separator to bypass dissolution–diffusion limitations. Lewis‐acidic Li+ sites regulate the interfacial Li+ solvation environment and promote PF6−‐derived LiF‐rich SEI formation. Li2SO4 also provides a finite sacrificial lithium contribution. The IFP‐LS enables exceptional cycling durability and roll‐to‐roll manufacturing at an added cost of only 0.163 USD m−2.








ABSTRACT
Employing functional lithium salts in electrolytes is an effective strategy to suppress anode instabilities and sluggish charge‐transfer kinetics in lithium batteries. However, high solubility requirements intrinsically exclude a broad class of promising, high‐lattice‐energy inorganic salts for carbonate electrolytes. Here, we establish an immobilized functional platform (IFP) by deploying insoluble lithium salts with strong Lewis‐acidic Li+ sites directly onto an aramid‐scaffolded separator. This design bypasses conventional dissolution–diffusion limitations, yielding a thin, ionically conductive, LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) driven by regulated interfacial Li+ solvation and enhanced anion‐derived decomposition. Systematic screening and 6Li/7Li isotope tracing identify Li2SO4 (LS) as the optimal IFP candidate (IFP‐LS) owing to its moderate Lewis acidity, superior solvent affinity, and industrial viability. Remarkably, LS provides a finite sacrificial lithium contribution during continuous SEI evolution, mitigating irreversible lithium consumption. Consequently, IFP‐LS separators quadruple the lifespan of Li||LiNi0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O2 cells at 0.7 C compared to bare separators, and deliver 88.4% capacity retention over 2400 cycles in Li||LiFePO4 cells at 5 C. Scalability is further validated through 100 m roll‐to‐roll manufacturing across diverse Ah‐level formats, adding only 0.163 USD m−2. This work overcomes the lithium salt solubility barrier and unlocks a vast library of potent materials for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries.

title: Dynamic Molecular Engineering Occluder for Spatiotemporally Adaptable Complex Tissue Repair
content:
A spatiotemporally adaptive, cell‐free occluder integrates dynamic covalent and non‐covalent networks across a multilayer architecture to meet the changing demands of tracheal fistula healing. Immediate airtight sealing and mechanical rescue are coupled with antibacterial protection, fibrosis‐free tissue integration, and native‐like epithelial regeneration, revealing dynamic chemistry as a temporal design principle for complex tissue repair.








ABSTRACT
Tracheal fistula is a life‐threatening disorder for which no current therapy can simultaneously provide immediate airway rescue and long‐term functional regeneration. Here we report a completely biodegradable, cell‐free, off‐the‐shelf therapeutic construct that enables spatiotemporally matched repair by dynamically adapting to the evolving physiological demands of healing. The system integrates dynamic covalent and non‐covalent interactions with distinct response timescales across spatially stratified layers, thereby supporting acute functional substitution, intermediate regenerative integration, and late‐stage tissue replacement within a single intervention. In rabbit models, the construct achieved immediate airtight sealing and restoration of ventilation, improved survival from 0% to 100%, and enabled native‐like tracheal regeneration with ciliated epithelium. In head‐to‐head comparisons, it outperformed both clinical flap repair and tissue‐engineered graft repair in functional epithelial reconstruction. In a goat model, it maintained airway patency under human‐scale physiological conditions. These findings establish a clinically relevant strategy for tracheal fistula repair and show that dynamically adaptive materials can bridge the gap between acute intervention and functional regeneration.

title: Hierarchical Triboelectric‐Plasmonic‐Coupled All‐Fabric Dual‐Mode Platform for Self‐Powered Respiratory Monitoring and Electrostatic‐Driven In Situ Pseudovirus Detection
content:
A hierarchical all‐fabric triboelectric‐plasmonic platform integrates self‐powered respiratory monitoring with electrostatic‐field‐assisted molecular enrichment and SERS detection. The engineered bilayer silver textile simultaneously serves as a triboelectric electrode and plasmonic interface, enabling a cooperative “monitor‐enrich‐detect” strategy for sensitive, in situ identification of respiratory pathogens and providing a wearable route toward autonomous respiratory health surveillance.








ABSTRACT
Respiratory infectious diseases represented by COVID‐19 necessitate proactive wearable diagnostic platforms with high integration and sensitivity. In this study, we present a hierarchical, all‐fabric dual‐mode sensor seamlessly integrating a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) for self‐powered physiological pre‐alert and a surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrate for biochemical verification. The core innovation is a rationally engineered bilayer silver (Ag) fabric via secondary Ag plating (Ag nanoparticles: ∼16 nm bottom, ∼92 nm top), forming abundant plasmonic “hot spots” and enabling SERS detection with an LOD down to 10−16 M. Meanwhile, the same fabric serves as a robust TENG electrode paired with high‐β‐phase PVDF nanofibers (∼70% β‐phase), enabling a power density of 461.28 mW m−2 and real‐time respiratory monitoring within < 0.02 s, with the results visualized on a self‐developed mobile APP for on‐site use. Moreover, TENG‐driven field‐assisted enrichment promotes the accumulation of negatively charged viral particles near the sensing surface, while the hierarchical Ag architecture provides abundant SERS‐active interfaces for virus‐substrate interactions, jointly facilitating in situ SERS detection down to 5 × 103 TU mL−1 for SARS‐CoV‐2 pseudovirus. The smart mask prototype also demonstrates > 99.4% antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. This “monitor‐enrich‐detect” triboelectric‐plasmonic‐coupled platform holds promise for early warning and risk mitigation of respiratory infectious disease transmission.

title: Heterogeneous Electric Double Layer with Ion‐Transport Pathways for Practical Zinc‐Ion Batteries
content:
Via cation‐anion coordination, a heterogeneous electric double layer (EDL) featuring dual‐nanodomains: apolar nanodomains thermodynamically suppress H2O‐induced side reactions, while interconnected polar nanodomains kinetically accelerate Zn2+ transport.








ABSTRACT
Manipulating the electric double layer (EDL) structure at nanoscale remains largely underexplored yet extremely challenging for practical Ah‐level aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, we construct a heterogeneous nanostructured EDL with intrinsic ion‐transport pathways via cation‐anion coordination strategy, which synergistically enhances the thermodynamic stability and kinetic reversibility of the Zn anode. In‐situ characterizations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the long‐chain ionic additive triggers the interfacial ion rearrangement and assembly within the EDL, where hydrophobic carbon chains self‐aggregate into dense apolar nanodomains, and cationic groups electrostatically attract anions and co‐assemble to form interconnected polar nanodomains. This uniquely heterogeneous EDL thermodynamically confines H2O activity and efficiently inhibits side reactions. Meanwhile, the interconnected polar ion‐transport pathways accelerate Zn2+ migration and desolvation kinetics, achieving an ultrahigh Zn2+ transference number (0.89) and dendrite‐free Zn deposition. Consequently, Zn//Zn cell delivers stable cycling over 1,200 h (25 mA cm−2, 12.5 mAh cm−2) and Zn//NVO full cell retains 100% capacity after 30,000 cycles at 5 A g−1. Furthermore, 0.2‐Ah and 1.1‐Ah pouch cells exhibit stable operation for 2,500 and 257 cycles, respectively. This work establishes a new paradigm for EDL nanostructure engineering, advancing practical AZIBs.

title: Low‐Temperature‐Induced Interfacial Transformation of the Aluminum Anode in Alkaline Electrolyte
content:
In situ EIS coupled with DRT identifies a sharp polarization rise at 5°C–0 °C for Al anodes. The origin is a low‐temperature interfacial restructuring‐induced impedance, where the interfacial composition shifts from an Al(OH)3/Al(OH)4−‐rich layer to a highly disordered Al2O3‐rich network, revealing a structural and compositional change of the interface.








ABSTRACT
The severe polarization of aluminum (Al) anodes in alkaline electrolytes at low temperatures remains a critical barrier to the commercialization of aqueous Al batteries, yet the interfacial origin of this impedance surge is not fully understood. Herein, we employ in situ dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) coupled with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis to identify a characteristic inflection point in the behavior of a pure Al anode in 4 m NaOH within the 5°C–0°C range. Below this threshold, a new relaxation process emerges at short time constants in the DRT spectrum, and its polarization contribution intensifies significantly with further cooling. We attribute this process to the low‐temperature‐induced formation of an interfacial highly disordered Al2O3‐rich layer, as confirmed by spectroscopic and computational analyses. We therefore propose an ‘impedance induced by interfacial restructuring at low temperatures’ model, wherein performance degradation arises primarily from interfacial structural and compositional evolution rather than from the conventionally assumed decrease in electrolyte conductivity. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for engineering low‐temperature‐adaptable Al anodes via interfacial design.

title: Pre‐Intercalated Cation Optimizing Proton Topochemistry for High‐Performance Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
content:
The ionic‐dipole interaction between pre‐intercalated K+ and lattice water induces the formation of a continuous hydrogen‐bonded network in K0.5V6O13, achieving ultrafast proton transport. Benefiting from the optimization of proton topochemistry, the capacity, rate performance, and cycling stability of KVO elevate significantly; the KVO||Zn pouch cell with 19.2 mg cm−2 high mass loading can cycle stably over 300 cycles at 0.5 A g−1.








ABSTRACT
Cation pre‐intercalated oxides have been widely explored as cathode materials for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs). Although the influence of intercalants on the material structure and Zn2+ storage capacity has been adequately studied, an in‐depth understanding of the influence of intercalants on proton storage is still lacking. Especially, proton transport exhibits ultrafast kinetics as an ideal charge carrier, playing a crucial role in the performance of AZIBs. We show that pre‐intercalated K+ in K0.5V6O13 (KVO) not only reinforces the [VO] framework but also optimizes the hydrogen‐bonded network composed of confined lattice water, achieving ultrafast proton transport. Benefiting from the optimization of proton topochemistry, the capacity, rate performance, and cycling stability of KVO improve significantly. KVO delivers a high reversible capacity of 462.9 mAh g−1 at 0.2 A g−1 and 82.3% retention after 20000 cycles at 20 A g−1. Even with the high mass loading of 19.2 mg cm−2, a KVO||Zn pouch cell with 539.2 mAh capacity can achieve stable cycling for more than 300 cycles at 0.5 A g−1. This work provides new insights into how pre‐intercalated cations affect the proton topochemistry and electrochemical performance of inorganic cathodes.

title: A Universal Spin‐Polarization‐Engineered Antibonding‐Orbital Modulation Paradigm for Accelerating Reaction Kinetics in Ultrahigh‐Rate Sodium‐Ion Batteries
content:
A universal spin‐polarization‐engineered antibonding‐orbital modulation strategy intrinsically regulates robust Fe/Co─S bonds in FeS2/CoS2 heterojunctions. Magnetic Mn doping induces Fe/Co spin‐state transition and increases antibonding‐orbital occupation, thereby accelerating conversion kinetics. The engineered anode delivers ultrahigh‐rate sodium storage and exceptional long‐term cycling stability.








ABSTRACT
Conversion‐type anode materials hold great promise for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass‐transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal–chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long‐standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin‐polarization‐engineered (SPE) antibonding‐orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh‐rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin‐state transition from low‐spin to high‐spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal eg orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin‐engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn‐FeS2/CoS2 anode delivers an ultrahigh‐rate capability of 300 mA h g−1 at 120 A g−1, together with exceptional long‐term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g−1), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial‐level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.

title: Successive Redox Mediation Supported by Pnictogen Chalcohalide Enables High‐Performance Zinc–Sulfur Batteries
content:
Sulfur cathodes offer high capacity but suffer sluggish kinetics and severe side reactions. We show that pnictogen chalcohalide nanorods with a trace iodide additive creates a stepwise dual‐mediation cascade (I0/I−, Bi3+/Bi0, S0/S2−) with gradient potentials accelerating sulfur redox kinetics. This enables the zinc–sulfur pouch cells with 70.1% capacity retention after 250 cycles at 0.8 mA cm−2.








ABSTRACT
Sulfur is a promising high‐capacity cathode but suffers from sluggish redox kinetics and severe side reactions in aqueous electrolytes. We introduce pnictogen chalcohalide Bi12.67S18Br2 nanorods (abbreviated as Bi‐S‐Br) as a multifunctional cathode material that functions as a sulfur/bismuth reservoir and a catalytic redox mediator (RM). By integrating a trace amount of iodide electrolyte additive, we demonstrate a potential pathway, featuring several redox couples with gradient potentials: I0/I− (0.530 V, RM1) > Bi3+/Bi0 (0.308 V, RM2) > S0/S2− (0.144 V vs. standard hydrogen electrode), whose stepwise dual mediation accelerates sulfur redox kinetics. The sulfurphilic Bi‐S‐Br nanorods also strengthen surface Bi–S interfacial interactions, thus localizing active species and suppressing sulfur disproportionation. As a result, Zn||Bi‐S‐Br cells exhibit synergistic discharge plateaus at 0.66 and 0.59 V and deliver a high specific capacity of 792 mAh gBi‐S‐Br−1 at 0.4 A g−1, with an energy density of 488.2 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 244.1 W kg−1, normalized to the Bi‐S‐Br mass. The practical Zn||Bi‐S‐Br pouch cell configuration sustains 250 cycles at 0.8 mA cm−2 with capacity retention of 70.1%. This study elucidated the successive redox mediation strategy for enhanced sulfur redox kinetics, offering a new design principle for high‐performance aqueous energy storage systems.

title: Dual‐Encrypted Ultraviolet Optical Communication Driven by Opto‐Piezoelectric Coupling in Two‐Dimensional Flexible Ferroelectric Single‐Crystalline Thin‐Films
content:
A dual‐encrypted ultraviolet optical communication system is realized with BA2EA2Pb3Br10 ferroelectric single‐crystalline thin‐films. Tensile strain substantially enhances photoresponsivity. Strain‐ratio keys derived from diverse bending states act as intrinsic hardware secrets for 4‐bit coding, achieving secure information transmission and broadening optoelectronic applications of two‐dimensional ferroelectrics.








ABSTRACT
The rapid development of flexible wearable electronics has triggered an urgent demand for high‐security and miniaturized encrypted optical communication systems. However, conventional optical encryption strategies predominantly rely on dual‐wavelength excitation, tunable light sources, or software‐based algorithms, leading to bulky configurations and vulnerable hardware‐level security. Herein, we report a dual‐encrypted ultraviolet optical communication system based on BA2EA2Pb3Br10 (1, where BA is n‐butylamine and EA is ethylamine) ferroelectric single‐crystalline thin‐films (SCFs). The 1 ferroelectric SCFs show a photoresponsivity that reaches 230% of the original level under +1.13% tensile strain. Notably, we innovatively define the strain‐ratio key (ε1/ε2, ε2/ε3, ε3/ε4) induced by distinct bending states as the intrinsic unclonable hardware secret key, and construct a 4‐bit combined coding scheme based on four distinguishable photocurrent levels modulated by these strain ratios to realize secure transmission of the message “FJIRSM.” This strain ratio‐based system avoids complex optical modulation, ensuring ultrahigh security, and expands the application of two‐dimensional ferroelectrics in advanced encrypted optoelectronics.

title: Iron‐Induced Interfacial Electronic Asymmetry Steers Pathway Divergence in Cobalt‐Centered Fenton‐Like Catalysis
content:
Interfacial Fe regulation at the Fe─O─Co interface switches and tunes Co‐centered Fenton‐like pathway competition, yielding a sulfate‐radical‐enriched yet nonradical‐retaining regime for deeper mineralization and improved oxidant utilization.








ABSTRACT
Deep mineralization and matrix tolerance are difficult to reconcile in advanced oxidation processes because radical and nonradical pathways are often coupled in a composition‐defined paradigm. Although multimetal materials can catalyze both pathways, the parallel reactions typically occur at different active sites, and their relative contributions are often governed by catalyst composition and active‐site distribution, making deliberate regulation of pathway competition difficult. Here, we propose a multimetal catalyst with an electronically asymmetric Fe─O─Co interface to enable pathway divergence within a Co‐centered catalytic environment. Fe introduction into CoNi layered hydroxides leads to electron density redistribution at neighboring Co sites and shifts PMS activation from a high‐valent CoIV═O‐biased route toward a sulfate‐radical‐enriched regime while retaining complementary nonradical oxidation. The optimized catalyst achieved 1.43‐fold greater TOC removal and a 1.47‐fold higher PMS utilization efficiency (PUE) for norfloxacin (NOR) degradation than the Fe‐free control, with robust decontamination performance against common background matrix interference and sustained activity over 96 h of high‐flux continuous‐flow operation. This work establishes interfacial Fe regulation as a pathway‐engineering strategy for steering oxidant‐activation selectivity through heterometal‐induced electronic asymmetry, providing a route to reconcile mineralization depth with matrix tolerance in Fenton‐like water treatment.

title: Regulated Co‐Solvation in Gel Polymer Electrolyte Enables Rapid and Selective Li+ Ion Transport for High‐Rate Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
A molecularly engineered dual‐regulated weak‐coordination gel polymer electrolyte with matched polymer–solvent co‐solvation of Li+ and anion‐binding capability is developed to enable stable cycling of high‐rate lithium metal batteries at room temperature.








ABSTRACT
The development of gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) suitable for high‐rate lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is urgently needed but remains inherently challenging. This difficulty originates from the competition between the polymer network and the liquid electrolyte for lithium ion (Li+) coordination. Polymer‐dominated coordination traps Li+ and slows transport, while solvent‐dominated solvation permits uncontrolled anion migration and causes concentration polarization. Here, we resolve this challenge by establishing a matched polymer–electrolyte co‐solvation state, which enables rapid and selective Li+ transport via a cooperative mechanism. We implement this concept through a dual‐regulated weak‐coordination gel polymer electrolyte (DWGPE), which comprises a fluorinated polymer backbone that attenuates Li+ binding, an amide‐functionalized crosslinker that immobilizes anions via hydrogen bonding, and a weakly solvating adiponitrile‐based liquid phase. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a cooperative transport mechanism that integrates polymer‐assisted hopping and solvent‐mediated vehicular diffusion, while suppressing anion mobility. Consequently, Li||DWGPE||LFP coin cells sustain 10 000 cycles at 6 C with 65% capacity retention, corresponding to an ultralow capacity decay of 0.003% per cycle. Our DWGPE also operates stably with high‐voltage NCM811 cathodes and in ampere‐hour‐level pouch cells. This work establishes polymer–electrolyte co‐solvation as a design framework for high‐performance GPEs toward fast‐charging LMBs.

title: Silicate Biomaterials‐Stimulated Vascularized Callus Organoids for Bone Tissue Regeneration
content:
A microfluidic‐assisted magnesium silicate‐engineered composite hydrogel was developed for vascularized callus organoid engineering. Magnesium silicate nanotube‐engineered composite hydrogel offered a favorable mechanical microenvironment for callus organoids, thereby activating the mechanotransduction‐related pathway for promoting the development of organoids, representing a promising therapeutic approach for vascularized bone repair.









ABSTRACT
Organoids that recapitulate native fracture callus can form spontaneous ossification centers within a bone defect, offering substantial promise for rapid bone regeneration. However, existing callus organoids generally lack a functional vascular network and an appropriate mechanical microenvironment, and their production limits scalability and uniformity. Here, we established a droplet‐based microfluidic platform for the high‐throughput generation of morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate‐engineered composite hydrogel microspheres, enabling the uniform construction of vascularized callus organoids. Importantly, morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate could regulate both the bulk mechanical performance and internal stress distribution of the composite hydrogels. In vitro, callus organoids modulated by magnesium silicate nanotubes significantly promoted chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, developed a stable endothelial network and mineralized structure. Furthermore, magnesium silicate nanotube‐engineered composite hydrogel (2NT‐GM) offered a favorable mechanical microenvironment for callus organoids, thereby activating the mechanotransduction‐related pathway for promoting the development of organoids. In a rat femoral condyle critical‐sized defect model, the vascularized callus organoids regulated by 2NT‐GM were further found to significantly promote vascular network formation, and facilitate bone regeneration at the bone defect center within 6 weeks of implantation. Together, this study suggests a promising strategy for bone tissue regeneration by developing vascularized callus organoids with the stimulation of inorganic silicate biomaterials.

title: Harnessing the Bacterial Membrane‐Derived Oral Vaccine to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity and Metabolic Control of T Cells
content:
A select B. bifidum‐derived oral vaccine effectively primes dendritic cell maturation and cooperates with anti‐PD1 therapy to evoke antitumor immune responses, significantly restraining in vivo tumor growth. Notably, this strategy leads to elevated secretion of microbiota‐driven metabolites, particularly tryptophan metabolite indole‐3‐acetic‐acid, thus potentiating the IFN‐γ+ T cell immunity and the cytotoxic T cell effector function with ICI therapy.








ABSTRACT
The fluctuating gastrointestinal milieu and its restrictive epithelial barrier represent critical challenges for the design of oral cancer vaccines. Nevertheless, leveraging the gut microbiome as an interventional strategy has recently gained traction, especially in patients on immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, microbial‐derived double‐layered membrane vesicles are developed as adjuvants and cell‐free carriers, fused with cell‐penetrating peptide‐modified antigens, and encapsulated in an alginate/chitosan‐microsystem to engineer oral vaccines. This design strategically harnesses the crosstalk between the gut microbiome and gut‐associated lymphoid tissues, driving dendritic cell maturation, plasma cell activation, and production of immune‐stimulatory cytokines within the mesenteric lymph nodes and lamina propria. In mouse prophylactic and therapeutic tumor models, the select Bifidobacterium bifidum‐derived oral vaccine combined with anti‐PD1 treatment enhances cytotoxic antitumor responses, along with Th1‐, Th17‐immunity, leading to potent tumor suppression, prolonged survival, and long‐term protection against tumor rechallenge. Mechanistically, the vaccine promotes interferon‐γ‐producing T cells and antitumor efficacy with ICI therapy via the improved microbiota diversity and signaling metabolites, with an indole‐3‐acetic‐acid (3IAA) enriched diet profoundly shaping T‐cell recruitment and differentiation. Our findings uncover a tryptophan metabolite‐driven immune axis that amplifies the specific antitumor immune response, redefining oral vaccines as a powerful tool for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Identifying a Figure of Merit for Solvent Optimization in Non‐Fullerene Organic Solar Cells via High‐Throughput Experiments
content:
Traditional solvent optimization in organic solar cells relies on device fabrication and performance evaluation. High‐throughput experiments combined with machine learning analysis identify a figure of merit for solvent optimization, thereby enabling rapid ranking of processing solvents prior to device fabrication and providing an efficient route toward accelerated solvent optimization.








ABSTRACT
Solvent optimization in organic solar cells (OSCs) remains largely empirical, requiring repeated device fabrication and characterization across a broad formulation space. Here, we introduce a high‐throughput workflow to decipher a figure of merit (FoM) for solvent optimization of non‐fullerene acceptor (NFA)‐based OSCs. Using D18:L8BO as a representative system, we prepare a diverse solvent formulation via high‐throughput experimentation and in situ optical characterization during film formation. Machine learning analysis unveils the initial donor‐to‐acceptor absorption ratio during deposition (I_D/A) as a key FoM, which enables the efficient optimization of solvents in OSCs. Comprehensive characterization identifies the photophysical and morphological properties associated with the optimized formulation. Evaluation across several polymer:Y‐series NFA systems further supports I_D/A as a FoM for solvent optimization. This study establishes an experimentally accessible strategy that integrates the exploration of broad solvent formulation spaces with targeted device validation into a targeted, data‐driven workflow, offering a practical route for accelerating OSC development.

title: Layered Spin‐Crossover Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Light‐Induced Control of Two‐Dimensional Quantum Materials
content:
Spin‐crossover metal‐organic frameworks (SCO‐MOFs) provide a route to control the electronic and magnetic properties of two‐dimensional quantum materials. By integrating a layered SCO‐MOFs with graphene, CrSBr, and NbSe2 nanodevices, thermally and light induced spin transitions induce strain that reversibly modulates charge transport, magnetic memory and superconducting behavior, opening new opportunities for MOF‐based electronic and spintronic heterostructures beyond conventional porous‐material applications.








ABSTRACT
Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored for gas separation, catalysis, or energy storage, yet their integration with other electronically functional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we integrate the layered Hofmann‐type spin‐crossover (SCO) MOF {FeII(pyS2Et)2[PtII(CN)4]} into electrical nanodevices to control the properties of two‐dimensional (2D) quantum materials. Our molecular approach exploits the stimuli‐responsive nature of SCO‐layered materials as switchable building blocks. We demonstrate selective modulation of the electronic transport in van der Waals heterostructures interfacing SCO with 2D quantum materials (few‐layer graphene, magnetic CrSBr, superconducting NbSe2) through the strain induced via thermal and light‐induced spin transitions. In graphene, the conductivity is selectively switched by light. In spin‐valves based on CrSBr bilayers, the MOF triggers magnetic hysteresis (absent in pristine CrSBr) and enables tunable non‐volatile zero‐field memory. In NbSe2, light modulates the superconducting critical current and transition temperature. These results establish layered stimuli‐responsive SCO MOFs as active molecular control elements for 2D quantum materials, providing a route to strain‐mediated control of electronic, magnetic, and superconducting functionalities, and extending MOF‐based architectures beyond traditional porous‐matter applications toward multifunctional electronics and spintronics.

title: Vacancy‐Associated La–Ir Pairs Enable Water‐Derived Oxygen‐Hydroxyl Coupling for Durable Low‐Ir PEM Water Electrolysis
content:
An Ir,La‐MCOδ catalyst featuring Laoct‐Iroct units with adjacent bridging and Ir z‐axis oxygen vacancies was developed, achieving over 1550 h of PEM water electrolysis at 1 A cm−2 with an ultralow Ir loading of only 0.12 mg cm−2. The mechanistic origin of the durable catalytic activity of Ir,La‐MCOδ was investigated, further revealing an oxygen‐vacancy‐mediated water‐derived oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling mechanism.








ABSTRACT
Developing highly stable, low‐iridium catalysts is critical for acidic oxygen evolution, but is limited by structural degradation driven by acid corrosion and voltage polarization. Herein, we report an iridium and lanthanum co‐doped manganese‐cobalt spinel catalyst, Ir,La‐MCOδ, featuring octahedral La–Ir pairs (Laoct–Iroct) with a theoretical favorable configuration of adjacent bridging and Ir z‐axis oxygen vacancies. This low‐Ir catalyst Ir,La‐MCOδ (0.12 mg Ir cm−2) exhibits an overpotential of merely 220 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in pH = 1 electrolyte, and demonstrates robust operation for over 1550 h at 1 A cm−2 in a proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer. Coupled (quasi)in situ characterizations and operando spectroscopy reveal that the adjacent oxygen vacancies mediate the evolution of oxygen intermediates, enabling water‐derived oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling with negligible lattice oxygen involvement, via a decoupled proton–electron transfer pathway. This mechanism preserves the structural integrity of the catalyst and yields a calculated reaction free‐energy change of merely 0.38 eV (U = 1.23 V) for the most unfavorable oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling elementary step, thereby endowing Ir,La‐MCOδ with exceptional durability. This work provides a valuable mechanistic insight into designing highly stable defective catalysts.

title: Sustained‐Release Regulation on FAPbI3 Crystallization to Enhance Photo‐Thermal Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
FAPbI3 crystallization kinetics is regulated by introducing oligomeric PEI homogenizing the PbI2 scaffold while oligomeric PEGDE slowing down FAI release. In situ polymerization PEI/PEGDE 3D network could passivate grain‐boundary and form an inner encapsulation. Resulting n‐i‐p devices enable 26.6% efficiency (26.2% certified efficiency), 92% and 96% retention of original efficiencies over 1,100 h 85°C thermal and MPPT stabilities, respectively.








ABSTRACT
Controlling crystallization kinetics of FAPbI3 perovskite is crucial for improving crystal quality, device performance and stability. Herein, we report a sustained‐release strategy to regulate the PbI2‐to‐FAPbI3 conversion. PbI2 lattice expansion arising from the interaction between PEI (oligomeric poly(ethyleneimine)) and iodide species suppresses nonuniform PbI2 crystallization and facilitates FAI infiltration. Moreover, the weak interaction between oligomeric PEGDE (poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether) and FAI slows the reaction between FAI and PbI2, leading to homogeneous phase conversion during annealing. Consequently, enlarged FAPbI3 grains are obtained with improved crystallographic orientation, reduced strain and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Furthermore, released PEI and PEGDE undergo in situ crosslinking to form a three‐dimensional network that passivates grain boundaries, stabilizes microstructure and affords inner encapsulation. The resulting champion n‐i‐p device presents a power conversion efficiency of 26.6% (certified 26.17%). Both films and devices exhibit enhanced photothermal stability. The PEI/PEGDE‐treated device maintains 92% of its initial efficiency at 85 °C for over 1,100 h, 96% after continuous illumination (∼100 mW cm−2) and maximum‐power‐point (MPP) tracking for over 1,500 h, and 89% after MPP tracking at 85 °C over 12 days. This work offers a polymerization‐assisted route for synchronizing crystallization control, defect passivation and inner encapsulation to enhance perovskite solar‐cell stability.

title: Strain‐Controlled Pt Single‐Atom Catalysts on Crumpled MXene Supports for Highly Active Hydrogen Evolution
content:
Crumpling turns MXene strain into a powerful regulator of hydrogen spillover around isolated Pt atoms. Strain‐mediated interfacial water restructuring promotes H2O dissociation at Mo sites and directs hydrogen transfer through a Mo‐O‐Pt bridge toward Pt sites. Exceptional Pt mass activity and stable ampere‐level electrolysis reveal a scalable route to strain‐engineered electrocatalysis.








ABSTRACT
Strain engineering offers a powerful means to regulate the electronic structure and catalytic behavior of active metal sites, yet a general framework linking strain to electrocatalytic performance remains elusive beyond the conventional d‐band model. Here we report crumpled double‐transition‐metal MXene nanosheets (Mo2TiC2Tx) decorated with Pt single atoms, in which a tunable strain field is introduced through a physical diaphragm balloon method. The resulting cMo2TiC2Tx‐PtSA catalyst exhibits outstanding alkaline hydrogen evolution performance, requiring overpotentials of only 24.9 and 75.5 mV to reach 10 and 50 mA cm−2, respectively, together with a mass activity of 11 859 mA mgPt−1, around 178‐fold higher than commercial Pt/C, a Tafel slope of 31.61 mV dec−1 and excellent durability. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that the ordered long‐range strain field around isolated Pt sites accelerates interfacial water activation while preserving near‐optimal H adsorption, thereby facilitating H2 release. The resulting catalyst delivered a high current density of 3 A cm−2 at a low voltage of 1.98 V and maintained stable operation at 1000 mA cm−2 for over 500 h. These performance metrics underscore the potential of cMo2TiC2Tx‐PtSA for industrial applications.
