title: Artificial Regulatory T Cells Orchestrate Phase‐Spanning Regeneration in Refractory Tissue Injuries
content:
Refractory tissue injuries exhibit impaired phase transitions that conventional exosome delivery remains limited in addressing due to rapid loss of vesicle integrity and bioactivity. We engineer artificial regulatory T cells (ATregs) that reconstruct a multivesicular‐body‐inspired protective storage architecture. Through spatial compartmentalization and interfacial regulation, ATregs preserve exosome integrity and enable sustained release, orchestrating sequential signaling from inflammation resolution to angiogenesis and tissue remodeling, ultimately enabling coordinated, phase‐spanning regeneration.








ABSTRACT
Regulatory T cells (Tregs) possess potent multiphasic reparative capacity; however, their application is limited by ethical and regulatory challenges associated with live cell therapies. Treg‐derived exosomes (TExo) exhibit low immunogenicity while enriching regenerative signaling relative to parental Tregs. Current exosome carriers place greater emphasis on sustained release than on factors affecting vesicle stability, such as nonspecific interactions and confinement effects. Inspired by the multivesicular body (MVB), we engineered artificial Tregs (ATregs) with an MVB‐like architecture that integrates vesicle protection with sustained release through a reconstructed storage microenvironment. This design enables phase‐aligned TExo release and extends functional activity by more than an order of magnitude compared with free TExo. ATregs sequentially coordinate the suppression of inflammation, enhancement of angiogenesis, and stimulation of skin appendage regeneration. In diabetic wounds and deep second‐degree burn models, which represent intrinsic repair dysfunction and severe structural tissue loss, ATregs markedly accelerate healing and outperform conventional strategies across murine and porcine models. These findings overcome the key limitations of exosome therapies and open a new avenue for next‐generation regenerative therapeutics.

title: Spatially Decoupled Cascade Oxygen Reduction on Bi Single‐Atom and Cluster‐Hybrid Sites for Hydroxyl Radical Generation
content:
A Bi single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid spatially decouples a two‐step ORR cascade, breaking the linear‐scaling constraint that limits single‐site catalysts. H2O2 is generated at single‐atom sites and relayed to neighboring clusters for activation to ·OH, with the hybrid interface thermodynamically ensuring selectivity and photoelectrocatalysis (PEC) kinetically accelerating the relay. This delivers 250 µM h−1 ·OH at neutral pH, with high activity retained across pH 3–9, and establishes single‐atom and cluster hybridization as a general strategy for decoupling cascade reactions.








ABSTRACT
The two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) for H2O2 production and the subsequent in situ activation to ·OH are constrained by linear scaling relationships, making it difficult for a single active site to simultaneously optimize O2 activation and H2O2 conversion. This work overcomes the trade‐off by spatially decoupling the cascade reaction onto single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid sites and employing photoelectrocatalysis (PEC). Through a ligand‐exchange and pyrolysis route derived from a metal–organic framework precursor, Bi single atoms and clusters are co‐anchored on B‐doped TiO2. The hybrid interface thermodynamically optimizes the intermediate adsorption energies to ensure cascade selectivity, whereas PEC kinetically accelerates the H2O2‐to‐·OH conversion by supplying photogenerated electrons. Density functional theory and free‐energy diagrams indicate that H2O2 forms at the single atoms and dissociates into ·OH at the clusters, with the relationship between the p‐band center and ·OH yield following the Sabatier principle. The catalyst delivers a ·OH production rate of 250 µM h−1 at neutral pH and remains active over a broad pH range (3–9). Moreover, it enables broad‐spectrum removal of recalcitrant organic pollutants and retains stable performance over 50 h of operation in a flow‐cell reactor. This work offers guidance for designing cascade catalysts at single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid interfaces.

title: Beyond Facet Engineering: Dislocation‐Mediated Nucleation Enables Stable Lithium Deposition on Practical Polycrystalline Cu Collectors
content:
Defect and texture engineering transforms practical polycrystalline Cu into a Li‐hosting interface that directs deposition from the outset. Dislocations create dense preferential nucleation sites, while <110>/<111>‐enriched orientations favor lateral Li migration and coalescence. The resulting compact deposition architecture persists during cycling, delivering highly reversible Li||Cu operation and improved zero‐excess‐Li full‐cell performance.








ABSTRACT
Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path‐dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles (n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full‐cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation‐mediated nucleation and orientation‐regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.

title: Nonreciprocal Bending in Ferroelectric Membranes Driven by Flexoelectricity
content:
Nonreciprocal bending is revealed in suspended functional membranes, where opposite loading directions produce markedly different mechanical responses. Experiments and phase‐field simulations connect this asymmetric behavior to the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.








ABSTRACT
Nonreciprocity reflects the asymmetric propagation or motion of an object in two opposite directions and can achieve directional transport in physics. However, nonreciprocity in natural quasi‐static mechanical systems, including nonreciprocal bending, has rarely been explored. Here we demonstrate nonreciprocal bending in a freestanding ferroelectric single‐crystalline PbTiO3 membrane using suspended‐membrane nanoindentation. The mechanical bending of the ferroelectric membrane is strongly asymmetric in the two opposite bending directions with a difference in effective elastic modulus of up to 33%. The elastic recovery of bending deformation also becomes polarity‐dependent. Such unconventional nonreciprocal bending originates from the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity, as revealed by phase‐field simulations. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.

title: Asymmetric‐Isomerization Dimer Acceptors via Modular Molecular Design Enable Highly Efficient Binary Organic Solar Cells
content:
In this work, we adopt an asymmetric‐isomerization strategy to design two novel dual‐asymmetric isomeric dimer acceptors QCl‐YF and QF‐YCl. Compared with QCl‐YF, QF‐YCl exhibits an enhanced ICT effect as evidenced by a larger electron‐hole spatial separation, which promotes LE/CT hybridization and enables more efficient carrier dynamics. Consequently, the QF‐YCl‐based device achieves a record PCE of 20.23% (vs. 19.60% for QCl‐YF).








ABSTRACT
Dimer acceptors are attractive for organic solar cells (OSCs) owing to their combination of stability and high efficiency, yet the efficiency of dimer‐based binary devices has long stagnated below 20%. The limitation stems from weak intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and poor locally excited/charge‐transfer (LE/CT) state hybridization, which are direct consequences of the canceled dipole moments in symmetric dimer architectures. In this work, we adopt an asymmetric‐isomerization strategy to design two novel dual‐asymmetric isomeric dimer acceptors QCl‐YF and QF‐YCl. Compared with QCl‐YF, QF‐YCl exhibits an enhanced ICT effect as evidenced by a larger electron‐hole spatial separation, which promotes LE/CT hybridization and enables more efficient carrier dynamics. Moreover, the stronger electrostatic potential and dipole moment of QF‐YCl enhances the intermolecular interactions to improve donor/acceptor compatibility and film‐forming process in blend film, consequently leading to more ordered film morphology. Consequently, the QF‐YCl‐based device achieves a record PCE of 20.23% (vs. 19.60% for QCl‐YF), achieving the highest efficiency for dimer‐based binary OSCs. This work demonstrates that asymmetric‐isomerization is a precise and effective design strategy for high‐performance dimer acceptors.

title: All‐In‐One Integration of Inherently Flame‐Retardant, UV‐Resistant, and Antibacterial Polymer by a Biguanide Unit
content:
This work implements an ultra‐efficient strategy to achieve the all‐in‐one integration of inherently flame‐retardant, UV‐resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through chemically copolymerizing a single biguanide unit, paving the way for the environmentally friendly development and high‐efficient design of next‐generation advanced protective materials.








ABSTRACT
The increasing fire accidents, excessive UV exposure, and health threats posed by bacterial infections urgently require advanced polymer materials integrating multiple safety protections. In this study, we propose an ultra‐efficient strategy to achieve the all‐in‐one integration of inherently flame‐retardant, UV‐resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through a single biguanide unit. The key lies in the unique triple protection mechanism exerted by the biguanide unit: high‐temperature char‐formation for flame retardance, n→π* transition absorption for UV‐resistance, and disruption of the negatively charged bacterial surface for antibacteria. As a result, the biguanide‐containing polymer material achieves the best UL‐94 V‐0 flame‐retardant rating with excellent self‐extinguishing properties, ≥99.3% ultra‐high shielding rate for UV light, and ≥99.0% remarkable antibacterial rate. Importantly, the biguanide unit is chemically bonded to the polymer main chain, which not only avoids the health risks and performance degradation caused by the additive migration, but also exhibits outstanding heat resistance, thermal stability, and easy processability. This work simultaneously achieves triple functional integration of polymer materials through a single biguanide unit, realizing previously unattainable multiple safety protections against dangerous fires, harmful UV, and widely‐existed bacteria.

title: Dynamic Proton‐Coordination Equilibrium Enables Nonfreezing Ion Transport for Ultralow‐Temperature Zinc Batteries
content:
A dynamic proton‐coordination equilibrium is established to reconstruct the hydration network and suppress ice crystallization, enabling continuous Zn2+ hopping transport under cryogenic conditions. Meanwhile, the coordination‐regulated electrolyte promotes formation of a robust hybrid interphase, which stabilizes Zn/electrolyte interfaces, suppresses parasitic reactions, and enables highly reversible Zn plating/stripping for ultralow‐temperature zinc batteries.








ABSTRACT
Hydrogel electrolytes (HEs) are promising for aqueous zinc batteries, yet suffer from freezing‐induced loss of ionic transport and interfacial instability at subzero temperatures. Here we report a proton‐mediated coordination equilibrium that enables nonfreezing Zn2+ transport in hydrogel electrolytes under ultralow‐temperature conditions. By coupling phytic acid with zinc phytate, proton activity and Zn–O coordination are dynamically balanced, continuously reconstructing the local hydration environment to suppress hydrogen‐bond ordering, stabilize bound water, and prevent water crystallization. Simultaneously, reversible coordination exchange sustains Zn2+ dissociation and migration through a hopping transport mechanism. At the Zn anode, proton‐mediated interfacial evolution drives the formation of a ZnS/Zn3(PO4)2‐rich hybrid interphase that accelerates interfacial kinetics and suppresses degradation. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte achieves an ionic conductivity of 2.4 mS cm−1 and an apparent Zn2+ transference number of 0.24 at −60°C, enabling Zn||Zn cells to cycle stably for over 3400 h and Zn||PANI full cells to retain 60.1% of their capacity after 4000 cycles at −60°C. These findings identify proton‐mediated coordination equilibrium as a general mechanism for preserving ionic transport in frozen aqueous environments and provide a blueprint for low‐temperature electrochemical energy storage.

title: Orthogonal Reversible Chemistries Affording Multistate Photoswitching in Polymers for Recyclable Intelligent Material Systems
content:
An orthogonal reversible chemistry is developed by combining photoisomerization with metal‐ligand coordination to create a dynamic polymer that can be switched among multiple states. Each state serves as a unique functional component, such as structural elements, shape‑memory modules, and adhesives, enabling the construction of multi‑component intelligent material systems including soft machines. These systems are fully recyclable through a one‑pot, contamination‑free process.








ABSTRACT
The wide applications of intelligent material systems in robotics, flexible devices, AI‐driven techniques, and other high‐tech areas call for the development of recyclable intelligent material systems toward a sustainable future. However, intelligent material systems typically comprise multiple components with heterogeneous structures that usually interfere with or cross‐contaminate each other during operation or recycling. Here, we design recyclable intelligent material systems based on orthogonal reversible chemistries, specifically photoisomerization of azobenzene and metal‐ligand coordination of ruthenium complexes. We create a material, P1‐Ru1, by crosslinking an azobenzene‐containing polymer with a ruthenium complex. P1‐Ru1 switches among multiple states that serve as structural elements, shape‐changing modules, adhesives, and other components in intelligent material systems such as soft machines. Crucially, multicomponent, heterogeneous intelligent material systems constructed using different states of P1‐Ru1 can be recycled via a one‐pot, cross‐contamination‐free process because all components share the same chemical origin. This work demonstrates that orthogonal reversible chemistries make intelligent responses and recyclability compatible in complex systems. Orthogonal reversible chemistries offer a new strategy for designing recyclable intelligent material systems with multiple components and heterogeneous structures for sustainable high‐tech applications.

title: “Water‐in‐Water” Biphasic Electrolyte for Aqueous Zinc‐ion Batteries
content:
The water‐in‐water (W/W) electrolyte introduces an aqueous two‐phase system into zinc batteries through PEG/Dex liquid–liquid phase separation. Inspired by phase‐separated compartments in cells, charged Dex‐rich droplets act as dynamic ion buffers that redistribute Zn2+ and homogenize interfacial ion flux. This aqueous–aqueous interfacial regulation enables uniform Zn deposition and highly reversible aqueous zinc batteries.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are constrained by unstable Zn metal interfaces, where nonuniform Zn2+ transport induces concentration polarization and accelerates parasitic reactions. Here we show that Zn2+ flux can instead be regulated by aqueous–aqueous interfaces. A fully aqueous “water‐in‐water” (W/W) biphasic electrolyte, comprising dextran (Dex)‐rich phase droplets (∼10 µm) suspended in a polyethylene glycol (PEG)‐rich aqueous phase, creates phase boundaries that continuously buffer local Zn2+ accumulation and redistribute ions during plating and stripping. As a result, Zn||Zn cells cycle stably for 1100 h at 10 mA cm−2 and 10 mAh cm−2, and Ah‐level Zn||NaV3O8 pouch cells sustain long‐term operation. This work demonstrates an aqueous electrolyte architecture in which interfacial electrostatics, rather than solvent chemistry, governs Zn2+ transport.

title: Bio‐Inspired Reconstruction of Wood‐Chip Electrolytes Enables Triple Zn2+ Confinement for Durable and Sustainable Flexible Zinc‐Air Batteries
content:
Inspired by the hierarchical architecture of wood, a biomass‐derived hydrogel electrolyte combines a lignin‐rich water‐retaining shell with cooperative Zn2+ confinement from phosphonate chelators, dynamic Schiff‐base motifs, and polymer domains. This triple‐confinement strategy regulates zincate chemistry, suppresses irreversible ZnO accumulation, and enables highly durable flexible zinc‐air batteries (ZABs).








ABSTRACT
Extending the operational lifetime of flexible zinc‐air batteries (ZABs) has traditionally focused on improving electrolyte water retention, yet most systems still fail within ∼400 h, revealing that dehydration alone is not the fundamental limitation. Here, a bio‐inspired hydrogel electrolyte reconstructed from wood chips overcomes this bottleneck by separating cellulose and lignin: cellulose forms a hydrated network while the extracted lignin is re‐applied as an outer water‐retentive layer, mimicking the hierarchical fiber‐bark architecture of plants. Beyond hydration, the electrolyte implements triple Zn2+ confinement through phosphate‐based chelators, dynamic Schiff‐base coordination, and polymeric domains, stabilizing Zn2+, suppressing ZnO accumulation, and maintaining interfacial reaction equilibrium at the zinc anode. Flexible ZABs incorporating this electrolyte deliver high power density (124.9 mW cm−2), robust mechanical adaptability, and extended cycling up to 600 h at 1 mA cm−2, while remaining operational under low‐temperature and dry conditions. Fully biodegradable and derived from abundant biomass, this system demonstrates that durability arises from hierarchical ion regulation and reaction‐equilibrium control rather than water retention alone, providing mechanistic insight into flexible ZABs failure. This work establishes a framework in which biomass valorization and bio‐inspired hierarchical design enable durable, high‐performance, and environmentally sustainable flexible energy storage.

title: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion–Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells
content:
Ordered orientation of Dion–Jacobson 2D perovskite films is obtained by preparing a Ruddlesden‐Popper 2D perovskite on the surface of the organic diammonium•PbI2 intermediate‐phase film. Solar cells with oriented 2D perovskite films yield an outstanding efficiency of 21.1%, retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1‐sun illumination.








ABSTRACT
Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate‐phase film with a Ruddlesden‐Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two‐step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums‐based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1‐sun illumination (ISOS‐L‐2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.

title: Chiral Phonon–Driven Ultrafast Spin Currents in a Non‐Magnetic Ferroelectric
content:
Broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy shows signatures of ultrafast spin‐current generation in non‐magnetic ferroelectric β$\beta$’‐In2Se3${\rm In}_2{\rm Se}_3$. Reversal of the emitted field upon sample inversion and substitution of Pt with W indicates spin‐Hall‐mediated charge conversion, while polarization‐resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, highlighting chiral phonons as a potential route to ultrafast spin transport.








ABSTRACT
The discovery that fundamental lattice vibrations can carry angular momentum allows non‐magnetic materials to exhibit properties that until now have only been observable in magnetic materials. However, the role of these specific vibrations, commonly known as chiral phonons, in driving ultrafast spin dynamics has not yet been explored experimentally. Here, using broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the non‐magnetic ferroelectric In2Se3$\mathrm{In}_2\mathrm{Se}_3$ generates signals consistent with a ultrafast spin current after excitation with an ultrafast laser pulse, which we attribute to a chiral phonon–induced spin Seebeck effect. We suggest that the transient heating creates an non‐equilibrium phonon distribution, resulting in a net angular momentum and magnetization perpendicular to the thermal gradient, which is converted into a terahertz electromagnetic pulse via an inverse spin‐Hall effect in a thin metal overlayer. The emitted field reverses sign upon flipping the sample orientation or replacing Pt with W, consistent with spin‐current generation. Polarization‐resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, indicating an additional polarization‐dependent ultrafast response. Our results establish chiral phonons as a route for generating ultrafast spin currents in non‐magnetic materials as well as providing a pathway toward terahertz sources with switchable handedness.

title: Synchronized Ablation of Multifocal Tumors Enabled by Multi‐Channel Lanthanide Nanocomposites
content:
A multi‐channel lanthanide nanocomposite enables orthogonal monitoring of tumor pH, glutathione, and temperature to guide customized therapy. Real‐time luminescence readouts determine a single irradiation protocol that synchronizes drug release and photothermal treatment, allowing efficient ablation of multifocal tumors while minimizing overtreatment and improving therapeutic precision.








ABSTRACT
The multifocal nature of orthotopic breast tumors makes it difficult to treat due to individual tumor differences, requiring multiple therapeutic interventions. Here, a customized therapeutic strategy is presented for multiple tumors by using the same prescription based on a multi‐channel lanthanide nanocomposite and orthogonally controlled drug release. The upconversion luminescence of the nanocomposite at different wavelengths can monitor pH‐responsive mitoxantrone (MXT) release, reduced glutathione‐responsive near‐infrared (NIR) absorbance change, and eigen temperature, respectively, allowing modulation of photothermal treatment and temperature‐responsive paclitaxel release through customized whole‐body irradiation to achieve synchronized ablation of different individual tumors. Small animal experiments confirm multifocal breast tumors can be treated through this customized therapeutic strategy with both high efficiency and low overtherapy risk.

title: High‐Performance Low Threshold Voltage n‐Type OECTs via a Stepwise Cyanation of Quinoxaline‐Based Polymeric Semiconductor
content:
A stepwise cyanation strategy tunes ionic‐electronic transport and threshold voltage in quinoxaline‐based n‐type OMIECs. QxCN‐CNTVT delivers a low threshold voltage, high µC*, and robust cycling stability. These favorable properties realize low‐power bioelectrical signal amplification and flexible OECT logic circuits.








ABSTRACT
Achieving both low threshold voltage (Vth) and high performance in organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) is critical for low‐power, high‐sensitivity bioelectronics, yet simultaneously achieving low Vth and high device performance remains a long‐standing challenge. Herein, we propose a stepwise cyanation strategy to modify quinoxaline‐based polymeric semiconductors to mitigate this dilemma. Benefiting from the strong electron‐withdrawing ability of cyano substituents, QxCN‐CNTVT functionalized with cyano groups on both donor and acceptor units exhibits a deep LUMO level of −4.23 eV, one of the deepest among reported n‐type ionic–electronic conductors. As a result, OECTs based on QxCN‐CNTVT demonstrate excellent comprehensive performance, with a high µC* value of up to 168.89 F cm−1 V−1 s−1 and a low Vth of 0.13 V, while maintaining superior operational stability (retaining ∼80% of the initial current after 10,000 s of continuous operation and 10,000 full switching cycles). Furthermore, QxCN‐CNTVT is successfully applied to complementary inverters for efficient amplification of electrooculogram (EOG) and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, as well as NAND and NOR logic gates for integrated logic functions. This work not only alleviates the widely observed imbalance between performance and Vth in n‐type OECTs but also provides a versatile molecular design strategy for next‐generation low‐power bioelectronic devices.

title: Molecularly Modulated Charge Retention Enables Post‐Illumination H2O2 Production in Imine‐Linked Polymers
content:
Tuning the amine‐centered units in imine‐linked polymer networks controls charge separation and retention. The C3N3‐centered structure sustains longer‐lived charges and promotes dark‐state H2O2 production after illumination. This molecular‐level control links structure with charge retention and dark catalysis, offering a simple strategy to extend photocatalytic activity beyond light irradiation.








ABSTRACT
Decoupling photocatalytic solar fuel generation from continuous illumination is a prerequisite for practical off‐grid applications, yet demands precise control over photogenerated charge retention and dark‐phase utilization. While persistent charge availability post‐light cutoff is central to dark‐state catalysis, a quantitative structure‐dynamics‐function relationship linking molecular design to charge‐retention kinetics and post‐illumination reactivity remains unestablished. Here, we report a molecular tuning strategy of the central amine‐derived units that systematically regulates charge separation, retention timescales, and dark‐state H2O2 production in imine‐linked polymer networks. Systematic evaluation of the series reveals a direct correlation between charge lifetime and dark activity. Compared with the N‐centered reference, the C3N3‐centered analogue exhibits drastically prolonged electron‐associated transient lifetime, with a ∼27‐fold longer decay timescale at the picosecond scale and a ∼3‐fold increase at the nanosecond scale. This enhanced charge retention corresponds to a dark‐state H2O2 production of 4941 µmol g−1 within 40 min, ∼1.5‐fold higher than that of the N‐centered counterpart. Density functional theory calculations reveal distinct electronic structures associated within the C3N3‐centered framework, providing a favorable electronic environment for electron localization and subsequent utilization. These results establish a molecular structure‐charge retention‐dark reaction relationship for photocatalytic H2O2 production beyond the illumination period.

title: Photocatalytic Tandem Reaction for Urea Synthesis From Atmospheric CO2 and N2
content:
A two‐step tandem photocatalytic system is proposed to directly convert atmospheric CO2 and N2 into urea. IL@PCN‐250‐Fe2Co captures CO2 and reduces it to CO, while HTP‐Cu3‐imi‐COF couples *CO with *NO (from N2 oxidation) via *OCNO intermediates, achieving a urea production rate of 259.87 µg·gcat−1·h−1.








ABSTRACT
Photocatalytic urea synthesis directly from atmospheric CO2 and N2 offers a sustainable route to bypass the energy‐intensive Bosch–Meiser process, yet simultaneously achieving CO2 capture and reduction, N2 activation, and C─N coupling within a single system remains challenging. Herein, we report a two‐step tandem platform combining ionic‐liquid‐modified metal–organic framework (IL@PCN‐250‐Fe2Co) with a trinuclear copper‐based covalent organic framework (HTP‐Cu3‐imi‐COF) for urea photosynthesis from air. The IL@MOF captures atmospheric CO2 and photoreduces it to CO, while HTP‐Cu3‐imi‐COF couples the generated CO with ambient N2 into urea. This synergistic tandem configuration delivers a urea production rate of 259.87 µg·gcat−1·h−1 under air, marking the first demonstration of photocatalytic urea synthesis from atmospheric CO2 and N2. In situ spectroscopic measurements and DFT calculations reveal that the imidazole‐functionalized HTP segments act as hole‐rich oxidation domains, promoting water oxidation to generate *OH species that oxidize locally enriched N2 to *NO intermediates. Simultaneously, the Cu3 clusters serve as electron‐rich centers for CO adsorption and activation, forming *CO that couples with *NO via the critical *OCNO intermediate toward urea formation. This work not only showcases the first photocatalytic urea synthesis from air but also establishes a modular paradigm for cascade catalysts that integrate capture and conversion toward sustainable chemical transformations.

title: Solvation‐Equilibrium Locking Enables Ultrawide‐Temperature Operation of High‐Voltage Lithium‐Metal Batteries
content:
Solvation‐equilibrium locking suppresses thermally driven Li+ solvation reorganization by balancing dipole‐dipole, ion–dipole, and ion–ion interactions. The resulting anion‐rich, temperature‐insensitive electrolyte enables high‐voltage lithium‐metal batteries to discharge at −85°C, operate up to 120°C, and remain functional after cooling to −122.9°C, while supporting high‐energy pouch‐cell operation.








ABSTRACT
High‐energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep‐sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature‐sensitive ion transport, Li+ solvation, and interfacial chemistry. A solvation‐equilibrium‐locked electrolyte (SELE) is reported by combining dimethyl sulfite (DMS), a low‐freezing weakly solvating solvent, with Pyr13DFOB (1‐methyl‐1‐propylpyrrolidinium difluoro(oxalato)borate) as an ionic‐liquid co‐solvent. Cooperative ion–dipole and weak C–H⋯O interactions between DMS and Pyr13+ regulate the free‐solvent reservoir, while TFSI− (bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and DFOB− enrich the primary Li+ coordination shell. Variable‐temperature 7Li NMR, Raman, and molecular dynamics simulations show that solvent‐separated ion pairs, contact ion pairs, and aggregates remain nearly invariant from −60°C to 60°C, unlike the strongly temperature‐responsive Pyr13DFOB‐free electrolyte. This locked anion‐rich solvation structure reduces solvent coordination around Li+, mitigates solvent‐derived interfacial decomposition and gas evolution, and promotes LiF‐ and borate‐rich interphases on Li metal and NMC811. Consequently, Li||NMC811 cells deliver discharge capacity at −85°C and operate up to 120°C, while pouch cells remain functional after cooling to −122.9°C. A 6.6 Ah Li||Ni90 pouch cell further achieves 565 Wh kg−1 under lean‐electrolyte conditions, establishing solvation‐equilibrium locking as a molecular design principle for lithium metal batteries operating over a broad temperature range.

title: A Simple Descriptor for Solid‐State Ionic Conductors Across Chemistries
content:
Researchers develop a simple and transferable descriptor, distance contraction, for solid‐state ion migration across Li‐, Na‐, K‐, and Mg‐ion conductors and diverse anion chemistries. By capturing the maximum local contraction experienced by the migrating ion, the descriptor enables rapid materials screening and unifies diverse ion‐transport mechanisms.








ABSTRACT
The discovery of new solid‐state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile‐ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile‐ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion‐migration barriers spanning Li‐, Na‐, K‐, and Mg‐ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆d, a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile‐ion–neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short‐range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low‐ from high‐barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆d in a high‐throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast‐ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast‐ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆d links diverse ion‐transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.

title: Self‐Fueling Nanobacteria Harnesses Leaked Pancreatic Fluid to Eradicate Residual Tumors After Surgery
content:
A postoperative pancreatic cancer therapy transforms leaked pancreatic fluid from a surgical complication into a therapeutic resource. Nanoengineered B.t. depletes tumor mucins, while a pancreatic enzyme corona enhances tumor penetration and cytotoxicity. Integrated with a TRPV1a‐loaded GelMA hydrogel, the platform suppresses recurrence, remodels the immune microenvironment, and alleviates pain after surgery.








ABSTRACT
Postoperative management of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains hindered by two closely linked challenges: the harmful effects of pancreatic fistula and the high risk of local tumor recurrence. Although leaked pancreatic fluid (PF) is generally regarded as a postoperative complication, its abundance of digestive enzymes also suggests an underexplored therapeutic opportunity. Here, we developed a localized therapeutic strategy that converts the enzyme‐rich fistula microenvironment from a pathological burden into an antitumor resource. To achieve this, we nano‐engineered Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (B.t.) and integrated it with TRPV1 antagonist‐loaded nanomicelles in a GelMA hydrogel, generating the platform TNPs‐N@B.t. + Gel. Mechanistically, this system acts in a coordinated manner within the postoperative PDAC microenvironment. B.t. degrades tumor‐associated mucins, thereby dismantling the protective barrier that shields PDAC cells from pancreatic enzymes and restoring their vulnerability to enzymatic attack. Meanwhile, PF forms an in situ digestive enzyme corona on the nanoengineered bacterial surface, which promotes deeper tumor penetration by disrupting intercellular adhesion. In parallel, delivery of the TRPV1 antagonist (TRPV1a) suppresses CGRP release, attenuates cancer‐associated fibroblast (CAF) activation, and facilitates NK‐cell‐associated antitumor responses. In postoperative PDAC models, TNPs‐N@B.t. + Gel showed durable local retention, enhanced tumor accumulation, suppressed recurrence, prolonged survival, and alleviated pain‐related behaviors without evident systemic toxicity.

title: An Ultrarobust Dual‐Modal Neural Fiber With In‐Sensor Computing
content:
An ultrarobust in‐sensor‐computing dual‐modal neural fiber simultaneously decodes touch position and pressure, achieving <5 mm position resolution and a 0.6 N detection limit. Seamlessly integrated into textiles, it combines flexibility, waterproofing, and reconfigurability with efficient multimodal feature fusion, supporting diverse human–machine interactions, including logic gate operations, the internet of things, underwater robotic control, and intelligent recognition.








ABSTRACT
Touch behavior constitutes the most direct physical manifestation of human intentions, meaning that intention decoding requires human–machine interfaces to simultaneously sense touch position and pressure. Conventional systems, however, rely on physically stacked discrete sensors and von Neumann architectures, causing data redundancy and impaired wearability. Here, we present an in‐sensor‐computing dual‐modal neural fiber (ID neural fiber) that overcomes this fundamental limitation. The ID neural fiber achieves an unprecedented position resolution of < 5 mm and a pressure detection limit of 0.6 N, combined with exceptional robustness–sustaining 300 times load‐bearing capacity and exhibiting < 8% performance fluctuation under bending. Coupled with flexibility, waterproofing, and reconfigurability, the ID neural fiber can be seamlessly integrated into textiles for reliable operation in harsh environments, including underwater robotic control. Crucially, the ID neural fiber enables in‐sensor computing that dramatically increases the information density and allows synchronized feature fusion through programmable logic gates, enabling efficient real‐time intention recognition. To capture touch habits, an intelligent system with the ID neural fiber achieves a remarkable identification accuracy of 98.21%. This work establishes a new material–architecture paradigm that unifies ultrarobustness, dual‐modality, and in‐sensor computing, setting the stage for next‐generation wearable human–machine interfaces with both comfort and intelligence.

title: Pathway Engineering Enables Durable Iridium‐Free Acidic Water Oxidation
content:
Lu doping in Co3O4 shifts the acidic OER pathway to direct O‐O coupling and stabilizes the lattice via Lu‐O bonds that suppress Co dissolution. As a noble‑metal‑free anode in PEMWE, it achieves 1 A cm−2 at 1.837 V with minimal degradation over 900 h under stepped currents from 100 to 500 mA cm−2, highlighting exceptional durability.








ABSTRACT
The pursuit of noble metal‐free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity‐stability trade‐off, wherein non‐precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium‐stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu0.08Co2.92O4) designed through site‐specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical simulations reveal that Lu incorporation introduces robust Lu‐O bonds and induces charge redistribution that strengthens Co‐O covalency and suppresses Co2+ dissolution, which is critical for improved OER durability, and simultaneously optimizes the Co‐Co distance to favor direct O‐O radical coupling with a reduced energy barrier. Leveraging these structural advantages, a practical PEMWE employing Lu0.08Co2.92O4 delivers an industrially relevant current density of 1000 mA cm−2 at 1.837 V. Separately, it maintains stable operation for over 900 h under a stepwise current density from 200 to 500 mA cm−2, highlighting its potential for sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Axial Benzotriazole‐Coordinated Ni Single Atoms Enable Rapid Interfacial Electron Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic Acetylene Semi‐Hydrogenation
content:
The interfacial electron transfer of photocatalytic acetylene semi‐hydrogenation is substantially accelerated by axially coordinating benzotriazole to Ni single atoms in graphitic carbon nitride, which strengthens the orbital overlap between Ni sites and acetylene. An ethylene production rate of 32.29 mmol gcat−1 h−1 with a C2H4 selectivity of 97.6% is achieved.








ABSTRACT
Photocatalytic semi‐hydrogenation of acetylene (C2H2) to ethylene (C2H4) often suffers from inefficient interfacial electron transfer from the photocatalysts to adsorbed C2H2. Here, we demonstrate that axial coordination of benzotriazole (BTA) to Ni single atoms in C3N4 (BTA‐Ni SAs‐C3N4) facilitates interfacial electron‐transfer processes. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, in situ transient surface photovoltage spectroscopy, in situ photochemical infrared spectroscopy, and theoretical simulations reveal that BTA‐coordinated Ni SAs serve as the centers for rapid electron transfer by upshifting the Ni d‐band center and strengthening the orbital overlap between Ni SA and adsorbed C2H2. Consequently, BTA‐Ni SAs‐C3N4 achieves a very high C2H4 production rate of 32.29 mmol gcat−1 h−1 with a C2H4 selectivity of 97.6% under simulated solar irradiation, which is ∼4‐times higher than that for Ni SAs‐C3N4. The apparent quantum yield at 365 nm is up to 4.65%, superior to reported photocatalytic acetylene semi‐hydrogenation. This work highlights the importance of interfacial charge transfer in photocatalytic acetylene hydrogenation and provides a rational strategy for designing high‐performance photocatalysts.

title: Tuning N‐Species Adsorption/Desorption Equilibrium by Ni1Aun‐SrTiO3 for Artificial Urea Photosynthesis
content:
Artificial urea photosynthesis from N2, CO2, and H2O is driven by tuning the N‐species adsorption/desorption equilibrium of the bimetallic Ni1Aun‐SrTiO3 photocatalyst, achieving a high yield of 1333.63 µg gcat.–1 with a collectible solid product. Tandem TPD‐MS and in situ Raman spectroscopy confirm *NH2 and *NH2COO– intermediates, providing mechanistic insights into urea photosynthesis.








ABSTRACT
Inefficient generation of N‐related intermediates, stemming from inert adsorption/photoactivation of N2, has hindered efficient artificial photosynthesis of urea from N2, CO2, and H2O. To overcome this bottleneck, we herein propose a strategy for modulating the adsorption/desorption equilibrium of N‐related species using precisely designed bimetallic Ni1Aun active sites supported on a strontium titanate (NiAu‐STO) semiconductor photocatalyst. This strategy significantly enhances N2 adsorption/activation and effective generation of N‐related intermediates to facilitate C–N coupling for the photocatalytic urea synthesis, affording a considerable urea production rate of 1333.63 µg gcat.−1, with successful crystallization of a collectible solid‐phase urea product. Furthermore, we developed a novel reaction‐temperature programmed desorption‐mass spectrometry tandem monitoring system to elucidate the adsorption behavior of N2, which can clarify the adsorption behavior of N2 and confirm the formation of critical N‐related intermediates (e.g., *NH2) on the NiAu‐STO photocatalyst. In addition, in situ Raman spectroscopy results further validated the formation of a distinctive C–N coupling intermediate (*NH2COO–) on the photocatalyst surface, providing mechanistic insights into urea photosynthesis from N2, CO2, and H2O.

title: From Dark Photocatalysis to Photobattery‐Type Operation: A Re‐Functionalized Ti‐MOF for Solar Energy Storage
content:
ReCl47‐bpy is developed as a solar‐rechargeable, Re‐functionalized two‐dimensional metal–organic framework (MOF) for light‐driven charge storage and dark utilization. Re–bipyridine sites stabilize photoinduced electrons, enabling two complementary configurations: a MOF suspension for long‐lived charge retention and dark H2 evolution, and a spin‐coated MOF photoelectrode for photocharging, dark electrical discharge, and photobattery‐type operation.








ABSTRACT
Efficient harvesting, storage, and on‐demand release of solar energy are essential for overcoming the intermittency of sunlight and enabling continuous solar energy‐driven processes, yet achieving storage of photogenerated charge remains challenging. Here, we report a Ti‐based bipyridine MOF, COK47‐bpy, and its ReCl(CO)3‐functionalized analogue, ReCl47‐bpy, as photochargeable materials for time‐decoupled solar energy utilization. Re incorporation introduces localized photosensitizing and “electron sink” sites while preserving the parent framework structure, enabling visible‐light response, faster charge accumulation, and improved charge retention. In colloidal suspension, ReCl47‐bpy reaches an electron storage capacity of 19.5 C g−1MOF under simulated solar irradiation and retains about 70% of the stored charge after 2.5 months. The stored electrons can be released on demand for dark hydrogen (H2) evolution with electron‐to‐H2 efficiencies exceeding 90%. Beyond colloids, when fabricated as robust FTO‐supported layers, ReCl47‐bpy|FTO photoelectrodes deliver capacities of up to ∼7.0 mAh g−1MOF upon photocharging under 1 Sun irradiation. Overall, this work establishes Re‐functionalized Ti‐MOFs as versatile platforms for solar‐driven charge storage, dark photocatalysis, and MOF‐based photoelectrodes, toward the development of next‐generation MOF‐based energy devices.

title: Polyacrylate‐Based Dielectric Elastomer Fiber Actuators for High‐Performance Artificial Muscles
content:
A continuous coaxial wet‐spinning strategy enables high‐performance polyacrylate dielectric elastomers to be directly processed into hollow fiber actuators. The resulting fiber actuators combine scalable fabrication with large prestretch‐free axial strain, high energy and power densities, and flexible modular assembly into artificial‐muscle architectures for diverse soft robotic systems.








ABSTRACT
Dielectric elastomer fiber actuators (DEFAs) are promising candidates for artificial muscle applications, owing to their high axial actuation and mechanical compliance, yet achieving scalable fabrication without compromising electromechanical performance remains a critical bottleneck. Existing continuous manufacturing routes are predominantly restricted to silicone elastomers, which yield limited actuation strains and low energy densities. Here, a continuous fabrication strategy that integrates coaxial wet spinning with in situ ultraviolet curing is developed to produce polyacrylate‐based DEFAs (PA‐DEFAs) from a bimodal‐networked polyacrylate dielectric elastomer at rates up to 22.5 mm s−1. The fiber geometry and electromechanical properties are readily tunable by adjusting the core‐to‐shell flow‐rate ratio and elastomer formulation. The resulting fiber actuators deliver a maximum prestretch‐free axial strain of ∼39%, a maximum energy density of 54.8 J kg−1, and a peak power density of 443 W kg−1—outperforming previously reported continuously fabricated DEFAs. The long and continuous fiber architecture further enables wrapped actuator and parallel‐connected arrays, facilitating seamless integration into diverse soft robotic systems, including a robotic arm, a crawling robot, and an underwater robotic manta‐ray with modular fault‐tolerance. By reconciling scalable manufacturing with high actuation performance, PA‐DEFAs establish a versatile and manufacturing‐compatible platform for next‐generation artificial muscles and adaptive soft robotics.

title: Closed Pores as Internal Stress‐Regulation Units for Practical Silicon–Carbon Anodes
content:
Closed nanopores serve as internal stress‐regulation units in silicon–carbon anodes, shifting lithiation‐induced deformation toward the particle interior while retaining open pathways for rapid Li+ transport. This pore architecture suppresses electrode swelling and improves rate and cycling performance, remains effective after kilogram‐scale synthesis and Ah‐scale pouch‐cell assembly, and is further extended to phosphorus‐doped carbon through machine‐learning‐guided screening.








ABSTRACT
Silicon–carbon anodes are among the most promising candidates for high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries, yet their practical implementation remains constrained by lithiation‐induced outward deformation, electrode cracking, and persistent interphase degradation. Here, closed pores are introduced as internal stress‐regulation units to address the coupled mechanical and electrochemical instability of silicon–carbon anodes. Heteroatom‐doped carbon hosts are engineered to contain abundant closed nanopores, which redirect expansion‐induced stress toward the particle interior and suppress macroscopic electrode swelling. Meanwhile, heteroatom doping enlarges the carbon interlayer spacing and enhances electronic conductivity, enabling accelerated and more balanced Li+ insertion/extraction kinetics. As a representative material, the nitrogen–doped silicon–carbon composite delivers a reversible capacity of 1756.5 mAh g−1, an initial Coulombic efficiency of 90.2%, and 868.4 mAh g−1 at 3 C, while reducing electrode thickness expansion from 38.4% to 13.1% after 50 cycles. The material is further produced in 6 kg batches and enables 2 Ah LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) pouch cells with 80.0% capacity retention after 1200 cycles and only 8.4% thickness growth after 900 cycles. Machine–learning–guided phosphorus doping further validates the transferability of the closed‐pore design. This work establishes closed‐pore stress regulation as a scalable structural strategy for practical low‐expansion silicon–carbon anodes.

title: Reconstruction of the Electric Double Layer for Long‐Lasting Aqueous Manganese Metal Batteries
content:
We designed a high‐LUMO additive, n‐decyltrimethylammonium bromide, to reconstruct the electric double layer in aqueous Mn metal batteries. Its high reduction stability enables persistent, indecomposable adsorption on the Mn surface, effectively stabilizing the interfacial chemical environment and suppressing HER. This approach enables a record‐high Coulombic efficiency of 93% and delivers 600 stable full‐cell cycles.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous Mn metal batteries (AMMBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to the natural abundance of Mn, their operational safety, and their high energy density. However, the high chemical reactivity of the Mn metal anode induces a severe hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in poor cycling reversibility. Fundamentally, HER is a parasitic cathodic reaction competing with Mn electrodeposition and may accompany Mn corrosion. Its kinetics are influenced by the interfacial water environment within the electric double layer (EDL). In this study, we propose a strategy for reconstructing the EDL by adding n‐decyltrimethylammonium bromide (10‐DTAB), a surfactant with a relatively high lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), to the electrolyte to stabilize the Mn anode. The high LUMO energy level enhances its reduction stability, thus preventing continuous decomposition during cycling and enabling sustained interfacial protection. Consequently, the Mn anode exhibits a markedly enhanced Coulombic efficiency of 93%. This study demonstrates a durable EDL regulation paradigm based on high‐LUMO additives, offering new insights into stabilizing Mn metal anodes and advancing AMMBs toward practical applications.

title: Durable Interphase Incorporating Cross‐Linked Polymer Enables Long‐Calendar‐Life Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
A cross‐linked polymer‐enhanced SEI (CPE SEI) is constructed to enhance the mechanical stability and passivation capability of the SEI. Compared with the alkoxides and oligomers in the baseline SEI, the cross‐linked polymer in the CPE SEI possesses high modulus and low swelling, thereby avoiding SEI reconstruction and electrolyte permeation and contributing to long‐calendar‐life lithium metal batteries.








ABSTRACT
The practical deployment of lithium (Li) metal batteries is hindered by not only cycle life but also calendar life. The poor calendar life stems from both the repeated reconstruction of the solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI) during cycles and, particularly, the continuous growth of SEI during storage. Herein, a durable SEI with high mechanical stability against volume fluctuations and superior passivation capability to suppress electrolyte permeation is demonstrated by integrating inorganics and a cross‐linked polymer into the SEI. Concretely, a cross‐linked polymer with high modulus and low swelling is in‐situ incorporated among the inorganics of an anion‐derived SEI. The elastic modulus of the SEI is significantly increased from 1.63 to 4.37 GPa, and the compactness of the SEI is also improved to suppress electrolyte permeation. Consequently, the cycle life and calendar life of Li metal coin cells are extended by 73% (from 190 to 329 cycles) and 129% (from 1553 to 3561 h), respectively. Furthermore, a prototype pouch cell (506 Wh kg−1) undergoes 124 cycles. This work establishes an effective strategy that concurrently improves the mechanical and passivation performance of the SEI, tackling the critical challenge of calendar life in Li metal batteries.

title: Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic
content:
To resolve the catastrophic disaster of plastic contamination, the Cu‐Fe dual‐single‐atom‐loaded In2P3S9 NSs photocatalyst was prepared for direct conversion of raw polyvinylidene fluoride plastic into valuable chemicals. The dual‐single‐atom catalyst exhibits exceptional performance, with a total acetic/formic acid production of ∼1351.8 µmol g−1.








ABSTRACT
Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium‐ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value‐added chemicals remain limited. To resolve this, Fe and Cu dual single atoms incorporated on a new two‐dimensional material nanosheets (In2P3S9 NSs/Fe‐Cu DSAs) were prepared as photocatalysts for direct raw PVDF plastic conversion to high‐value chemicals. The best‐performing photocatalyst (Fe1.0Cu0.5) achieves a total acetic/formic acid generation of ∼1351.8 µmol g−1. Various in situ characterizations such as atomic force microscopy‐kelvin probe force microscopy, x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) demonstrate superior electron extraction from In2P3S9 NSs to Fe and Cu DSAs, after which the electrons are subsequently scavenged by O2 under ambient conditions. Moreover, quenching experiments as well as in situ infrared spectroscopy, and in situ EPR reveal the vital impact of photoexcited electrons and hydroxyl radicals in PVDF upcycling into high‐value products. These findings highlight the significant potential of photocatalysis in transforming one of the most resistant plastic wastes (PVDF) into value‐added products, providing a sustainable remedy for plastic pollution crisis.

title: Spatially Decoupled Charge Compensation Enables Versatile Cation–Anion Co‐Intercalation in Layered Metal Oxide Cathodes
content:
We introduce a spatially decoupled charge‐compensation strategy in layered vanadium oxide to facilitate the stable co‐(de)intercalation of multivalent cations (Mvn+) and anions. Unlike conventional charge‐compensation mechanisms that rely on O2−/O2− redox within rigid inorganic skeletons, the intercalated organic molecules serve as redox‐active centers, effectively accommodating Mvn+ and anions co‐(de)intercalation while minimizing charge and structural perturbations in the host lattice.








ABSTRACT
Multivalent cation–anion co‐(de)intercalation offers a promising pathway to higher energy densities in multivalent ion batteries. However, its practical realization is challenged by lattice strain and the lack of effective dual charge‐compensation strategies. Here, we report a layered vanadium oxide cathode with pre‐intercalated melamine ligands (MeVO) that enables a spatially decoupled charge‐compensation mechanism—organic ligands serve as redox centers for anions, while metal sites accommodate multivalent cation redox. This design alleviates electrostatic crowding, promotes ion mobility, and preserves structural integrity. Using Mg2+‐TFSI− as a representative system, MeVO delivers a record cycle life of over 36 000 cycles at a loading of approximately 3 mg cm−2 and an areal capacity of 3.3 mAh cm−2 at a higher loading of 16.4 mg cm−2, surpassing leading Mg‐ion cathodes. The hybrid structure also supports co‐(de)intercalation of various multivalent cations and anions, demonstrating its potential as a versatile intercalation platform for high‐performance energy storage.

title: Robust Dipicolinic Acid‐Anchored Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Wide‐Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics
content:
The dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchor group is designed for a novel type of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM), denoted as XS21, to intensify both the interfacial stability and device performance.








ABSTRACT
The anchoring group of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) hole‐transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material, denoted by XS21, engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual‐action mechanism of pyridine–Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate‐metal interaction. Furthermore, XS21 imparts both low acid‐dissociation constants (Ka) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide‐bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing XS21 deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open‐circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating XS21 into monolithic all‐perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi‐dentate pyridine‐carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next‐generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Stress‐Resistant Plant Cell‐Wall Inspired Cell Armor Enables Red Blood Cell Lyophilization
content:
A modular, biomimetic armor inspired by plant cell walls was constructed on red blood cells to enable successful lyophilization and ambient‐temperature storage. The ternary coating—comprising MOF NPs, Zn2+, and polymers—synergistically protects cells from freezing and drying‐induced damage. This interface engineering strategy achieved approximately 95% recovery while maintaining key cellular functions, paving the way for the global distribution of cell‐based therapies without cold‐chain requirements.








ABSTRACT
Lyophilization offers an attractive route for ambient‐temperature storage of biological systems by eliminating cold‐chain dependence and suppressing solution‐phase degradation. However, lyophilizing mammalian cells remains challenging due to their vulnerability to coupled stresses, including ice‐induced mechanical injury and membrane destabilization during freezing and dehydration. In nature, stress‐resistant plant cells survive extreme conditions through multifunctional cell walls. Inspired by their natural survival strategies, we engineer an artificial membrane armor (AMA) that enables efficient lyophilization of red blood cells (RBCs). This biomimetic AMA integrates a nanoporous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF‐8) for mechanical support, a water‐retentive polymer matrix for hydration retention and colloidal stabilization, and Zn2+ coordination preserves membrane fluidity and suppresses freeze‐ and dehydration‐driven membrane phase transitions. Through synergistic interfacial protection, the AMA effectively buffers coupled stresses associated with lyophilization, enabling ∼95% post‐rehydration recovery of RBCs using an ultra‐low protectant content (<5 wt%) together with an ambient shelf‐life of at least 3 months, unachievable with previous methods. Furthermore, the rehydrated RBCs preserve their native morphology, membrane mechanics, metabolic activity, oxygen transport capability, and in vivo circulation behavior. This work establishes a bioinspired interfacial engineering strategy for transferring desiccation tolerance from plants to mammalian cells, advancing ambient‐temperature biostorage of sensitive living systems.

title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation‐Type Framework Anodes for Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
content:
A synchronic multilevel assembly strategy enables precise synthesis of mesoporous nanosized intercalation‐type framework anodes, where the identified M‐Na4Ti5O12/C delivers outstanding fast‐charging and pouch‐cell performance via favorable ion transport and robust interfacial kinetics.








ABSTRACT
Intercalation‐type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast‐charging sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation‐type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic‐scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M‐Na4Ti5O12/C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g−1 at 10 A g−1) and cycling stability (<0.023% capacity fade per cycle over 1000 cycles at 0.2 A g−1) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na+ diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low‐barrier, nanoscale ion‐conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg−1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high‐rate battery materials.

title: High‐Performance Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fibers via a Tandem Alignment Strategy
content:
A tandem alignment strategy based on electrospinning fabricates highly aligned thin liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers. These fibers exhibit excellent actuation performance, including large deformation (80%), ultrafast contraction (1485% s−1), and high power density (6105 W kg−1), alongside resonant oscillation under thermal stimuli at a certain frequency. This work provides a novel strategy for fabricating high‐performance LCE fibers. 








ABSTRACT
Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers have shown great potential as shape‐memory soft materials due to their large and reversible deformation capacity. However, fabrication methods for LCE fibers with ultrafast thermal response and the exploration of the factors influencing their thermal actuation performance remain limited. A tandem alignment strategy based on electrospinning is presented to fabricate highly aligned LCE fibers. These LCE fibers achieve an order parameter of up to 0.78 and exhibit exceptional actuation performance under thermal stimulation, including an actuation strain of 80%, an actuation speed of 1485% s−1, and a peak power density of 6105 W kg−1. Furthermore, the actuation performance can be significantly enhanced by resonance. Under constant heating conditions, modulation of the heating frequency enables the actuation speed of the LCE fibers to be amplified up to 10‐fold, achieving bioinspired energy efficiency optimization similar to the wing‐flapping of insects. The LCE fibers demonstrate promising applicability in scenarios requiring ultrafast and efficient thermal actuation.

title: In Situ Formation of a Highly Selective Nickel Single Atom Catalyst for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO
content:
Development of a novel method for synthesizing Ni single atom catalysts for highly selective electrochemical CO2 reduction in situ. This catalyst achieves 100% selectivity for CO and is formed in an industrially relevant cell architecture. Using post‐mortem XRD, STEM, and EDS and operando XAS, the identity of the active site and the mechanism behind its formation are discovered.








ABSTRACT
Nickel single atom catalysts (Ni‐SACs) perform electrochemical CO2 reduction (ECO2R) with near‐unity selectivity, making them promising new catalysts for future industrial applications. However, modern synthesis methods are long and complicated, preventing large‐scale economic feasibility. This has spurred interest in finding facile, scalable electrochemical pathways to synthesize SACs at ambient temperatures. Here, we propose a mechanism where highly selective Ni‐SACs are generated in situ using a Ni anode as the Ni source. In short, during activation, Ni dissolves from the anode, migrates through the membrane, and electrodeposits as Ni(0) on a nitrogen‐doped carbon precatalyst. When voltage is removed, the deposited Ni disperses to active sites throughout the cathode surface. Using this method, a highly active and selective Ni catalyst is generated in situ, achieving ECO2R selectivity of 100% at ‐2.4 V in chronoamperometric experiments and >90% for 7 h of operation at ‐2.4 V. Using post‐mortem XRD, STEM, EDS, and operando EXAFS, the mechanism for successful generation of the in situ Ni‐SAC was uncovered. This study takes a new look at electrochemical SAC synthesis, offering a scalable pathway that maintains the simplicity of electrodeposition techniques while converting selectivity‐limiting metal clusters into single atom sites through a simple, in situ cell treatment procedure.

title: Robust Spin Splitting and Fermiology in the Layered Altermagnet CoNb4${\rm CoNb}_4$Se8${\rm Se}_8$
content:
The emergence of an altermagnetic phase is demonstrated in the cobalt‐intercalated superconducting 2H‐NbSe2 polymorph. A combined theoretical and experimental approach directly probes the magnetism, the altermagnetic lifting of Kramers degeneracy, and the electronic phase space, establishing CoNb4Se8 as the first g‐wave altermagnetic layered material.








ABSTRACT
Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum‐dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three‐dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination‐resolved micro‐ARPES, fine photon‐energy mapping, spin‐ARPES, and density functional theory, we map the three‐dimensional fermiology of the layered g‐wave altermagnet CoNb4Se8${\rm CoNb}_4{\rm Se}_8$, obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H‐NbSe2${\rm NbSe}_2$. We resolve the spin–split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin‐ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time‐reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry‐protected nodal Γ$\Gamma$–K direction. We further report a weak low‐temperature anomaly near T0 ≈ 50–60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature‐dependent micro‐ARPES, and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum‐resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.

title: Magnetic‐Field‐Annealing‐Induced Short‐Range Order in High‐Entropy Alloys for Enhanced Electromagnetic Response
content:
Magnetic field annealing selectively engineers Co‐centered short‐range order in high‐entropy alloys, as revealed by DFT‐trained atomistic simulations and Warren–Cowley parameter analysis, achieving synergistic modulation of magnetic exchange, polarization relaxation, and impedance matching for multifunctional electromagnetic devices.








ABSTRACT
The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response. Here, magnetic field annealing (MFA) is investigated in rGO‐supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0.5, and 0.95 T. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses. Reflection loss yields a minimum of −72.30 dB at 1.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.40 GHz. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4.08 GHz, corresponding to 92.7% retention of temperature‐specific maxima. Local microscopy, field‐associated atomistic modeling, and fixed‐composition electronic‐structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co‐centered chemical correlations. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration.

title: Vitamin C‐Induced Photo‐Redox Threshold Enables High‐Fidelity Volumetric Printing of Collagen
content:
Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) of native proteins is limited by uncontrolled background crosslinking. Here, vitamin C is introduced as a biocompatible redox regulator to establish a tunable nonlinear polymerization threshold response for TVP. This strategy effectively suppresses background crosslinking and enables high‐fidelity printing of unmodified collagen. Subsequent post‐printing densification yields robust, elastic, and cell‐compatible constructs with enhanced resolution for tissue engineering applications.








ABSTRACT
Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) enables rapid fabrication of complex, centimeter‐scale 3D architectures. TVP of native proteins such as collagen is attractive because it preserves native bioactive motifs that regulate cell–matrix signaling. However, direct TVP of collagen remains challenging because dityrosine crosslinking, driven by visible‐light‐activated Ru(II)bpy32+/sodium persulfate (SPS), lacks an effective inhibitory mechanism. This results in near‐immediate crosslinking upon light exposure, leading to an insufficient nonlinear threshold response that fails to suppress background curing. Here, we introduce vitamin C (L‐ascorbic acid) as a biocompatible redox regulator to overcome this limitation. We demonstrated that vitamin C established a photo‐redox threshold by suppressing Ru(III) accumulation and scavenging persulfate radicals within the Ru/SPS system, thereby delaying dityrosine crosslinking until vitamin C depletion. This threshold generated the nonlinear response required for TVP, enabling high‐fidelity volumetric printing of collagen. Post‐printing construct densification (∼53% shrinkage) further improved feature resolution (80 µm positive; 120 µm negative) and yielded mechanically stable and highly stretchable hydrogels (up to 180% strain). Collagen resin with vitamin C supported both cell seeding post‐printing and cell‐laden printing with high cell density and viability, enabling the rapid biofabrication of cell‐instructive 3D microenvironments.

title: Nanoparticles and Medicine Thirty Years After the First FDA Approval: Time to Renew the Vows
content:
Thirty years after the approval of Doxil, nanomedicine has generated extraordinary scientific output but more limited clinical translation in areas that require selective systemic targeting. Progress increasingly depends on understanding the biological processes that govern biodistribution, tissue access, cellular uptake, intracellular trafficking, and target engagement.








ABSTRACT
Thirty years after the approval of Doxil, nanomedicine has generated extraordinary scientific output and enabled therapeutic modalities that would otherwise have remained impractical. Its clinical translation, however, remains more limited than the scale and sophistication of the field might suggest, particularly when targeted systemic delivery is required. In the recent past, others have highlighted those limitations, however, what concerns us is that some of the assumptions that constrained earlier generations of nanomedicines are now re‐emerging in AAV‐based gene therapy and in vivo CAR‐T platforms. More precise payloads do not make delivery more precise, nor do viral vectors escape the biological barriers encountered by synthetic nanoparticles. In this Perspective, we revisit the liver paradox, the distinction between organ accumulation and functional delivery, the protein corona and the promise of biomimetic systems. Our intention is not to add another catalogue of limitations, but to ask what should change. We argue that the next phase of drug delivery should be less focused on adding complexity to the carrier and more committed to quantifying its biological journey.

title: Tuning Ligand Accessibility via Solvation Entropy for Universal Recovery of Spent Ternary Cathodes
content:
A high‐entropy deep eutectic solvent diversifies local solvation structures and reorganizes ligand‐solvent interactions to enhance ligand accessibility. During rapid cathode dissolution, Ni preferentially associates with oxalate, whereas Co adopts chloride‐dominant coordination, facilitating selective nickel oxalate precipitation and cobalt retention in the leachate. This strategy enables efficient nickel separation from spent NCM cathodes with diverse compositions.








ABSTRACT
Industrial recycling of spent lithium‐ion batteries is challenged by increasingly heterogeneous feedstocks with highly variable cathode compositions. Such compositional fluctuations undermine selective metal separation and necessitate complex process regulation and excessive chemical consumption. In this study, we develop a high‐entropy deep eutectic solvent (HE‐DES) through solvation entropy engineering to regulate ligand accessibility and competitive metal‐ligand interactions. This facilitates the dissolution of Li, Co, and Mn while selectively enriching Ni in recovered solids from diverse spent NCM cathodes. For NCM111, the metal‐normalized Ni fraction reaches 94.40%, with a Ni‐to‐impurity enrichment ratio of 16.86, approximately 3.6 times that of the low‐entropy counterpart. Molecular simulations reveal diversified local solvation structures and reorganized ligand‐solvent associations in HE‐DES, accompanied by enhanced ligand mobility and distinct Ni/Co coordination environments. Meanwhile, the multicomponent solvent regulates ligand‐associated chemical environments at the solid–liquid interface, facilitating selective nickel oxalate formation during cathode dissolution. This work establishes solvent microenvironment engineering as a complementary design principle to conventional ligand engineering, opening new opportunities for selective metal separation in complex multimetal systems.

title: Interfacial Amorphous Lithium Polysulfide Reservoir Design Enables High‐Power and Energy‐Dense All‐Solid‐State Li─S Battery
content:
An ALR is designed to activate the sulfur surface by creating a disordered Li–S interfacial environment, transforming discrete triple‐phase contacts into a point‐to‐surface reaction network. Such ALR can create rapid Li+ conduction and ensure continuous Li+ supply for accelerated solid‐state S/Li2S conversion.








ABSTRACT
All‐solid‐state Li─S batteries (ASSLSBs) promise ultrahigh energy density and safety but suffer from sluggish charge transfer kinetics at the triple‐phase (sulfur, carbon, and solid electrolyte) interface. Herein, we construct an amorphous lithium reservoir (ALR) made of short‐chained lithium polysulfides on sulfur particles to boost the interfacial sulfur redox kinetics and stability, thereby enabling high‐power and energy‐dense performance in ASSLSBs. Spectroscopic analyses (Raman, XPS, NMR, XAFS) reveal the ALR features a disordered Li─S bonding behavior, which store and anchor Li+ ions surrounding the sulfur particles, creating rapid Li+ conduction pathways and ensuring continuous Li+ supply for accelerated S/Li2S conversion. Consequently, the ASSLSBs exhibit superior rate capability, achieving a high reversible capacity of 1115 mAh g−1 at 1C and 732.8 mAh g−1 at 2C, respectively, as well as excellent cycling stability with an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.049% per cycle after 1000 cycles at 1C. Moreover, the ALR design also demonstrate a high practical capacity of 12.8 mAh cm−2 under high sulfur loading of 10 mg cm−2, suggesting its promise to resolve the longstanding kinetics issue and paves a practical path for future high‐energy‐density ASSLSBs.
