title: NET‐Inhibiting Bio‐Orthogonal Gelated Neutrophils Reverse Maladaptive Trained Immunity and Protect Against Periodontitis Recurrence
content:
To reverse NET‐mediated MTI, we engineered tPA@AGNs‐DNase I through metabolic glycoengineering and click chemistry. This biomaterial platform cleared NETs in situ by degrading existing NETs and disrupting fibrin–neutrophil engagement. Local administration of tPA@AGNs‐DNase I reversed bone marrow epigenetic reprogramming, resolved primary inflammation, and blunted secondary hyperinflammation and bone loss.








ABSTRACT
Maladaptive trained immunity (MTI) establishes pathogenic innate immune memory that amplifies the immune response to recurrent chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, but erasing this memory remains challenging. In this study, we identified neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) as key mediators of periodontitis‐induced MTI that reprogrammed bone marrow epigenetics and transcriptomics to amplify inflammation upon secondary challenge. Thus, we designed a NET‐inhibiting bioengineered platform (tPA@AGNs‐DNase I) to erase MTI and prevent recurrent inflammation. This platform was constructed by encapsulating tPA within activated gelated neutrophils (AGNs) and conjugating DNase I onto the surface by glycoengineering and click chemistry. Leveraging the inflammation‐homing property of AGNs, the platform enabled co‐delivery of two enzymes: DNase I degraded the DNA scaffold of NETs, while tPA disrupted fibrin‒neutrophil engagement to block NETosis, thereby achieving synergistic NET clearance. Local periodontal administration of tPA@AGNs‐DNase I not only resolved primary inflammation but also reversed established MTI by restoring aberrant bone marrow epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming, thereby markedly attenuating recurrent hyperinflammation and alveolar bone loss in a religature‐induced periodontitis model. Collectively, this work provides a bioengineered platform that erases central MTI via in situ NET clearance, offering a paradigm‐shifting strategy to control chronic inflammatory disease recurrence.

title: An Inflammation‐Responsive and Biodegradable Microneedle Patch for Periodontal Soft and Hard Tissue Regeneration via Temporally Coordinated Sustained Release of Hydrogen and Calcium Ions
content:
For local adjunctive treatment of periodontitis, this study develops a microneedle delivery system by integrating poly(lactic‐co‐glycolic acid) microspheres encapsulating CaSi2 into an inflammation‐responsive microneedle matrix. The system enables lesion‐triggered release followed by sustained intervention, alleviates oxidative stress and inflammatory imbalance, effectively suppresses alveolar bone resorption, and simultaneously promotes osteogenesis, cell migration, and angiogenesis, thereby facilitating periodontal tissue repair.








ABSTRACT
Periodontitis progression is driven by a self‐perpetuating pathological microenvironment that couples inflammation, oxidative stress, osteoimmune disruption, and impaired regeneration, leading to alveolar bone resorption and periodontal tissue destruction. To address this challenge, we developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive microneedle system (CaSi2@PLGA MNs). By integrating CaSi2@PLGA microspheres, formed by encapsulating calcium silicide (CaSi2) in poly(lactic‐co‐glycolic acid) (PLGA), into a ROS‐responsive microneedle matrix, we established a temporally coordinated therapeutic strategy featuring hierarchical release that couples two sequential processes: rapid microsphere release triggered by the inflammatory microenvironment, followed by gradual microsphere hydrolysis to enable sustained H2 and Ca2+ delivery over several days. This staged delivery enables an orderly transition from early periodontal inflammation to longer‐term tissue regeneration and repair. In vitro, the microspheres alleviated macrophage oxidative stress, promoted macrophage polarization toward a repair‐associated phenotype, and further supported osteogenic differentiation, cell migration, and angiogenesis. In vivo, CaSi2@PLGA MNs improved the periodontal inflammatory status, reduced alveolar bone resorption, promoted collagen remodeling and regeneration‐related marker expression, thereby demonstrating periodontal tissue repair potential. Overall, this study establishes a temporally coordinated local‐delivery platform that integrates inflammation control with regenerative support, providing a promising adjunctive strategy for periodontitis and demonstrating potential for extension to other inflammation‐associated osteolytic diseases.

title: Three‐Dimensional In Situ Tunable Mechanical Metamaterials
content:
Two types of gear‐based 3D mechanical metamaterials are reported that achieve in situ, continuous, and reversible tuning of triaxial stiffness over a wide range (∼30 times) via synchronous rotation. By integrating spherical or face gears, either the orthogonal stiffness or the nonlinear behavior is controlled in 3D space, enabling robust, programmable static and dynamic properties.








ABSTRACT
Mechanical metamaterials with in situ, smooth, and broad‐range tunability of stiffness are highly anticipated in engineering, but existing designs are limited to unidirectional or bidirectional control. As the stiffness lacks the multi‐directional coupling effect for shape morphing, creating three‐dimensional (3D) metamaterials with triaxial tunability remains challenging in configuration design, fabrication, and actuation. Here we create two types of gear‐based 3D mechanical metamaterials that achieve in situ, wide‐range, continuous, reversible tunability of 3D stiffness. The first uses spherical gears containing ellipsoidal cavities as the variable‐stiffness components, while the second conceives planetary‐like 3D gear assemblies as the metacell. They feature orthotropic stiffness in three axes—all can be tuned in situ by about 30 times via synchronous rotation. Moreover, the nonlinear buckling properties are also tunable in 3D space. The integrated actuation methods are conceived to achieve robust and smooth control. We clarify the principles and demonstrate the properties of 3D in situ tunability by analytical, numerical, and experimental methods. Therefore, this work systematically proves the possibility of programmable metamaterials with in situ 3D tunability, offering feasible ways for conceiving advanced structures with actively controllable 3D static and dynamic properties.

title: Buckled Silver Microflake Conductors With In Situ‐Generated Ag–O Coordination Enable 3D‐Printed Stretchable Cardiac Bioelectrodes
content:
In situ‐generated Ag–O coordination regulates stress distribution and suppresses crack propagation, maintaining conductive networks under deformation. A synergistic strategy enables stretchable, electrically stable cardiac electrodes by integrating AgMF inks with biaxial buckling and wet‐adhesive hydrogels. The 3D‐printable electrodes exhibit high conductivity and stable resistance under 50% strain, enabling puncture‐free cardiac interfaces for long‐term biosensing applications.








ABSTRACT
Metallic pacemaker electrodes risk myocardial injury during implantation, while silver micro‐flakes (AgMFs), despite excellent conductivity, are too rigid for stretchable devices without proper composite/device engineering. Here, we present a synergistic strategy to fabricate fully stretchable, electrically stable, and crack‐resistant cardiac electrodes by integrating AgMF‐based ink with metal‐organic interfacial bonding, biaxial buckling, and wet‐adhesive hydrogels. In situ‐generated Ag–O coordination of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) in the polymer matrix/conductor dissipates stress and suppresses crack propagation, effectively compensating for AgMF rigidity and enabling intact buckled microstructures. The resulting electrodes exhibit high conductivity (∼2.1 × 104 S cm−1) and stable resistance under 50% cyclic strain, exceeding cardiac motion requirements (15%–20%). The ink is 3D‐printable into mesh electrodes and can be integrated with wet‐adhesive hydrogels to form puncture‐free, stretchable metallic cardiac bioelectrodes with excellent biosafety, offering a promising route toward leadless pacemakers and long‐term wireless cardiac monitoring. A multiscale synergistic strategy integrating metal‐organic interfacial bonding with stretch‐release‐induced buckled architectures enables silver microflake conductors with simultaneously high conductivity and large deformability, demonstrated for 3D printing of bioadaptive, puncture‐free cardiac electrodes and stretchable wireless coils for dynamic cardiac stimulation and long‐term electrophysiological monitoring.

title: Synergistic Lewis Base Organocatalysis and Electrocatalysis for the Enantioselective Construction of α‐Fluorinated Quaternary Stereocenters
content:
Combining chiral isothiourea (ITU) organocatalysis with electrochemistry enables the enantioselective radical cross‐coupling of fluorinated acetic esters with silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. This synergistic strategy generates α‐carbonyl tertiary radicals via anodic oxidation of C1‐ammonium enolates and constructs sterically congested α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters in high yields (up to 95%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee), offering a sustainable platform for valuable chiral fluorinated molecules.








ABSTRACT
The construction of α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters—a structural motif of high value in pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules—remains a formidable synthetic challenge due to inherent steric and stereoelectronic constraints. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy combining chiral isothiourea (ITU) organocatalysis with electrochemistry, enabling the direct and highly enantioselective α‐alkylation of bench‐stable fluorinated acetic esters with both silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. This approach integrates anodic single‐electron oxidation with asymmetric Lewis base catalysis, converting in situ‐generated disubstituted C1‐ammonium enolates into configurationally well‐defined, chiral ITU‐bound α‐carbonyl tertiary radical intermediates. Subsequent stereocontrolled radical cross‐coupling with SOMOphilic partners furnishes a broad range of esters bearing α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters in high yields (up to 95%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). This work not only fills a significant gap in the single‐electron chemistry of disubstituted C1‐ammonium enolates but also provides a versatile platform for the rapid assembly of optically active α‐fluorinated quaternary carbonyl compounds, with significant potential in drug discovery and complex molecule synthesis.

title: Black Titanium‐Oxo Cluster as a Dual‐Mode Catalyst for Regioselective Protein Editing
content:
A structurally engineered titanium‐oxo cluster enables both photooxidative and hydrolytic modification of β‐lactoglobulin—driving selective ROS‐mediated oxidation under irradiation and protein hydrolysis at elevated temperatures.








ABSTRACT
Atomically precise titanium‐oxo clusters are discrete molecular analogues of TiO2 and structural building blocks of many metal–organic frameworks. Combining features of homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, they provide a versatile platform for catalyst design. However, due to limited stability in aqueous media, they remain largely unexplored in biologically relevant catalysis. Here, we report a structurally engineered hexanuclear titanium‐oxo cluster (tBu‐Ti6) with promising photophysical properties, including a very low optical gap of 1.56 eV. Using β‐lactoglobulin as a model protein, we demonstrate that tBu‐Ti6 is an effective heterogeneous catalyst in aqueous solution, promoting both hydrolytic and photooxidative protein cleavage via two distinct pathways: Lewis acid‐mediated hydrolysis and reactive oxygen species‐driven photocatalysis. Nano‐scale liquid chromatography‐tandem mass spectrometry (nLC‐MS/MS) reveals preferential cleavage near negatively charged regions of the protein, indicating electrostatic substrate recognition. Under 370 nm irradiation, tBu‐Ti6 induces oxidation of tyrosine, tryptophan, and methionine residues in the intact β‐lactoglobulin, underscoring its potential as a photocatalyst for selective protein modifications. During reactions in aqueous solutions, the cluster remains structurally intact, shows no decomposition or dissolution, and is reusable without loss of activity. Together, these results establish TOCs as versatile molecular catalysts for controlled protein modifications and underscore their potential in bioinspired catalysis.

title: Rational Design of a Chiral Hybrid Ge(II) Halide With Giant Chiroptical Activity for Circularly Polarized Light Detection
content:
Due to the stereochemical activity of the Ge2+ 4s2 lone‐pair, the strong lone‐pair expression in chiral hybrid (R/S‐MBA)GeI3 halides induces remarkable chirality‐favoring distortions, including a large asymmetric bond angle variance and projected deflection angle of the chiral [–Ge–I–]∞ chains. These structural distortions collectively enhance the intrinsic chiroptical activity, enabling high‐performance circularly polarized light detection.








ABSTRACT
Chiral hybrid metal halides integrate semiconducting optoelectronic functionality with intrinsic chirality, offering new opportunities in the field of next‐generation chiral photonics and spintronics. However, the incorporation of chiral organic ligands alone is often insufficient to induce pronounced chiral structural distortions, thereby limiting the resulting chiroptical activity. Herein, we demonstrate for the first time that the stereochemically active 4s2 lone‐pair of Ge2+ can serve as an internal structural amplifier of chirality. We rationally designed and synthesized a pair of enantiomeric chiral hybrid Ge(II) halides, denoted as (R/S‐MBA)GeI3 (MBA is methylbenzylammonium). Specifically, the strong lone‐pair expression in (R/S‐MBA)GeI3 drives significant chirality‐favorable distortions, manifested by a large asymmetric bond angle variance and projected deflection angle of the chiral [−Ge−I−]∞ chains. This enhanced structural chirality increases the circular dichroism (CD) anisotropy factor (gCD) of (R/S‐MBA)GeI3 to 2.66 times that of the Pb(II) homologs. Benefiting from the superior chiroptical activity, (R/S‐MBA)GeI3 further exhibits second‐harmonic generation (SHG)‐CD anisotropy factor (gSHG‐CD) values of −1.17/1.09, while the corresponding devices achieve photocurrent anisotropy factors (gIph) of −0.403/0.391. Finally, we demonstrated a proof‐of‐concept circularly polarized light‐encrypted optical communication system. Our work provides a new insight into the rational design of high‐performance chiral functional materials.

title: Rare‐Earth‐Modulated Fe–Tb Dual‐Metal Single‐Atom Site Catalyst Enables Enhanced Activity and Durability for Acidic Oxygen Reduction
content:
Leveraging the oxophilicity of rare‐earth elements, a rare‐earth‐modulated Fe─Tb dual‐metal single‐atom site catalyst was designed for proton exchange membrane fuel cells. The neighboring Tb single‐atom acts as an “intermediate director” that promotes *OH desorption from Fe─N4 sites, alleviates high *OH coverage, and thereby enables stable and efficient acidic ORR.








ABSTRACT
The critical dependence on Pt in proton‐exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a bottleneck for commercialization. Single‐atom‐site catalysts, such as Fe‐NC, show comparable activity for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in PEMFCs, yet their inferior stability constrains practical applications. In this work, we introduced the rare‐earth element Tb as a single‐atom site into the Fe‐NC system and constructed a dual‐metal single‐atom site catalyst (denoted as FeTb‐NC). Theoretical calculations and experiments suggest that Tb centers, with strong oxophilicity and unique electronic structure, synergistically regulate *OH binding on adjacent FeN4 sites, thereby lowering the energy barrier for *OH desorption. This elevates the activity of Fe centers and, more importantly, significantly lowers *OH coverage on FeN4, mitigating its detrimental effects. The optimized FeTb‐NC catalyst displays improved performance: The half‐wave potential is as high as 0.89 V (vs. RHE), retaining 88% of its initial current density after 100 h at 0.8 V. The PEMFC assembled with FeTb‐NC as the cathode catalyst exhibits competitive performance and durability; the peak power density reaches 1.10 W cm−2 under H2/O2 conditions, and the device maintains 80% current‐density retention after 100 h under H2/air conditions. This work offers new insights into performance optimization of Fe–NC‐based materials and supports development of Pt‐free PEMFCs.

title: Concentration‐Driven Solvation Reorganization Featuring Viologen Clustering Enables Air‐Tolerant Aqueous Organic Redox Flow Batteries
content:
Molecular‐salt concentration induces viologen solvation transition, thereby improving redox stability in aqueous organic redox‐flow batteries under ambient air.








ABSTRACT
Viologen derivatives are promising anolytes in aqueous organic redox‐flow batteries (AORFBs), but long‐term stability under ambient air remains challenging. Using 1,1′‐bis[3‐(trimethylammonio)propyl]‐4,4′‐bipyridinium tetrachloride (BVCl4), we show through physicochemical characterization and molecular dynamics simulations that increasing BV concentration beyond a critical threshold induces a solvation transition characterized by viologen clustering. Controlled O2 exposure of bulk‐electrolyzed BV4+/BV3+• solutions using a carbon felt electrode, together with air‐exposed AORFB full‐cell cycling, shows that BV is converted to redox‐inactive byproducts via OH–/reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by BV3+•‐O2 galvanic reactions and electrode‐driven hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The degradation is suppressed in a nonmonotonic manner governed by the solvation‐transition threshold. We suggest that the enhanced air tolerance of concentrated BV electrolytes arises from this solvation reorganization, associated with viologen‐clustering‐induced steric shielding against O2/OH−/ROS attack and restricted BV hydration that limits Grotthuss‐type OH− transport to reactive BV sites. Additionally, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance measurements at an Au electrode directly visualize BV2+ as the most degradation‐prone state, forming redox‐inactive deposits through reactions with OH−/ROS generated locally by HER and oxygen reduction reaction; this pathway is strongly attenuated once electrolyte solvation reorganizes. Voltammetry at an Au ultramicroelectrode further reveals that solvation‐transition‐driven clustering suppresses BV3+• disproportionation.

title: Surfactant‐Induced Morphology Reconstruction for High‐Performance Near‐Infrared Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
content:
A homologous series of hydroxyl‐functional quaternary ammonium surfactants reveals how alkyl‐chain length governs perovskite crystallization, morphology, photon extraction, and charge transport. An intermediate chain length provides the optimal balance of these effects, enabling near‐infrared PeLEDs with a peak EQE of 27.0% and strongly suppressed efficiency roll‐off.








ABSTRACT
High‐performance near‐infrared (NIR) perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) require the simultaneous suppression of nonradiative recombination and efficient photon extraction, in which additive often play a vital role. However, molecular design rules that connect additive structure with both crystallization control and optical morphology remain poorly defined. Here, we employ a series of hydroxyl‐functional quaternary ammonium surfactants—TMPAC, HDPAC, and DDPAC—with different alkyl‐chain lengths while retaining a common polar headgroup. This molecular design reveals how hydrophobic‐tail length regulates precursor organization and governs the balance among emissive quality, optical outcoupling, and charge transport. Increasing the alkyl‐chain length alters the phase‐conversion kinetics, suppresses lateral grain coalescence, and promotes anisotropic out‐of‐plane growth, thereby producing corrugated FAPbI3 films. The intermediate‐chain HDPAC provides sufficient interfacial organization to improve radiative efficiency and photon extraction while maintaining favorable charge‐transport balance. HDPAC‐based devices achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 27.0%, exhibit markedly suppressed efficiency roll‐off, and deliver a maximum radiance exceeding 513 W sr−1 m−2. These results establish hydrophobic‐tail length as an effective molecule‐level modulator for coupling interfacial crystallization control with photon management in perovskite emitters.

title: Photoinduced Homolytic Carbon–Palladium Bond Cleavage of Zwitterionic π‐Allylpalladium Species and Annulation with 1,3‐Dienes and 1,3‐Enynes
content:
A distinctive annulation pathway for zwitterionic π‐allylpalladium(II) species has been established through visible‐light‐triggered homolytic cleavage of the C–Pd bond, radical addition to alkenes, recombination with Pd(I), and Pd(II)‐mediated conversion. The protocol possesses broad substrate compatibility, delivering various functionalized cyclic frameworks efficiently.








ABSTRACT
The zwitterionic π‐allylpalladium species are versatile intermediates in modern annulation chemistry, yet their assembling partners have been largely limited to electrophilic reagents or dipolarophiles. Herein, we report a previously inaccessible (4 + 2) annulation reaction of common π‐allylpalladium(II) dipoles with electron‐neutral 1,3‐dienes and 1‐aryl‐substituted 1,3‐enynes via a distinct cooperative photo‐induced pathway. Mechanistic studies indicate that the process proceeds through visible light‐promoted homolytic cleavage of the allylic C–Pd bond to generate Pd(I) and allylic radicals, which undergo addition to polyunsaturated systems. Subsequent Pd(I)–radical recombination and intramolecular allylic substitution furnish a broad array of multifunctional oxa‐ and aza‐heterocycles, as well as carbocyclic frameworks, in moderate to good yields. In addition, their assemblies with electron‐poor dienes are also applicable, whereas the regioselectivity is distinct from that observed in traditional dipole‐based annulations. Furthermore, the asymmetric version is successful by employing chiral bisphosphine ligands, with fair to good enantioselectivity achieved.

title: Programmable Amino Migration−Enabled Diversification of Allylamines
content:
A programmable radical migration strategy transforms allylamines into versatile synthons for divergent molecular construction. Controlled interception of a common translocated radical intermediate through complementary radical capture, atom−transfer radical addition (ATRA), and radical−polar crossover (RPC) pathways enables modular 1,2,3−trifunctionalization, providing rapid access to densely functionalized, C(sp3)−rich amino architectures.








ABSTRACT
Migration−enabled alkene functionalization offers an attractive strategy for accessing molecular architectures beyond the reach of conventional alkene transformations. Yet existing approaches typically channel translocated radical intermediates into a single reaction manifold, limiting the broader potential of migration chemistry for divergent synthesis. Here, we establish a programmable migration−enabled synthesis platform that redirects allylamines from passive alkene substrates into versatile synthons for divergent molecular construction. Through the integration of radical functionalization with amino migration, this strategy generates a migratory radical intermediate that undergoes selective diversification via complementary radical−trapping, atom−transfer radical addition (ATRA), and radical−polar crossover (RPC) pathways under mild photocatalytic conditions, enabling divergent 1,2,3−trifunctionalization of allylamines. Broad compatibility with radical precursors, bifunctional reagents, nucleophiles, and diverse allylamine scaffolds provides access to more than 70 densely functionalized, C(sp3)−rich amino architectures, including molecules bearing quaternary carbon centers. More broadly, this work establishes radical migration as a programmable design principle for molecular diversification and expands the synthetic utility of allylamines as modular synthons for the systematic exploration of structure−function relationships.

title: Gold‐Catalyzed “Anti‐Baldwin” Cyclization of Unactivated Alkenes
content:
A rare example of kinetically disfavored 5‐endo‐trig cyclization of unactivated alkenes is disclosed. The key to the success of this transformation is that the kinetically favored 4‐exo‐trig cyclization is reversible, thereby enabling equilibration to the thermodynamically favored 5‐endo‐trig cyclization intermediate, which then undergoes reductive elimination to form the product.








ABSTRACT
Owing to the unfavorable orbital alignments and geometric constraints, 5‐endo‐trig cyclizations are kinetically disfavored as stated by Sir Jack Baldwin. Consequently, reports of such cyclization are scarce and primarily rely on the use of activated alkenes. Herein, we report a rare example of “anti‐Baldwin” cyclization of unactivated alkenes. The key to the success of this transformation is that the kinetically favored 4‐exo‐trig cyclization is reversible, thereby enabling equilibration to the thermodynamically favored 5‐endo‐trig cyclization intermediate, which then undergoes reductive elimination to form the product.

title: Short‐Range Molecular Ordering Enables Efficient and Stable Recombination Junction in Monolithic Perovskite/CIGS Tandem Solar Cells
content:
A short‐range ordered molecular architecture is developed for the recombination junction in monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells. Locally ordered domains facilitate charge transport, while the surrounding disordered regions suppress ion migration. The resulting devices achieve a certified efficiency of 28.94% and retain 98% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point (MPP) tracking.








ABSTRACT
Monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells have made remarkable progress in recent years and are highly promising for next‐generation photovoltaics. The recombination junction (RJ) linking the top and bottom subcells is an essential component that governs both device efficiency and operational stability. However, depositing a uniform RJ on the complex CIGS substrate while simultaneously achieving charge transport and operational robustness remains a formidable challenge. Here, we construct a short‐range ordered (SRO) hole‐selective architecture for the RJ by exploiting π–π interactions between a self‐assembled molecule (SAM) and a polymeric SAM (PCCP). The SRO architecture shortens the intermolecular π–π stacking distance to accelerate carrier transport, while the surrounding amorphous regions effectively interrupt ion migration pathways. Furthermore, this strategy enables conformal coverage over the complex CIGS topography, improves interfacial robustness, and enhances structural resilience in service. Consequently, monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells employing the SRO‐RJ achieve a maximum power conversion efficiency of 29.60% (certified 28.94%, 0.2036 cm2) and retain 98% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking. Our findings establish short‐range molecular ordering as an effective strategy for engineering efficient and durable recombination junctions in monolithic tandem photovoltaics.

title: PCET beyond pKa: Disaggregation and Additional Base Effects as Neglected Key Factors for Unlocking Inaccessible Substrates in Direct Intermolecular Photocatalytic Ring‐Opening Remote Alkylation of Cycloalkanols
content:
Base effects beyond simple pKa relations enable redox‐neutral ring opening of nonactivated cycloalkanols for remote Giese alkylations from previously inaccessible substrates. In‐depth NMR studies have revealed the critical importance of the aggregation state and alcohol–base pre‐organization to govern reactivity in such oxidative multisite proton‐coupled electron transfer reactions (MS‐PCET).








ABSTRACT
Photocatalytic oxidative multisite proton‐coupled electron transfer (MS‐PCET) reactions have emerged as a promising tool for the activation of strong O─H bonds in (cyclo)alkanols. However, these methods often require the use of e‐rich arene‐containing derivatives (para‐methoxyphenyl (PMP), etc.) — a factor that greatly restricts their broader applicability. In this study, we report the successful implementation of targeted modulation of the base partner in photocatalytic cascade reactions of cyclic alcohols, unlocking previously rather inaccessible, nonactivated substrates. This approach successfully bypasses the prevalent limitations of ring‐opening transformations of cycloalkanols by disaggregation of the bulk alcohol and strategic base selection. As a result, we here demonstrate an operationally simple and widely applicable protocol for the redox‐neutral transformations of cycloalkanols into terminally C(sp3)‐C(sp3)‐coupled, functionalized open‐chain products. NMR‐based mechanistic studies, comprising in‐depth H‐bond analysis as well as DOSY and ROESY experiments, have elucidated the previously unrecognized crucial role of substrate disaggregation in this multisite PCET, along with (pyridine) base effects surpassing typical pKa‐related and/or steric effects. Ultimately, our insights, for the first time, reveal the critical importance of the aggregation state and the design of productive alcohol‐base pre‐organization beyond pKa and enabled us to successfully pioneer remote alkylative Giese‐type C─C‐bond formations of previously challenging alkyl‐substituted cycloalkanols.

title: Safranine T‐Derived Activable Photosensitizer to Synergistically Regulate the RSS/ROS Dynamic Equilibrium for Boosted Photosensitization
content:
A reactive sulfur species (RSS)‐activatable photosensitizer triggers a three‐step synergistic cascade: RSS consumption (Stage I), Photodynamic therapy (PDT) activation (Stage II), and massive reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst (Stage III). This three‐stage synergistic cascade remodels intracellular RSS/ROS redox homeostasis, thereby dismantling tumor redox tolerance and greatly enhancing the therapeutic potency of PDT.








ABSTRACT
Photodynamic therapy (PDT) eliminates lesions like tumors via reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐mediated oxidative damage. However, tumors overexpress reactive sulfur species (RSS) that scavenge cytotoxic ROS, endowing cancer cells with strong antioxidant resistance and weakening PDT efficacy. We fabricated a biosafe, readily available activatable photosensitizer ST‐DNBS based on safranine T (ST). ST‐DNBS selectively consumes RSS overexpressed in tumors and recovers photochemically active ST to produce massive ROS. For example, 6 µM ST‑DNBS depletes substantial glutathione (GSH), leading to a marked reduction in the characteristic absorbance of TNB2− (5‐thio‐2‐nitrobenzoate dianion) at 412 nm in the DTNB (Ellman's reagent) assay relative to the control; ROS produced after 24 s of irradiation causes a 6.2‐fold decrease in the UV absorbance of 1,3‐diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF). Tumor‐activatable ST‐DNBS depletes intracellular RSS to collapse tumor antioxidant systems, blocking ROS clearance and boosting intracellular ROS buildup. This RSS/ROS redox balance remodeling greatly enhances photodynamic activity, achieving a 90% tumor inhibition rate. Our RSS‐scavenging, tumor‐activated photosensitizer offers a practical strategy to overcome tumor antioxidant barriers and improve PDT antitumor performance.

title: Selective Reductive Amination of Long‐Chain Diols to Primary Diamines Over Nitrogen‐Modulated Ru0/Ruδ+ Dual Sites
content:
Selective reductive amination of long‐chain bio‐diols to primary diamines is enabled by N‐modulated Ru0/Ruδ+ dual sites. Cooperative O─H and Cα─H activation accelerates rate‐determining diol dehydrogenation, while interfacial Ru‐Nx coordination weakens NH3 adsorption and suppresses carbon deposition, delivering 98.5% 1,9‐nonanediamine yield with durable ten‐cycle stability.








ABSTRACT
Linear primary diamines (DAs) are essential monomers for nylon and polyamide. Sustainable production of DAs from bio‐diols via reductive amination (RA) requires to achieve the tandem diols dehydrogenation (rate‐determining), aldimine condensation and imine hydrogenation, which remains challenging due to low efficiency, poor selectivity, and rapid catalyst deactivation under ammonia‐rich conditions. In this study, we report an efficient and durable catalytic system for the RA of linear primary bio‐diols to DAs by constructing a Run‐Nx‐C catalyst with N‐modulated Ru0/Ruδ+ dual sites. In the RA of 1,9‐nonanediol, a high yield of 1,9‐nonanediamine up to 98.5% is achieved under mild conditions (170°C, 0.3 MPa H2, 0.7 MPa NH3) for at least 10 cycles. Mechanistic studies reveal that Ruδ+ and Ru0 sites cooperatively drive diol dehydrogenation through O─H and Cα─H bond activation, respectively, while their synergistic interplay further promotes the subsequent RA toward DAs formation. DFT and AIMD simulations reveal that N‐modulated Ruδ+ sites exhibit weaker NH3 adsorption than pristine Ruδ+ surfaces, thereby mitigating the excessive deposition of imine‐derived intermediates and improving catalytic stability. Run‐Nx‐C was further evaluated for the conversion of selected biomass‐ and polyester‐derived substrates into value‐added DAs.

title: Engineering Synthetic Molecular Operations Controlled by DNA‐Binding Proteins Through Templated Proximity
content:
DNA‐binding proteins are harnessed as programmable interfaces that control synthetic molecular operations through templated proximity. Protein recognition induces spatial colocalization of split DNA components, triggering DNA strand displacement reactions that translate biological inputs into programmable nucleic acid processes. This strategy enables DBPs to perform modular bespoke operations, linking natural biomolecular recognition to synthetic information processing networks.








ABSTRACT
We describe a DNA‐based molecular framework that enables DNA‐binding proteins (DBPs) to perform diverse synthetic operations beyond their natural functions. We introduce templated proximity as a mechanism through which DBP–DNA recognition events are converted into programmable DNA strand displacement reactions. In this architecture, protein binding templates the spatial colocalization of split DNA components, generating functional nucleic acid outputs that can be propagated into downstream processes. Using representative DBPs, including EGR1, YY1, and p53, we couple protein recognition to DNA strand displacement, activation of a fluorogenic RNA aptamer, regulation of CRISPR–Cas12a and Cas13 activity, and DBP‐triggered activation of hierarchical CRISPR cascades. These results establish templated proximity as a general transduction principle for integrating DNA‐binding proteins into modular nucleic acid reaction networks and demonstrate that DBPs can function as programmable interfaces connecting natural biomolecular recognition with engineered DNA‐based information processing, enabling modular communication layers with tailored synthetic functionality.

title: Selective Oxidation of Toluene to Benzaldehyde Driven by Electroreduction of Oxygen to Hydrogen Peroxide Coupled With In Situ Electro‐Fenton Reaction
content:
Cathodic electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide from oxygen reduction is coupled with in situ electro‐Fenton reaction for selective oxidization of toluene to benzaldehyde, establishing a novel electrochemical process for the oxidation of inert C─H bonds.








ABSTRACT
Selective toluene oxidation is a pivotal reaction in the fine chemical industry. While electrooxidation at high anodic potentials shows promise, the low efficiency of the generation of reactive oxygen species limits the product yield. Herein, we describe a cathodic strategy for selective oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde via coupling the electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide from oxygen reduction with an in situ electro‐Fenton reaction (eH2O2‐EF). Among the different metal–nitrogen–carbon single‐atom catalysts (M‐NC SAC, M = Fe, Co, and Ni), Co‐NC SAC stands out as the best catalyst, featuring a benzaldehyde selectivity of 90.63% and a yield of 21.9 mmol gcat−1$g_{cat}^{ - 1}$ h−1 at −0.3 V versus RHE with stable operation over 23 cycles. In situ spectroscopy and radical scavenging and quantification experiments indicate that the eH2O2‐EF proceeds via toluene adsorption, ·OH‐mediated oxidation, and desorption of products, where the ·OH generation and intermediate adsorption/desorption jointly determine the benzaldehyde yield. Theoretical analysis indicates that the Co‐NC SAC thermodynamically facilitates H2O2 generation, accompanied by moderate benzaldehyde adsorption and an uphill further‐oxidation step, leading to selective benzaldehyde production. This work establishes a novel cathodic paradigm for the selective oxidation of inert aromatic Csp3${{C}_{s{{p}^3}}}$‐H bonds under mild conditions.

title: Covalent Organic Framework‐Templated Spatial Confinement of Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
We reported a covalent organic framework (COF)‐templated spatial confinement (CTSC) strategy to regulate self‐assembled monolayers in inverted perovskite solar cells; through suppressing molecular aggregation and improving buried interface uniformity, CTSC promotes compact perovskite growth, reduces interfacial recombination, and enables a best efficiency of 27.03% with enhanced long‐term stability. 








ABSTRACT
Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as efficient hole‐contacting layers for p‐i‐n perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and weak bonding with the substrate result in heterogeneous buried interfaces. Herein, a covalent organic framework (COF)‐templated spatial confinement (CTSC) strategy is developed by employing a newly designed phosphonate–carbazole‐based COF, namely COF‐TPACz, to regulate the buried interface. The nanoscale island‐like COF domains could restrict the penetration of aggregated SAM molecules and allow well‐distributed ones to anchor on exposed substrates. Meanwhile, hydrogen‐bonding and π–π interactions between COF‐TPACz and SAM favor a more uniform molecular arrangement on the COF domains. These adjustments synergistically suppress molecular aggregation and improve surface coverage, yielding a denser and more homogeneous SAM interface. Furthermore, the improved interface optimizes upper perovskite crystallization, promotes compact and vertically extended grains, and strengthens buried interfacial contact, thereby suppressing nonradiative recombination and facilitating charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the CTSC‐based PSCs achieve a peak efficiency of 27.03%, together with enhanced long‐term stability. We believe these findings provide a conceptual advance for realizing homogeneous SAM via spatial confinement and a viable route toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Ligand‐Engineered Metal‐Organic‐Covalent‐Organic Frameworks Enable Red‐Light‐Driven H2O2 Photosynthesis and Tunable Biomass Upgrading
content:
Ligand‑engineered isostructural Ru‑based MOCOFs are reported for efficient red‑light‑driven H2O2 photosynthesis coupled with biomass upgrading. Tuning the local coordination environment of Ru(II) centers modulates intersystem‑crossing efficiency, steering competing OO bond‑cleavage pathways of peroxide intermediates to deliver controllable product selectivity toward PN or FN derivatives.








ABSTRACT
Harvesting low‐energy photons, particularly in the deep‐red and near‐infrared regions, for artificial photosynthesis remains a significant challenge due to the inherent difficulty in driving multi‐electron redox processes with limited photon energy. Herein, we reported a tunable ligand engineering strategy to construct a series of isostructural metal‐organic‐covalent‐organic frameworks (MOCOFs), namely MOCOF‐phenx (x = 0, 1, 2 and 3). By gradient increasing the number of phenanthroline ligands around the Ru(II) center, we precisely modulated the electronic structures and excited‐state properties of the resulting MOCOFs. Remarkably, the ligand‐engineered MOCOFs showed excellent red‐light‐driven H2O2 generation coupled with switchable biomass upgrading, in which the reaction selectivity of furfuryl alcohol oxidation was profoundly governed. MOCOF‐phen0 preferentially affords 6‐hydroxy‐2H‐pyran‐3(6H)‐one (PN) with 91.4% selectivity, whereas MOCOF‐phen3 steers the reaction towards 5‐hydroxy‐2,5‐dihydrofuran‐2‐one (FN). This work establishes a molecular‐level design blueprint for low‐energy‐light‐driven photocatalysis, demonstrating ligand engineering in crystalline framework materials for optimizing activity and selectivity towards sustainable photosynthesis.

title: Autonomous Scanning Electrochemical Cell Microscopy Enables Rapid Exploration of Large Compositionally Complex Material Spaces
content:
An autonomous robotic scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) platform combines active learning with automated library exchange to navigate vast composition spaces of compositionally complex materials. Applied to Au–Ir–Rh, the platform predicts full voltammetric responses across 966 compositions, learning the composition–activity relationship after measuring only 15% of the libraries.








ABSTRACT
Alloying is a central strategy in electrocatalysis, enabling fine‐tuning of the electronic structure. In particular, compositionally complex solid solutions (CCSSs), often called high‐entropy alloys, are of high interest. However, the “combinatorial explosion” in the number of possible compositions poses a critical bottleneck for the discovery of CCSS electrocatalysts. We present an autonomous scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) system for ultrahigh‐throughput and large‐scale CCSS activity screening. The platform rapidly establishes composition–activity relationships across multiple thin‐film CCSS materials libraries via active learning and automated library exchange. Embedding analytical expressions of voltammetry in the algorithm enables the learning of whole voltammograms rather than a single selected metric. As a demonstration, we investigated hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activities of Au–Ir–Rh, where Ir and Rh exhibit strong metal‐hydrogen binding and Au exhibits weak binding as derived from the HER volcano plot. The activity trend was accurately predicted after measuring only 15% of all 966 measurement areas. Au30Ir20Rh50 and Au10Ir35Rh55 exhibit the highest activities with standard rate constants of ∼0.012 cm s−1, demonstrating positive synergistic contributions from elemental mixing. The proposed platform is broadly applicable to a wide range of electrocatalytic reactions, providing a general pathway for accelerating CCSS electrocatalyst discovery.

title: Catalytic Aziridination With Simple Acyl Azides via Validated Copper‐Acyl Nitrenes
content:
Terminal copper‐acyl nitrenes and their reactivity were reported. The nitrenes and catalytic mechanism were characterized by UV/Vis, low‐temperature Evans NMR and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, Eyring analysis, Hammett analysis, cryogenic high‐resolution mass spectrometry, density functional theory, domain‐based local pair natural orbital coupled cluster calculations and complete active space calculations. 








ABSTRACT
Terminal copper‐nitrenes are widely proposed as reactive intermediates in catalytic N‐group transfer, but well‐defined copper‐acyl nitrenes remain largely unexplored. We show that simple aryl acyl azides serve as effective precursors to terminal copper‐acyl nitrenes that catalytically convert styrene into N‐acyl aziridines in yields of up to 76%. Ten copper‐acyl nitrenes were generated, detected, and characterized by spectroscopic, kinetic, and computational methods. The active species exhibits a singlet ground state, as supported by Evans NMR and EPR spectroscopy, and multireference calculations. Mechanistic studies reveal predominantly polar nitrene transfer together with a spin‐crossover event leading to a persistent radical intermediate. The use of readily available acyl azides broadens the scope of copper‐catalyzed aziridination beyond nitrene precursors bearing strongly electron‐withdrawing substituents and identifies copper‐acyl nitrenes as competent and mechanistically distinct nitrene‐transfer agents.

title: Coupled Self‐Alkalization and Chelation Chemistry Enables Highly Reversible Zn Anodes and Rechargeable Alkaline Zn–I2 Batteries
content:
Coupled self‐alkalization and chelation chemistry using ethylenediamine (EN) reconstructs Zn dissolution, transport, and interfacial chemistry in alkaline media. Beyond stabilizing Zn, EN coordinates reactive I+ intermediates, enabling high‐energy Zn–I2 batteries (812.9 Wh kg−1) and the first anode‐free alkaline Zn–I2 configuration.








ABSTRACT
The practical development of alkaline rechargeable zinc‐based batteries (ARZBs) is fundamentally limited by the intrinsic trade‐off among redox potential, high Zn2+ concentration, and Zn anode stability. Herein, we report a synergistic “self‐alkalization + chelation chemistry” electrolyte using ethylenediamine (EN) as a multifunctional co‐solvent. Acting simultaneously as an organic base and a Zn2+ chelating ligand, EN enables in situ OH− generation while forming soluble five‐membered Zn chelates, thereby reconstructing Zn dissolution chemistry in alkaline media. The resulting electrolyte achieves a Zn2+ concentration of 1 M at pH 12.45, transforming Zn transport from diffusion‐limited to migration‐assisted behavior. Meanwhile, preferential adsorption and in situ decomposition of EN generate an organic–inorganic hybrid interphase that effectively suppresses corrosion and parasitic reactions. As a result, Zn||Zn coin cells exhibit stable Zn plating/stripping for 380 h. Furthermore, EN stabilizes reactive I+ intermediates through coordination chemistry, enabling rechargeable alkaline Zn||I2 batteries with a high energy density of 812.9 Wh kg−1. More importantly, the exceptionally high Zn2+ flux and interfacial reversibility enable the first demonstration of anode‐free alkaline Zn||I2 batteries, which operate stably for 860 cycles. This work establishes a general electrolyte engineering strategy for decoupling the long‐standing electrolyte trilemma in ARZBs and advancing high‐energy aqueous batteries.

title: Bidirectional Sulfur Redox Regulation Enabling Ultra‐Stable High‐Sulfur‐Loading All‐Solid‐State Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
content:
A dual‐function amorphous‐crystalline Li6.05P0.95Nb0.05S5Cl0.8I0.2 (LPNSCI) catholyte regulates sulfur conversion in both directions. During discharge, niobium (Nb)‐centered Li‐rich sites accelerate lithium sulfide (Li2S) nucleation; during charge, iodine species drive Li2S oxidation. This chemistry enables 84.2% sulfur utilization at 6 mg cm−2 and 736 mAh g−1 after 1500 cycles.








ABSTRACT
All‐solid‐state lithium‐sulfur batteries are promising for high‐energy storage but are limited by sluggish sulfur redox and poor cycling stability. Herein, we design a new amorphous‐crystalline Li6.05P0.95Nb0.05S5Cl0.8I0.2 electrolyte that reconstructs interfacial Li+ transport and enables bidirectional regulation of sulfur redox. The amorphous structure improves solid‐solid contact and creates additional continuous Li+ pathways around sulfur, while the crystal framework maintains fast Li+ ion‐conducting channels. During the discharge, we further uncover an Nb reduction mechanism in which Nb4+ is reduced to Nb3+, generating Li‐rich sites that promote Li2S nucleation and sulfur reduction. During the charge, I− is oxidized to I2, which acts as the redox mediator for Li2S oxidation, while I3− formation helps stabilize unconsumed I2. This bidirectional regulation enables 84.2% sulfur utilization at a high sulfur loading of 6 mg cm−2 and retains 736 mAh g−1 with 93.1% capacity retention after 1500 cycles at 0.5 C. These findings provide a mechanistic strategy for high‐sulfur‐loading all‐solid‐state Li‐S batteries.

title: Unraveling Synergistic Substrate–H2 Activation and Tunable Counteranion Effects in Ru‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of 2‐Substituted Quinolines: An Integrated Kinetic and DFT Study
content:
Compared with the asymmetric hydrogenation of simple alkenes, ketones and imines, the asymmetric hydrogenation of heteroarenes is more complex. In this work, the reaction mechanism of the asymmetric hydrogenation of 2‐substituted quinolines was systematically investigated by combining kinetic studies and DFT calculations, revealing a novel synergistic substrate–H2 activation mode. In the rate‐determining step, the catalyst counteranion is not a spectator but directly participates: it facilitates active‐site formation via anion dissociation and stabilizes the charge‐separated H2‐cleavage transition state through electronic effects, thereby influencing the reaction rate. This mechanistic model was further extended to the asymmetric hydrogenation of 2‐substituted indoles, where a preliminary counteranion effect was observed, indicating the generality of this anion‐regulated mechanism in the asymmetric hydrogenation of N‐heteroarenes.








ABSTRACT
Although the asymmetric hydrogenation of N‐heteroarenes has achieved remarkable synthetic advances, the underlying mechanism remains incompletely understood. Herein, we combine kinetic and DFT studies to reveal a novel synergistic substrate–H2 activation mode in the Ru‐catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of quinolines. Both the quinoline substrate and the in situ generated dihydroquinoline intermediate act as sequential proton acceptors, causing a dynamic shift in the rate‐determining step between the first and second H2 heterolytic cleavage events. This conclusion is strongly supported by Hammett analysis (ρ = −1.19) and saturation kinetics. Notably, we identify a pronounced and tunable counteranion effect that plays two non‐spectator roles: (i) facilitating active‐site formation via anion dissociation, and (ii) stabilizing the charge‐separated H2‐cleavage transition state through electronic effects, affording up to a 13‐fold rate enhancement. DFT calculations confirm that substrate‐assisted H2 activation and anion‐assisted direct proton transfer are energetically favorable. This synergistic, anion‐regulated mechanism has also been validated in indole hydrogenation, and offers an improved understanding of the outer‐sphere catalytic hydrogenation manifold that diverges from the traditional concerted H−/H+ transfer pathway. This work thus provides a unified theoretical framework for the asymmetric hydrogenation of diverse N‐heteroarene substrates.

title: Amphiphilic Interface‐Mediated Dual‐Domain Architecture Enhances Phosphatase‐Like Activity for Plastic Additives Assay
content:
Plastic additives persist as environmental pollutants, necessitating advanced detection. We present amphiphilic F127‑modified Pt nanozymes with functionally distinguishable dual‐domain architecture, surpassing natural alkaline phosphatase and achieving 2–6 orders of magnitude higher efficiency than most reported nanozymes. Mechanistic studies reveal synergistic adsorption‑catalysis via spatial site separation. Integrated with machine learning, this platform enables simultaneous detection of mixed additives in real samples.








ABSTRACT
Plastics are ubiquitous, and their performance depends on phosphate ester additives used as plasticizers and flame retardants. Leaching of these additives causes environmental persistence and biotoxicity, demanding efficient detection. To overcome the polarity mismatch in detecting plastic additives, we developed amphiphilic F127‐modified Pt with Pt‐OH sites (Pt‐OH/F) for colorimetric detection of mixed plastic additives. Pt‐OH/F outperforms alkaline phosphatase and works directly in water, with catalytic efficiency 2–6 orders of magnitude higher than reported nanozymes. The integration of F127 with Pt‐OH sites creates a functionally distinct dual‐domain architecture composed of an amphiphilic enrichment domain and a catalytic domain, thereby overcoming the polarity restriction of natural phosphatases. Within this architecture, the spatial separation of adsorption sites from catalytic sites prevents competitive occupancy and enhances catalytic activity. Finally, the developed nanozymes can achieve simultaneous qualitative and quantitative detection of leached plastic additives in real samples, showing the potential for on‐site analysis of plastic waste.

title: Stabilizing High‐Voltage Oxygen Holes via π‐Bonding Mediated Frontier‐Orbital Character Inversion in Intermediate‐Regime Oxide Cathodes
content:
In intermediate‐regime Li2RuO3, delithiation induces an intrinsic frontier‐orbital character inversion from Ru 4d‐ to O 2p‐dominated redox states. Weakening Ru─O π bonding elevates the oxygen‐hole redox potential, enabling non‐dimerized oxygen holes to persist at higher voltages. In contrast, conventional Li2RuO3 undergoes further oxygen oxidation toward O─O dimerization.








ABSTRACT
Oxygen redox chemistry offers a promising route to higher energy densities in layered oxide cathodes. However, it is commonly plagued by unstable O─O dimerization that leads to voltage hysteresis and capacity loss. While oxygen hole can mitigate these degradation pathways, its lower operating voltage results in reduced energy density. Herein, high‐voltage oxygen‐hole states are stabilized in Li2RuO3 through precisely tailoring the Ru─O π‐bonding interaction. The successful modulation arises from a dynamic evolution of the electronic structure during delithiation, the so‐called frontier‐orbital character inversion, which has been experimentally validated through combined analysis of the elemental contributions to states near the Fermi level. Oxygen oxidation subsequently involves an O 2p‐dominated antibonding state, avoiding the pronounced bond destabilization associated with electron removal from bonding orbitals. Such behavior is attributed to the unique position of ruthenates within the intermediate regime between Mott–Hubbard and charge‐transfer insulators. And this specific electronic state positioning facilitates a dynamic transition toward a stable negative charge‐transfer regime. This boundary‐crossing effect is especially pronounced in high‐valent systems owing to intense covalency modulations upon oxidation. These insights establish a clear electronic‐structure‐based design principle, highlighting the importance of orbital engineering in boundary‐regime systems to achieve stable and high‐voltage anionic redox.

title: Terminal Engineering Drives Compact π–π Stacking to Suppress Electron–Phonon Coupling in Narrow‐Bandgap Electron Acceptors
content:
A series of ultranarrow‐bandgap electron acceptors based on the resonant N—B←N unit are developed through terminal‐group engineering. The progressively shortened π–π stacking distance suppresses electron–phonon coupling and nonradiative energy loss. The resulting short‐wavelength infrared (SWIR) organic photodetector exhibits a high responsivity of 0.29 A W−1 and a specific detectivity of 1.84 × 1012 Jones at 1180 nm.








ABSTRACT
Ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors are attractive for short‐wavelength infrared (SWIR) photodetection, yet their extended spectral response is accompanied by strong electron–phonon coupling and substantial nonradiative energy losses. Herein, we reveal that intermolecular π–π stacking provides an effective molecular handle for regulating electron–phonon coupling in ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors. A series of ultranarrow‐bandgap acceptors with systematically varied terminal groups are developed, enabling progressive shortening of the π–π stacking distance from 3.74 to 3.53 Å. The resulting compact intermolecular packing strengthens intermolecular interactions and suppresses electron–phonon coupling, thereby reducing vibrational relaxation, prolonging exciton lifetimes, and mitigating nonradiative energy losses. Consequently, the BIP‐M8‐based organic photodetector delivers a responsivity of 0.29 A W−1 and a specific detectivity of 1.84 × 1012 Jones at 1180 nm, with a detectivity exceeding 1011 Jones over 400–1300 nm. These results establish intermolecular π–π stacking as a molecular design parameter for controlling vibronic interactions and mitigating nonradiative energy losses in ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors, offering a general strategy for high‐performance SWIR optoelectronics.

title: Constructing Dynamic Interfacial Hydration Network Channel for Efficient Co‑Transport of OH− and H2 in Water‑Electrolysis Cathodes
content:
Incorporating sulfone‐functionalized covalent organic frameworks into the cathode catalyst layer of alkaline water electrolysis creates dynamic hydrogen‐bonding networks that promote Grotthuss‐type OH− transport while preserving open gas pathways. By balancing water affinity and mobility, the optimized electrode achieves 10.30 A cm−2 at 2.0 V, offering a biomimetic strategy for high‐current‐density hydrogen production.








ABSTRACT
Efficient mass transport at the electrode–electrolyte interface of anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM‐WE) is fundamentally constrained by antagonistic hydration requirements. Drawing inspiration from biological channels that mediate hydrophilic yet non‐retentive transport, we designed a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with tunable sulfone densities as synthetic nanochannels. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations revealed that the sulfone moiety (O═S═O) established weak, labile hydrogen bonds with water, engendering a highly dynamic hydrogen‐bonding network. This unique hydration environment established a surface‐wetting yet bulk‐open state within the COF nanochannels, wherein a dynamic interfacial hydration network channel was maintained within the pores for efficient OH− conduction, while the bulk pore volume remained non‐flooded for unobstructed H2 evacuation. When incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer, the sulfone‐rich 2S‐COF delivers a current density of 10.30 A cm−2 at 2.0 V under industrially relevant conditions (1 M KOH, 80°C), representing a 48% enhancement over the COF‐free electrode. This work establishes a bio‐inspired strategy for molecular‐level control of interfacial hydration, providing a generalizable platform for designing high‐performance electrochemical interfaces that require concurrent ion and gas management.

title: Steering C–C Coupling via Amorphous Nd2O3 Pinning for Efficient CO2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
content:
Amorphous Nd2O3 nanostructures pin the Cu interface to restrain Cu migration and stabilize undercoordinated active sites during CO2RR. Meanwhile, interfacial modulation redirects C–C coupling from conventional CO–CO dimerization toward the thermodynamically favored asymmetric CO–CHO pathway, enabling efficient and durable ethylene production at ampere‐level current densities.








ABSTRACT
Copper‐catalyzed electrochemical CO2 reduction provides a sustainable route for carbon fixation. However, the undercoordinated Cu active sites that facilitate C–C coupling readily undergo rapid, detrimental structural reconstruction under negative potentials. To tackle this challenge, we introduce amorphous Nd2O3 nanostructures pinned at the Cu2O interface to stabilize the undercoordinated Cu sites. Electron microscopy and spectroscopy reveal that this pinning interface not only refines the Cu2O grains by approximately half but also stabilizes the high density of defect sites generated during reconstruction. Density functional theory further unveils that the interface thermodynamically redirects the coupling pathway from the energy‐demanding CO–CO dimerization towards the more favorable CO–CHO asymmetric coupling (*CO + *CHO → *COCHO). The desired catalyst achieves a peak C2H4 Faradaic efficiency of 59.5% at 1.1 A cm−2 and a record partial current density of 762.5 mA cm−2 at 1.5 A cm−2 in a flow cell, with stable operation over 30 hours. We showcase a facile yet effective material design strategy that breaks the selectivity‐stability trade‐off of Cu catalysts, paving the way for industrially viable CO2‐to‐C2H4 electrolysis.

title: Enantioselective Radical Hydrosilylation of Electron‐Deficient Alkenes Enabled by Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
content:
The first catalytic enantioselective radical hydrosilylation of α,β‐unsaturated esters is enabled by metallaphotoredox catalysis. Decoupling Si─C bond formation from asymmetric protonation overrides racemic background addition, affording enantioenriched β‐silylated carbonyls with broad scope, gram‐scale utility, and extension to hydrogermylation.








ABSTRACT
Catalytic enantioselective hydrosilylation of electron‐deficient alkenes remains an outstanding challenge due to difficulties in simultaneously controlling chemo‐, regio‐, and enantioselectivity. Herein, we report a general and practical strategy enabling the first enantioselective radical hydrosilylation of α,β‐unsaturated esters via metallaphotoredox catalysis. This approach integrates photocatalytically generated bromine radical‐facilitated hydrogen atom transfer to convert hydrosilanes into silyl radicals with a chiral nickel catalyst that stabilizes carbon‐centered radical intermediates and directs asymmetric protonation. The method circumvents alkene coordination and migratory insertion steps, and effectively overrides racemic background radical addition. By decoupling Si─C bond formation from the enantioselectivity‐determining step, it accommodates a broad substrate scope. The redox‐neutral, fully atom‐economical protocol proceeds under mild conditions without stoichiometric organometallic reagents or external oxidants/reductants, delivering β‐silylated carbonyl compounds with high chemo‐, regio‐, and enantioselectivity. Furthermore, the strategy extends to enantioselective hydrogermylation and is amenable to gram‐scale synthesis. This work provides a conceptually distinct blueprint for enantioselective hydrosilylation and establishes a mechanistic rationale for controlling enantioselectivity in radical conjugate addition.

title: One‐Step Conversion of Thermoplastic Elastomers into Ionic Ordered Mesoporous Polymers via Interface‐Directed Chain Scission: A Plastic Upcycling Strategy for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
content:
Waste upcycling for water harvesting: A small amount of radical initiator added during sulfonation of a commodity styrenic elastomer triggers interface‐directed chain scission, converting the polymer into an ionic ordered mesoporous framework in a single solid‐state step. The material can capture atmospheric water rapidly at 2.46 g g−1 with solar‐driven regeneration, turning low‐value plastic waste into a high‐performance sorbent.








ABSTRACT
As a cornerstone of the circular materials economy, chemical recycling typically breaks commodity plastics down into small molecular building blocks. While this strategy is reasonable for most plastics, styrenic thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) can be a notable exception. These materials can intrinsically self‐assemble into ordered nanostructures, yet most upcycling methods discard this morphological asset, leaving TPEs a compelling but underexploited feedstock for high‐value applications. Here, we report a one‐step approach that upcycles TPEs into ionic ordered mesoporous polymers (OMPs) in their solid state, through interface‐directed chain scission. Adding a small amount of radical initiator (dicumyl peroxide) during the sulfonation of polystyrene‐block‐poly(ethylene‐ran‐butylene)‐block‐polystyrene (SEBS) leverages a diffusion‐controlled reaction front to selectively cleave the minority polystyrene domains, while crosslinking and sulfonating the majority phase. This one‐step process at 145°C installs ionic character and establishing uniform mesoporosity without the high‐temperature calcination (typically > 350°C) that conventionally erodes functional groups. Furthermore, the resulting OMPs act as high‐performance sorbents for atmospheric water harvesting, demonstrating rapid kinetics, solar‐driven regeneration, and excellent cycling stability, while a simple lithium chloride (LiCl) encapsulation step enhances their water uptake capacity to 2.46 g/g.

title: A Room‐Temperature Fluorescent‐Free Imidazol‐2‐Ylidene: A Versatile Platform for Fluorophore Diversification
content:
Fluorescent free imidazol‐2‐ylidene was prepared via rational backbone engineering, and its photophysical properties were studied in detail, revealing the participation of the carbene moiety in the emission process. The reactivity of this NHC with boranes and chalcogens afforded a novel family of efficient fluorophores with modular emission wavelengths, showing the potential of such scaffolds in designing new luminescent heteroaromatics.








ABSTRACT
N‐Heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) have become key ligands in luminescent transition‐metal complexes, yet the intrinsic photophysical properties of free NHCs remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of the first isolable free imidazol‐2‐ylidene exhibiting room‐temperature fluorescence in both solution and solid states, through the incorporation of a tetrahedral boron moiety into the backbone of the emblematic 1,3‐dimesityl‐2H‐imidazol‐2‐ylidene (IMes) scaffold. Theoretical calculations reveal direct involvement of the carbene center in the lowest singlet excited state and therefore in the emission process. Exploiting the specific reactivity of the carbene center, conversion into the corresponding borane, urea, thiourea, and selenourea adducts enables systematic modulation of the emission wavelength, quantum yield, and photostability. These combined experimental and theoretical results establish free conventional NHCs as a previously unrecognized class of intrinsically emissive organic molecules and identify carbene molecular engineering as a viable strategy for functional luminophores.

title: Encapsulating Metal–Organic Cluster in Metal–Organic Framework Film for Tandem Amplifying Third‐Order Nonlinear Optics
content:
Achieving tandem synergistic modulation of the third‐order nonlinear optical (NLO) response of metal–organic clusters (MOC) and metal–organic frameworks (MOF) remains a significant challenge. This paper encapsulates iron‐based MOC (FeOC) within ordered nanochannels of a conductive Ni‐HHTP MOF film, constructing a film with electrically tunable NLO properties. Results show that FeOC encapsulation increases the nonlinear absorption coefficient (β) of the Ni‐HHTP film from 4.9 × 10−6 m/W to 9.7 × 10−6 m/W, and further increases it to 19.6 × 10−6 m/W after applying a 2 V voltage. This enhancement is attributed to the combined effect of the tandem synergistic effect of guest encapsulation and electrical modulation on the excited‐state absorption (ESA) and carrier dynamics of the film, providing a synergistic strategy for developing adaptive optoelectronic devices.








ABSTRACT
Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and metal–organic clusters (MOCs) are promising platforms for third‐order nonlinear optics (NLO) because their inorganic–organic components enable designable structures and tunable photo/electronic properties. However, integrating MOFs and MOCs for tandem third‐order NLO remains unexplored. Here, we combine MOF and MOC for third‐order NLO by encapsulating MOC in a porous MOF film. A [001]‐oriented conductive MOF Ni‐HHTP film (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) is prepared by liquid‐phase heating drop‐coating and shows excellent electro‐regulated third‐order NLO. Furthermore, iron‐based MOC (FeOC) is encapsulated into the ordered nanochannels of Ni‐HHTP film (Ni‐HHTP@FeOC) using an immersion strategy. The results show that the encapsulation of FeOC in the Ni‐HHTP film can enhance charge transfer and improve excited‐state absorption, with the nonlinear absorption coefficient (β) increasing from 4.9 × 10−6 to 9.7 × 10−6 m/W after loading. An applied electric field further modulates carrier concentration and excited‐state lifetime, enabling dynamic adjustment of the third‐order NLO response; β increased to 19.6 × 10−6 m/W for Ni‐HHTP@FeOC‐2 V. This work is the first to combine MOF and MOC materials for high third‐order NLO performance and provides a synergistic strategy for regulating third‐order NLO performance through tandem encapsulation and electronic stimulation, offering new design concepts for adaptive optoelectronic devices.

title: Molecular Regulation of Excited‐State Dynamics Enables Photochemically Stable Organic Semiconductors
content:
Excited‐state vibrational dynamics are identified as a molecular handle for photochemical stability in organic photovoltaics. Incorporating melatonin into the donor layer suppresses vibrationally induced structural fluctuations and radical generation, enabling a D18/L8‐BO device with 21.10% efficiency and a more than threefold longer T80 lifetime, with generality validated across multiple donor–acceptor systems.








ABSTRACT
Photochemical degradation fundamentally limits the operational stability of organic photovoltaics (OPVs), yet the molecular processes linking excited‐state dynamics to irreversible chemical reactions remain poorly understood. Here, we show that excited‐state vibrational processes represent a previously underexplored molecular degree of freedom governing photochemical stability and can be regulated to suppress degradation. By incorporating melatonin into the donor layer of an OPV device, excited‐state molecular motions are effectively modulated, reducing vibrationally induced structural fluctuations, suppressing radical generation, and mitigating subsequent photochemical degradation under prolonged illumination. Comprehensive characterization reveals that molecular regulation modifies excited‐state relaxation pathways, thereby decreasing the probability of irreversible chemical transformations while preserving efficient charge generation and transport. As a result, D18/L8‐BO based binary device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 21.10% (certified as 20.6%), together with a more than threefold enhancement in T80 lifetime under continuous illumination. The effectiveness of this strategy is further validated across multiple systems, demonstrating its general applicability. These findings establish a molecular connection between excited‐state vibrational dynamics and photochemical degradation, and identify regulation of excited‐state molecular motions as an effective strategy for simultaneously achieving high efficiency and long‐term stability in OPV devices.

title: Tailored Mn Doping Enables Substantially Boosted Fluorescence Emission in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectric Scintillator
content:
Mn2+ doping of the 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectric (GABA)2CdCl4 preserves robust ferroelectricity while enabling bright orange‐red emission with a PLQY of 67%. The resulting first Mn2+‐doped organic‐inorganic hybrid perovskite ferroelectric scintillator delivers a high x‐ray light yield of 52,170 photons MeV−1 and a low detection limit of 62.3 nGy s−1.








ABSTRACT
Organic‐inorganic ferroelectric materials, due to their advantages such as spontaneous polarization, controllable electric domains and multi‐physical field coupling effects, are widely applied in fields including sensors, actuators and optoelectronics. However, there are few successful cases that combine ferroelectricity with dopant‐induced efficient luminescence effects in ferroelectric materials. Herein, through delicate Mn2+ ion doping, we have successfully designed a multifunctional luminescent ferroelectric material, (GABA)2CdCl4:4%Mn2+ (GABA = γ‐aminobutyric acid) which retains its excellent ferroelectric properties with a spontaneous polarization of 4.0 µC cm−2. Meanwhile, its photoluminescence intensity can be systematically modulated by varying the Mn2+ doping concentration, demonstrating excellent controllability and functional versatility. Notably, Mn2+ doping induces a distinct bulk orange‐red luminescence at 610 nm, dramatically boosting the quantum yield from 0.11% to 67%. Leveraging such superior bulk luminescence, (GABA)2CdCl4:4%Mn2+ delivers a high light yield of 52 170 photons MeV−1 and a low detection limit of 62.3 nGy s−1, along with good environmental and radiation stability, marking the first Mn2+‐doped organic‐inorganic hybrid perovskite ferroelectric x‐ray scintillator.

title: Adaptive Active Site Programming via Electrolyte Engineering Toward Enhanced Catalytic Activity
content:
Active‐site reconstruction during electrocatalysis is often unpredictable and difficult to be controlled. By combining pH‐ and potential‐dependent thermodynamic analysis with experimental validation, electrolyte anions are identified as programmable axial ligands that can redefine Fe─N─C active sites. It is identified that nitrate coordination delivers enhanced ORR activity across a broad pH range, establishing a strategy for electrolyte‐guided active‐site programming.








ABSTRACT
Precise control over active site coordination is essential for advancing electrocatalysis, yet remains challenging due to insufficient understanding of how operating environments, particularly electrolyte anions, reshape local structure, and coordination. Here, we combine grand canonical ensemble calculations with experimental validations to investigate five representative anions (F−, Cl−, Br−, NO3−, and H2PO4−) across a range of pH and potential conditions. Using Fe─N─C single‐atom catalysts and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) as a prototypical system, we reveal the adaptive evolution of active site coordination: Anions act as axial ligands that modulate the electronic structure of active sites and enable pH‐dependent regulation of catalytic activity. Specifically, NO3− serves as the most effective axial ligand for enhancing catalytic activity across the entire pH range. Electrochemical measurements show enhanced ORR activity, and spectroscopic characterizations directly reveal axial NO3 coordination upon introducing NO3−, supporting the theoretical predictions. Based on these insights, we propose an adaptive framework for electrolyte‐guided active site programming, which enables the selection of proper anion ligand with optimal catalytic activity under specific working conditions. This work bridges mechanistic modeling and experimental design, precisely constructing the active center for enhanced electrocatalytic activity.

title: Regiospecific Sila‐Matteson Homologative Arylation of Biased (N‐Oxide) Azines
content:
Benzyl‐like nucleophiles are assembled through a homologative event conducted on halosilanes: The transformation enabled by the hypercoordinative attitude of silicon benefits from using azine N‐oxides as competent activating agents, thus precisely transferring the so‐formed benzyl‐element to the intrinsically electrophilic vicinal carbon (C2) of the heterocycles.








ABSTRACT
The judicious selection of silicon—as a Lewis acid—able to generate penta‐ and hexavalent hypercoordinated ate complexes is herein presented as a strategy to realize conceptually novel homologative arylations. Chemically stable aryl‐ equipped C1‐silanes, conveniently activated with the same biased (N‐oxide) substrate in the presence of fluoride, furnish—upon fine‐tuning of consecutive [1,2]‐transposition events—benzyl‐like nucleophilic elements which are precisely transferred at the C2‐position of azines. These benzyl synthons originate from combining an aryl residue and the homologating methylene fragment. The regioselective logic is levered on the unique capability of silicon to undergo two controllable expansive‐contractive modifications of its coordinative sphere. Compared to single rearrangements accomplished with labile C1‐donors on boron manifolds—retained in the final products (Matteson‐like)—the silicon approach directly gathers heteroatom‐free azines, thus documenting high versatility for rapid and predictable functionalization.

title: Molecular Investigation on the Transformation of Carbon Nanotube Bundles Into Carbon Fibers During Annealing
content:
All‐atom simulations reveal how carbon nanotube bundles transform into carbon fibers during high‐temperature annealing. Neighboring tubes coalesce through stress‐biased sequential unzipping, driving an initial porosification followed by densification and graphitization. The resulting structural continuity gives CNT‐derived fibers a higher axial modulus than PAN‐derived counterparts at equal density, offering molecular guidelines for next‐generation carbon fibers.








ABSTRACT
In this study, we uncover the atomistic mechanism governing the transformation of highly aligned carbon nanotube fibers into graphitic carbon fibers during thermal annealing. Under sustained thermal loading, the constituent nanotubes coalesce with their neighbors to form progressively larger tubular structures. This irreversible structural evolution is driven by the elastic recoil that accompanies the release of strain energy stored in the highly curved nanotube walls; because larger tubes carry less curvature strain, coalescence proceeds only toward larger diameters. In parallel, the fiber cross section first undergoes a transient porosification and then densifies into an ordered graphitic arrangement. The development is closely tied to the diameter‐dependent compressive modulus of the nanotubes, allowing the internal voids to collapse and the structure to transition from a tubular assembly to a fully densified state. Mechanical evaluation shows that the resulting fibers attain an exceptional axial modulus of 748 GPa. This mechanical enhancement stems from a seamless, interconnected carbon network that minimizes dangling ends and enables efficient load transfer. Collectively, these results position carbon nanotubes as compelling precursors for advanced carbon fiber manufacturing and provide theoretical guidance for refining the annealing process toward high performance carbon fibers.
